</details>

## Validation

- Build and Web and desktop TypeScript checks passed in WSL.
- Focused mocked browser validation passed **2 of 2** on `90cec36` at 620px and 390px. Both clients imported a five-level JSON structure, expanded and edited it, added and removed an item, and submitted the exact JSON with the selected top-level key. The five files changed by this patch are identical on the rebased head `1659d72`.
- Full local ST on `1659d72` planned 54 cases and executed 51. 34 passed and 17 failed.
- Full local mocked E2E on `1659d72` planned 188 cases. The governed-download batch ran 5 cases with 2 passed and 3 failed. JiuwenSwarm did not start for the literature, research, and fresh configuration batches. The manual download approval case failed at the same scripted-model timeout on unmodified `main` (`96f9c8c`), with zero model calls on both revisions.
- The full UT plan contained 7,629 cases. The initial run was blocked by the runner's non-root requirement. The non-root rerun stopped during Node test collection (`NODE_COLLECTION_FAILED`) before any cases ran.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`

User impact: Nested starting values are easier to read and edit in the evolution settings dialog.

Compatibility and migration: Existing direction JSON continues to use the same format.

pr:1225.body:
The repository already contains skills, specialists and connectors, but they are only discoverable by reading the tree, and a research session package (`.sdresearch`) has no home at all once it is produced. This adds the hub. A build-time exporter projects the tracked sources into download artifacts and an import catalogue; the database is the source of the site's browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`); nginx serves the site beside the API, so page, catalogue and downloads share one origin. Accounts, uploads, version history, review and short-lived download links live behind `/api/v1`, modelled on the openJiuwen Agentic Hub reference, and the importer carries the existing catalogue across.

Earlier this was two pull requests (#1225 and #1243); they now ship as one change, because the site switch and the importer only make sense with the service.

## The site (`apps/hub`)

Five tabs — skills, team skills, specialists, connectors and session packages — share one category tree, a searchable list and a detail view. Routes are real paths (`/skills/<id>`, `/teams/<id>`, `/sessions/<id>`), so a refresh or a shared link resolves to the same asset. Every asset exposes its README and a download. The UI is bilingual (zh/en) and follows the Agentic Hub reference: gradient hero, per-tab counts, segmented tabs, a pill search, an icon-led rail that becomes a chip strip below 900 px, and the reference's 1600 px container with a 1536 px detail card.

Downloads open the browser's save dialog where the browser has one (Chrome and Edge), so the file goes to the folder the person picks; the bytes come from a same-origin `/api/v1/artifacts/{id}/content` endpoint, which a private bucket needs no CORS rule for, and the plain navigation to the presigned URL remains the fallback. Session headers show a localized run time and the model the package recorded; obvious placeholders such as `local-*` are not shown as if they were a model.

Detail pages carry the tile, name, category, version pill and the primary download; beneath them a reading column (description, Readme and Files tabs) sits beside a "Basic information" card that shows only fields the catalog carries. Files is a two-pane browser: the left pane lists exactly what the archive holds — SKILL.md plus every resource, with its size — and the right pane renders the selected file in place, markdown for `.md`, a source listing for text files, a note instead of a preview for binaries.

## The exporter (`scripts/hub`)

`pnpm hub:export` reads only tracked sources — `skills/`, `packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`, `packages/mcp-sources/src/*` and `extensions_config.json` — and writes `apps/hub/public/`, which is gitignored because every input is tracked. Skill and specialist archives are built in memory (`fflate`), so an export needs no network and no temporary directory. Each skill's files are also copied to `skills/<id>/<path>` (44 files, 0.42 MB) so the Files tab never unpacks a zip in the browser.

## External skills and session packages

`pnpm hub:sync-skills` freezes a snapshot of the MindScienceSkills tree (364 skills) from GitCode into `snapshot.tar.gz` and `index.json`; extraction refuses absolute paths and `..` entries.

A session drop is `<id>.sdresearch` plus an `<id>.json` sidecar, and publication is all-or-nothing: one bad package aborts before the first byte is written. Verification enforces the contract — 50 MiB cap, whole-file sha256, the manifest inventory, `records.json` hashed but never parsed. The published `sessions/index.json` is the persistent index; a run merges by id, a package leaves only through an explicit `unpublish`, and unpublishing leaves the uploaded file in place so old links keep working.

## Deployment

The site is served by nginx at `/`, which proxies `/api/` to the service, so page, catalogue and download content share one origin. `docker-compose.yml` runs MySQL, the API and nginx on one host; `pnpm hub:build:api --root` builds the site without the exporter, and the database is the source of the browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`).

The static publishing workflows are gone: a production write is a deployment, not a push to `main`. The exporter remains as the importer's input, and `pnpm hub:sync-skills` remains a manual snapshot step.

## The backend (`services/hub-api`)

FastAPI + SQLAlchemy. The reference establishes the shape: an asset row carrying what the site shows, a version row carrying what a download serves, review state on the version, and `public_latest_version` deciding what is listed. This keeps that contract and differs where our data does: five asset kinds in one lifecycle (`skill`, `team`, `specialist`, `connector`, `session`) instead of six per-type models; no plugin-specific schema validation; stateless HMAC session tokens instead of Redis, so the database is the only stateful dependency; and the reference's `{code, message, data}` envelope and `/api/v1/...` paths.

Uploads are validated before anything is written: the 50 MiB cap measured on the bytes rather than `Content-Length`, path traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, encrypted and duplicate entries, an uncompressed-size ceiling, and a per-entry sha256 inventory that becomes the Files tab. Downloads resolve through `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`, which checks visibility and returns a short-lived presigned URL. Registration closes after the first account, which is the administrator; later accounts come from the administrator.

## Storage and data placement

One private bucket; keys are `assets/<kind>/<publisher>/<asset>/<version>/<filename>` composed in one function. Nothing is anonymously readable, and a bucket listing is refused. Metadata — assets, versions, manifests, users, review state, audit — lives in the database; the bytes live in the bucket; the site and its `catalog.json` remain static files served by the front end.

## Importer and site switch

`scripts/import_catalog.py` reads the exporter's `catalog.json` and writes the same data into the database and the bucket: it preserves catalogue ids, verifies each artifact against the catalogue's sha256 before uploading, wraps single-file specialists and connectors in a one-entry archive while checking the digest against the file rather than the wrapper, marks imported versions approved, and is idempotent. `--dry-run` validates without writing.

The site gets one build-time switch: with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE=/api/v1` the download button asks the API for a URL before navigating, which a private bucket requires; if that call fails the anchor still points at the catalogue URL, so a static deployment is unchanged.

## CI

`hub-api.yml` runs the service's tests and builds its image on changes under `services/hub-api`; it is informational and not part of `merge-gate`. The hub's exporter and site checks run in the UT layer, which builds the workspace: L1 stays the static slice (install only), matching the repository's layering.

## Screenshots

Taken from the built site against the local stack (Chromium, 1440 and 390 CSS px):

| Home, 1440 | Detail with the Files tab, 1440 |
|---|---|
| ![Home at 1440](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-1440.png) | ![Detail Files tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-files-1440.png) |

| Detail in Chinese, 1440 | Home at 390 |
|---|---|
| ![Chinese detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-zh-1440.png) | ![Home at 390](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-390.png) |

## Validation

- `pnpm hub:test`: 44 passed (4 suites), including the case asserting every served skill file matches the repository byte for byte.
- `python -m pytest` in `services/hub-api`: 18 passed — registration and its closing, login, tampered tokens, administrator-created accounts, upload → pending → hidden, approval → listed and downloadable with matching sha256, rejection, owner-only uploads, the Files listing and text preview, path-shaped ids through the `%2F` encoding, the size/traversal/non-zip refusals, and the importer end to end including idempotence and a checksum mismatch.
- Importer against the real catalogue: 387 assets, 385 versions, two session packages skipped because their `.sdresearch` files were not in the site tree.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and the hub build with and without the API switch.
- The earlier static-hub layers (UT 7718 planned / 7687 executed / 7670 passed, ST 63 planned / 62 passed, mocked E2E 188 planned / 181 passed) were measured on `de624faa`; the failures are this host's known constants and are itemised in the commit history of the branch. UI-only commits after that re-ran typecheck, build and `hub:test`.

## E2E user journeys

**Static site — PASS.** Driven in headless Chromium at 1440, 768 and 390 CSS px in English and 390 in Chinese: `document.scrollWidth` equals `clientWidth` on home and detail pages, the rail becomes a chip strip below 900 px, deep links resolve after a reload, session READMEs are fetched from the sibling prefix, and the Files browser lists and previews the archive's contents. A publication increment kept the entries it did not deliver (1 → 2 → 3 packages, every earlier URL still 200), and unpublishing removed only the named id while its file still returned 200.

**Backend — PASS on a local stack.** MySQL 8.0 (container) + the service + the built site + the real bucket, driven over HTTP and in Chromium; not yet on a deployment host.

- Import into MySQL and OBS: 387 assets, 385 versions; two sessions skipped as above.
- `http://127.0.0.1:8612/site/skills/antibody-design`: the button's static `href` is `/site/packages/antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`; the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/antibody-design?version=1.0.0` and the presigned URL serves 109171 bytes whose sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- The path-id external skill `astronomy/astronomical_analysis/astropy`: the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/astronomy%2Fastronomical_analysis%2Fastropy?version=snapshot-20261117` and the download's sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- Over HTTP, not the test client: administrator login, create, upload (`201`, `pending`), approve, download; the bytes match, and the test asset and object were removed.
- The bucket is private: an unsigned `GET` of an object returns `403`, as does a bucket listing.
- The save dialog path was driven in Chromium with the picker stubbed (headless cannot show the dialog): suggested name `antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`, 109171 bytes written, equal to the catalogue's size; the session header reads `Run at Nov 17, 2026, 6:38 AM` and `Model DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, with no `local-smoke`.

Building against the real bucket surfaced three fixes now in the branch: boto3 1.36+ adds a CRC32 trailer OBS rejects (`XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch`); external skill ids are paths up to 88 characters (84 exceed 64), so columns are 191 and routes use a path converter; and the development host's clock is 28 minutes fast, which SigV4 rejects — the smoke tooling compensates, the service deliberately does not, and its README states that the deployment host must run NTP.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` — the GitHub label is pending a maintainer, because this account has no write access to the upstream repository's labels.

User impact: a static site lists the repository's skills, specialists, connectors and session packages with READMEs and downloads; assets can also be published into a service with accounts, review and version history, served from a private bucket through short-lived links.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing behaviour. New app, new service, new scripts and three workflows. The database schema is created at startup and the importer is the migration path from `catalog.json`; the static publishing pipeline keeps working while the backend is introduced.

pr:1228.body:
Saved artifacts can disappear from a Desktop conversation when a terminal run's event history is pruned or unavailable. This increment recovers those cards and lets readers expand additional files in place.

Refs #1202.

## Increment on #1257

#1257 already delivered the card presentation, per-run grouping, subagent lineage walk, kind ordering and exact-version panel preview. This branch retains those implementations. The superseded full-width list and shared-schema selector from the old #1228 head are removed from the PR diff.

- Retain terminal SessionRun rows independently of replay, using the existing Session/epoch guards and bounded cache.
- Attach one strip to a replayed answer, a stored answer, or the run's status after its starting message when no answer survives. Do not synthesize empty turns without eligible outputs.
- Recover missing subagent lineage from the existing catalog; cache successful reads and retry failures on the next outputs refresh, including another version from the same child. Ignore stale Session/client reads.
- Keep main's five-card selection; expand remaining files, including intermediate kinds, within the same strip, with collapse and a panel action.
- Keep known queued/running/blocked outputs hidden even after the event connection closes. Preserve terminal failure/cancellation and usage presentation.

- Keep keyboard focus inside the disclosure after Enter on either toggle; both controls identify the same list with `aria-controls` and expose `aria-expanded`. The browser regression asserts focus and the list association in both directions.

No new endpoint, schema change or second grouping/rendering implementation. Design: [English](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/1a717200a99a9fe7bb530995e2eabeb31330aa15/docs/en/design/desktop-artifact-recovery.md) / [中文](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/1a717200a99a9fe7bb530995e2eabeb31330aa15/docs/zh/design/desktop-artifact-recovery.md) (files included in this PR). The closing keyword is deliberately **Refs**, crediting #1257 for the acceptance it already delivered rather than claiming the entire original feature here.

## Verification

Functional validation and capture source: `1a717200a99a9fe7bb530995e2eabeb31330aa15`. Current head `e2c4015c1831c2fe2bab76e432a443ba82f21deb` adds only the 12 PNG files; executable application code is identical to that tested source. The implementation remains linear on main `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7`, with no merge commit. Old head `12dedcb94` is preserved in a local backup branch.

| Check | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop typecheck | Passed |
| Complete Desktop unit suite | **1405 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**; test concurrency limited to 2 after an initial unrelated App-render subprocess timeout under parallel repository load |
| Desktop conversation, artifact recovery and panel browser journeys | **18 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** |
| zh-CN / English screenshot journeys | **2 passed**, producing the 12 images below |
| Architecture boundaries / design Markdown | Passed on the integrated implementation |
| Repository build | Passed; including the final-head build used by repository E2E |

The browser journeys render the actual Desktop app in the isolated WSL Vite harness (private port 14275), with page-owned API fixtures and no live LLM calls. They cover pruned and failed event reads, no-answer completed/failed/cancelled outcomes, blocked output suppression, same-child catalog failure/recovery, live-to-replay deduplication, reopening and switching Sessions, expansion/collapse, and opening v1 while the existing tab displays v2.

### Repository gate limits — not reported as green

The broader repository run used the incremental parent `afe401d47` before the active-status and keyboard-focus follow-ups; the tested source above was then revalidated with the complete Desktop suite and browser journeys above. Repository E2E was also retried on the final head.

- `pnpm test`: after building the required native Runner SEA, **37 passed / 1 failed** in the binary stage. The same command on unmodified main `a8573558` reproduces the same failure: standalone Runner SEA cannot find `@sciencediscovery/network/src/index.mjs`. The recursive package stage is not reached, so this is not a claim of a complete passing repository test run.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: **planned 8124 / executed 8124 / passed 8115 / failed 9 / skipped 0**. Failures are in CI policy, RACE, Evolve, API usage, Runner timeout/cursor and tagged-selftest cases. Main replay reproduced the RACE 120-second timeout and Unicode log-cursor 60-second timeout; other failures are not all attributed to main. The separate main replay also lacked its Evolve sidecar environment, so that result is not proof of an equivalent product failure.
- `pnpm ci:st`: **planned 63 / executed 62 / passed 55 / failed 7 / skipped 0**. Unmodified main's same layer reports **planned 63 / executed 62 / passed 57 / failed 5 / skipped 0**. Both runs recorded a roughly 600-second Evolve-distribution worker and one unreported planned case. The failure sets differ and are not claimed to be fully attributed or resolved.
- `pnpm ci:e2e`: the initial download failed with `ECONNRESET`; a subsequent run had stack-provisioning failures and the configured `.e2e/browsers` path lacked its headless executable. That attempt reported **planned 189 / executed 145 / passed 0 / failed 145 / skipped 12**, with the remainder unreported. These are not 145 demonstrated product regressions. After correcting that cache location, a bounded retry reached passing artifact/research journeys but exceeded the 900-second limit (exit 124), without a complete result summary. That retry remains incomplete; the separate **18 Desktop journeys passed**.

These failures remain visible for review/CI follow-up. No assertion, selector or gate was weakened to obtain a green result; no unrelated backend/packaging changes are included.

pr:1240.body:
Refs #1239 (evidence part — see scope below).

## Summary

Nightly run 44361037291, shard `research-11`: the managed Python base setup reached terminal `failed` and J5 was BLOCKED with no executed case. The failure transcript existed in the API response (`setup.error` / `components.conda.error`) but J5 and J3 built their BLOCKED reason from `setup.state` + `setup.message` only, so the transcript never reached the journey report and the next occurrence could not be attributed to an external channel/network problem or to a repository defect.

This PR carries that transcript into the BLOCKED reason. It does **not** investigate the Nightly setup failure itself — that failure is still unconfirmed as a repository defect (same commit, same run, J3 passed the readiness assertion in the L2 job), and it cannot be fixed until a transcript is captured.

## What changed

- `test/helpers/environment-setup.ts`: widened `EnvironmentSetup` with optional `error` and `components` (matching `packages/schema/src/environment.ts:451-485`), and added one shared formatter `formatEnvironmentSetupBlockedReason(setup)`. It returns the existing `state: message` text, appends a length-bounded `setup.error`, and appends `conda: <components.conda.error>` only when it differs from `setup.error`. The bound is 1200 chars, the same as the `#1108` precedent (`MANAGED_SHELL_REASON_LIMIT`).
- `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` (J5) and `test/journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts` (J3): the BLOCKED reason now goes through the formatter.
- `test/helpers/journeys.ts`: `environmentSetup()` return type widened to the exported `EnvironmentSetup` (no runtime change).
- `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts`: 6 new cases (see below).

A failed setup remains BLOCKED; no pass/fail semantics change. Test helpers/specs only — no runner, API, or workflow change.

## Proof package

1. **Base SHA:** upstream `main` @ `59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608` (merge commit of #1236). Reproduced and fixed on this commit.
2. **Reproduction before the fix:** an out-of-tree probe feeds a failed setup (with `error` and `components.conda.error`) through `waitForEnvironmentSetup` and builds J5's reason exactly as the spec did. The object carries both error fields, but the reason is only `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: Conda environment setup failed)` — the transcript is absent (`LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: false`, `ECONNRESET: false`).
3. **After the fix:** the same probe through the formatter prints the transcript in the reason (`LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: true`, `ECONNRESET: true`), and an identical conda error is printed once. New unit tests fail on base (the formatter does not exist there) and pass after: `node --test test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` → **17/17 pass** (11 pre-existing + 6 new).
4. **Control case:** a setup without `error` renders byte-identically to before — covered for `error` absent, `null`, `""`, whitespace-only, `components: {}`, and `components: { conda: {} }`. The skip condition (`setup.state !== "ready"`) and J3's `.toBe("ready")` assertion are untouched.
5. **Regression scope:**
   - `node --test test/helpers/*.unit.ts`: 53 tests, 50 pass, 3 fail. The 3 failures are file-level load errors (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: test/e2e-auth.js`, generated by the E2E global setup and absent from this checkout). Verified pre-existing via `git stash`: same 3 files fail on the clean base (47 tests, 44 pass). No new failure from this diff.
   - `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: exit 0.
   - Not run: the full `pnpm ci:ut` layer (same `e2e-auth.js` limitation), the real E2E J5 (needs a paid Nightly / live stack), and the mocked J3 E2E (needs bubblewrap, not installed on this VM). The new unit tests are the verification for this evidence-only change.
6. **Diff scope:** 5 files, +137/−7. No derived files, snapshots, or docs to regenerate; no docs pin the old reason text.
7. **Risks checked and excluded:**
   - Secrets: `setup.error` is already credential-redacted at the source (`redactNetworkError` in `environment-store.ts:1458`, and `failSetup` is the sole writer of both `setup.error` and component errors), and the journey report redacts the BLOCKED reason (`journey-report.ts:377-380`). Appending the transcript adds no new secret channel.
   - Bound: both transcripts pass through the 1200-char bound; worst case ≈ 2.5k chars total in the reason.
   - Micromamba: a micromamba failure reaches the reason via `setup.error` (its failure is terminal for that attempt, so `lastSetupError` is the micromamba error); no information is lost by not appending `components.micromamba.error` separately.
   - The differing-conda branch is defensive: `failSetup` writes the same string to both fields, so today they are identical or the component one is null. It is kept (bounded, tested) so a future store change reporting a distinct per-component transcript still surfaces it.
   - Known limitation (follow-up, not this PR): a multi-line reason renders imperfectly in the journey report — `journey-report.ts:458` blockquotes only the first line in `report.md`, and the HTML `<blockquote>` collapses line breaks. No content is lost in either format; fixing the renderer touches shared report code and is left as a follow-up.

Refs #1239.

## E2E user journeys

- J5 (real E2E): BLOCKED / not run — needs a paid Nightly run / live stack with real model credentials; the new unit tests are the verification for this evidence-only change.
- J3 (mocked E2E): BLOCKED / not run — needs bubblewrap and a running stack, neither available on this VM.
- Unit: `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` 17/17 pass (see Validation above).

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none — test helpers/specs only; the next Nightly run's BLOCKED reason will carry the setup failure transcript.
Compatibility and migration: none

---

Note for the maintainer: I cannot apply the `release:internal` label myself (403), and I did not use auto-merge. Could you please add the `release:internal` label and add this PR to the merge queue when it is ready?

pr:1267.body:
Closes #1265

A provider that refuses `temperature` failed every run with the generic `semantic-error [181001]`, even though the same endpoint served another model fine. The request was always retryable — the field the provider named simply was not on the list of fields this client is willing to drop.

## Root cause

Verified on `main` `a117ae99`, not taken from the report:

- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:346` copies whatever sampling the swarm request carries into the model policy (`temperature`, `top_p`).
- `packages/model/src/client.ts:1574` (`:1594`, `:1614` for the OpenAI Responses and Anthropic variants) writes it into the provider request whenever the policy has it.
- The only 400 recovery is `rejectedControlFallback` (`packages/model/src/client.ts:938`). It gated on a hardcoded thinking-control regex — `/(thinking|reasoning|enable_thinking|chat_template_kwargs)/i` — so a detail that named only `temperature` never reached the per-field check, and `retryWithoutRejectedFields` returned `undefined`. The error was rethrown and the run ended.
- Two further reasons it would still have failed after adding the field to the list, both found while implementing:
  - `rejectedControlWording` (`:833`) is the vocabulary that proves a *parameter* was rejected. It read `unsupported|not supported|…|not allowed|not permitted|no such parameter`, and **`deprecated` was not in it** — which is exactly the word this provider used.
  - the candidate list the retreat is built from was the thinking controls only (`thinkingControlFields`, `:815`).

## What changed

- `temperature` and `top_p` join the retry candidates: `samplingControlFields` is added to a new `retryableControlFields`, which is what the pre-filter, the per-field wording check, the stripped retry, and the retry budget now use.
- `deprecated` and `no longer supported` are added to the rejection vocabulary, so "`temperature` is deprecated for this model" is recognised as a parameter rejection.
- The pre-filter no longer hardcodes thinking words: it asks whether the detail names any field this client can drop.
- The helpers that were thinking-only are renamed to say what they do now (`rejectedRetryableControlFields`, `carriedRetryableControls`, `withoutNamedFields`, `rememberRejectedControls`, …); their two consumers (`services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`, and a doc reference in `completion.ts`) follow.
- The existing safety rule is untouched: a complaint about a control's **value** or the **state** it was sent in still strips nothing. `valueComplaintWording` keeps `when … is enabled/on/set` out of the rejection path, so "temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled" still fails the call rather than silently changing the requested mode.

## Tests

Two new cases in `packages/model/src/client.test.ts`, both with a stub server:

- **the fix**: the server answers `400 {"message":"`temperature` is deprecated for this model."}` when `temperature` is present and streams a normal turn when it is not. The first turn succeeds after the strip, `top_p` (which the 400 never named) survives, and a second turn sends no `temperature` — the rejection is remembered for the endpoint.
- **the guard**: a 400 saying "temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled" is still not a rejection — the call fails once and `temperature` is never stripped.

Mutation-checked, each revert turning the first case red and the file restored afterwards:

| Reverted | Result |
| --- | --- |
| sampling fields dropped from the retry list | `not ok — a 400 that deprecates a sampling field strips it…` |
| `deprecated` removed from the wording | same case red |
| pre-filter restored to the thinking-only regex | same case red |

## Verification

- `packages/model` `node --import tsx --test src/client.test.ts`: **49/49**, including the two new cases. Run on this Windows host with the suite's `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run only — the file declares `os:linux`, and the tag was restored before pushing, so CI is what reports the tagged run.
- `tsc -p packages/model/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repository root): clean.

## Deliberately not in this PR

- **The gateway keeps forwarding sampling to endpoints that never asked for it.** `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:346` could stop passing `temperature`/`top_p` for endpoints the user configured no sampling for, which would avoid the 400 entirely. That is a behaviour change for every provider — a model that currently receives the swarm's own defaults would stop receiving them — so it belongs in its own change with its own evidence. This PR fixes the failure, not the habit.
- **`services/evolve` is untouched.** `completion.py:116-121` already omits `temperature` by default for the same reason; that is a separate path and a separate fix history.
- **Where `temperature: 0.95` / `top_p: 0.95` come from is not claimed.** The swarm log states it produced those numbers, and `GET /api/models` on the reporting install carries no sampling fields, so it is a JiuwenSwarm/openJiuwen default — and that source is not in this repository. **I could not locate it**, so this description does not name one.

## Risk

The retry only happens after a `400` that names a field the request actually carried, and it stops as soon as the field is accepted. A provider that accepts `temperature` sees exactly the request it saw before.

pr:1272.body:
Closes #1271

## The defect

The release-version gate read `application/package.json`'s `version` from the **working tree**. On a `pull_request` event the checkout is the **merge commit** — the head merged into the current base — while the comparison point came from `pull_request.base.sha`. A branch based on an older `main` was therefore compared against a tree it never wrote.

The incident: #1264, based on `222e7b06` (0.4.1) while `main` had moved to `0c3d4d52` (0.4.0-rc1, from #1258). The branch changes only `services/api/**`, but the merge tree carried `0.4.0-rc1`, so the gate reported a release change:

```
CI policy failed: application/package.json moves 0.4.1 -> 0.4.0-rc1, which is a
release change, but the title "fix(api): tell /distill-session it has nothing to
distil" does not start with "chore(release):".
```

`Select CI policy` fails first, so L1, UT and ST are skipped and `merge-gate` fails: **nothing on that head is validated**. Rebasing the same head onto current `main` made it pass, which is what identified the trigger as the stale base rather than the change.

Impact: every pull request whose branch is behind `main` is blocked before L1 by a rule it does not violate, and the only workaround — rebase — is undiscoverable and clears approvals.

## The fix

Both sides of the comparison now come from git objects:

```js
const headVersion = versionOf(showFile(head, VERSION_FILE));
const baseVersion = versionOf(showFile(base, VERSION_FILE));
...
const files = Object.fromEntries(RELEASE_METADATA.map(path => [path, readFromHead(path)]));
```

The working tree is not consulted at all. `pull_request.head.sha` is now required alongside `base.sha`, and its absence is a named error rather than a silent pass. The success line prints the version it accepted **from the head commit**, so a stale checkout can no longer make a green gate look like it verified something else:

```
release version OK: application/package.json at 0.4.1 (head 222e7b06a418)
```

## Verification

- **The incident, on real commits:** with the working tree at current `main` (`0.4.0-rc1`) and an event whose `base` and `head` are both `222e7b06` (`0.4.1`), the check now answers `release version OK … at 0.4.1 (head 222e7b06a418)`, rc=0. Before the change the same shape produced the failure above.
- **New regression case** (`a branch behind main is not a version bump (#1271)`): base and head both 0.4.1, and it asserts that no metadata file is even read. Plus `every metadata file is read from the pull request head, and the base from the base`, and a case asserting an event without `head.sha` is refused.
- **Mutation check:** restoring the working-tree read fails three cases, including the #1271 one (`22 pass, 3 fail`); restored, 25/25. So the regression case is load-bearing, not decorative.
- `.ci/*.test.mjs` — the whole selftest including the contract test: **178/178**.
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check`: catalog OK.

## Note on the gate's placement

This changes `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` only — no workflow file, no job in the graph. The placement of the gate itself was settled on #1258 (`policy` job) and is not reopened here.

pr:1290.body:
Closes #1251

Search Sessions, projects and artifacts from the desktop client — #1251's search, opened from the column's title row.

**No longer stacked.** `#1250` is merged, so the diff is this PR's own delta only.

## The owner's decision, quoted

On 2026-11-26 the code owner asked for this shape, in these words:

> 「我需要你把搜索的放大镜图标放到左上角的科研会话那个高度，然后放在侧边栏的右侧，在"收起侧栏"图标左边一点的位置，注意控制间距，不要离得太远了。点击放大镜之后，在屏幕中央出现弹窗，弹窗上支持输入搜索内容，弹窗最底部支持筛选类型：全部，项目，会话，产物（我不确定还有没有别的，如果有，你就自己加）。如果用户选择的是全部，搜索结果要按照类型做分类，按照时间由新到旧排序。」

The owner also withdrew #1251's fourth criterion — the narrowing (仅当前项目 / 仅运行中 /
有产物 / 时间窗口, the choice surviving a reload) — on 2026-11-26 at 22:18 CST. That is why this
delivery is smaller than the criterion list, and the record is in the repository rather than in
this description alone: criterion 4 is struck through in [#1251](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1251)
under *Withdrawn scope*, and the decision — what, who, when — is written out in
[this comment](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1251#issuecomment-7194112097) on the issue.

## What the column does

**搜索 is a magnifier in the title row, not a row in the list.** It sits beside 收起侧栏,
8px from it, and opens a dialog in the middle of the window: the field, the hits and the
kinds, with the page behind it dimmed. Ctrl/Cmd+K opens the same dialog, Escape closes it.

**The field holds the caret when the dialog opens**, so the keys work without a click:
`Escape` closes, `↑`/`↓` walk the hits in the order drawn, `Enter` opens the one under the
cursor. Opening a hit closes the dialog and hands the hit to the workspace, which opens the
Session, Project or artifact it names.

**The dialog's footer is its only filter:** 全部, 项目, 会话, 产物. 全部 groups the hits
by kind in that order, and every group is newest first; a kind shows only itself. Ordering
is read from the rows themselves — `WorkbenchSearchResult` now carries `updatedAt` (a
Session's own stamp, an artifact's, or for a Project the stamp of its newest Session) —
because the route promises no order of its own.

**Search covers active Sessions.** An archived Session is not searchable and neither are
its artifacts; an imported read-only snapshot **is** searchable — 活跃 is archived versus
live, not writable versus read-only (the owner's answer, recorded here so the choice can
be checked).

**The narrowings are gone.** 项目范围 / 运行中 / 有产物 / 指定时间 used to hang off the
search row; with the row removed there is nowhere for them to live, and the owner's
decision was to drop the feature rather than move it. The column lists every active
Session again, and the stored preference, its module and its tests are gone with it. The
copy those controls used — twenty `sidebar.*` keys, both dictionaries — is gone too, so a
reader cannot find the labels of a control that no longer exists.

## What this does **not** claim

Path-only resolution prefers the calling Session's own Artifact, then a cross-Session candidate where `ARTIFACT_SESSION_CONFLICT` still applies. An evolve design started with `--no-confirm` could stop on a checkpoint without creating its search. When the checkpoint was not a parseable auto card, the cardless continuation needed the design's pace from the transcript at that instant, but the client's own push had just dropped that settle, so the pace was unknown and it returned silently.

## Changes
- `use-auto-continue.ts`: fall back to the Session's last observed pace while `checkpointMode` is unknown; treat `finalContent` as proof a turn ended; report (and anchor) a notice for endings the client will not push.
- `EvolveStallNotice` names the missing search and offers the sentence to send.

pr:1337.body:
A report's `[evidenceN]` chip opened 科学记忆 scoped to the report's Session, and the persisted chip references carried no owning Session. Citing a node created in an earlier Session of the same project therefore always showed "This memory was not found", implying the record was deleted.

## Changes
- Card-side fallback: read the citation's scope first; when nothing matches and the citation names no Session, read once unscoped and use the hit's `sessionId` for provenance. Budget refusals and an unreachable or disabled service stay "unavailable", never "missing".
- The unscoped read is limited to `GLOBALLY_UNIQUE_ID_LABELS` (`Artifact`, `Evidence`, `SourceFile`), whose node id is the record's own key. `DbRecord` is excluded on purpose: its id is the bare `identifier` and the graph keys those nodes by `(session_id, source, identifier)`, so a citation that names no Session returns `unlocated` instead of accepting a same-id record from another Session. The stale "Node ids are globally unique" comment now states this actual semantics.
- A page the sidecar cut short is not proof that nothing exists. `resolveCitation` carries `truncated` out of the scoped and the unscoped read alike and returns the new `unlocated` outcome instead of `missing`; `missing` is now reachable only from a page the sidecar did not cap.
- `memory.notFoundBody` (en/zh) now only says no record matches the citation; an outage keeps its own message, and `unlocated` has its own copy (`memory.unlocatedTitle` / `unlocatedBody`, en/zh) so it never renders the not-found sentence.
- New citations carry the owning Session: the sidecar's `cited_targets`/`chip_map` gain `session_id`, `toChipMap()` copies it, and the report reference persists it. Artifact chips keep none because the artifact dialog resolves them through the project.

## Validation
All numbers below were produced in the task checkout at head `c5ac07e1141e911971859730c8fe9973eb426968` (tree `aa11afc5302aec0f80fd67c2391f9f66524f81f3`), after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; each names the local log it comes from. - Regression tests against the previous implementation: with only the changed source files restored to `76bf461c` and the new tests kept, the two touched test files give 37 tests / 30 passed / 7 failed, failing exactly on the truncated-page cases (scoped, widened, own-Session, already-unscoped) and the foreign same-id `DbRecord` cases (log: `.tmp/prefix-run.log`).
- Sandboxed layers: `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` still cannot preflight in the task environment — `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE`, no user namespaces, planned 8148/63/189 and executed 0. They are reported as **not run locally**, not as passing; the sandbox-free equivalent is the build + desktop UT + typecheck above, and the containerised layers come from this PR's CI.

pr:1341.body:
Nightly 45212568993 recorded `research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}` for research-11 and the harness scored it `FAIL` with `provider faults 0`. Idea Tree relays the local `/internal/evolve-llm` proxy's answer (`vendor/idea_tree/research.py:240-250`), and only the gateway's own vocabulary counted as provider context, so nothing matched. First defect of #1340.

## Change
- `Model HTTP <5xx>` now counts as provider context: the relayed 502/ECONNRESET text classifies as `provider-transport`, a relayed provider 5xx as `provider-server-error` with its status. `429`/`422` stay non-provider.
- The proxy's own 503 "no API token" refusal stays a product failure and vetoes a sibling outage.
- Review follow-up: the proxy also writes 5xx itself — a 502 for its request validation (`completion.ts:67-78`), its own abort/20-minute ceiling (`llm-proxy.ts:89,123,176-179`), an unreachable upstream, and the catch-all 500 `Internal server error` (`http/index.ts:5044-5051`). A relayed 5xx carrying that product wording is now vetoed, on the relayed line, so it cannot excuse a product failure; the gateway's relayed 5xx is unchanged.
- Regression cases in both classifier test files.

## Validation
`node --test ...`: 40/40 pass; with the previous classifier restored 38 pass, 2 fail (the new cases). `pnpm ci:selftest`: 185/185 (184 before). `pnpm test:tagged:selftest`: 76 tests, 69 pass, 6 fail / 1 skip — the same six pre-existing `No module named 'pytest'` failures as baseline. Not run: `ci:ut`/`ci:st`/`ci:e2e` (no `bwrap`; no product behaviour change).

## E2E user journeys
Not applicable: CI accounting code only.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: nightly accounting stops blaming the product for a provider outage and stops excusing the proxy's own 5xx.
Compatibility and migration: none

pr:1361.body:
## Summary

1. Routes only **merge queue (`merge_group`)** runs of **`UT`** and the three heavy **L2 mocked E2E shards (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`)** to self-hosted Docker runners (`[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`), gated behind the repository variable `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'` (default off).
2. Enables **in-runner 2-stack local parallelism (`CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`)** for the two long standard mocked E2E shards (`standard-config` and `standard-journeys`) so each job runs two fully isolated local stacks in parallel (disjoint loopback ports, runtime directories, `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` roots, desktop Vite port/cache directories, and Playwright `workers: 1`), cutting L2 end-to-end wall time roughly in half on both self-hosted and GitHub-hosted runners.

Closes #1360

## Motivation

In merge-queue runs, `UT` (~13 min) and the three heavy L2 mocked E2E shards (`standard-config` ~20 min, `standard-journeys` ~20 min plus ~3.5 min queued behind `max-parallel: 4`, `research` ~10 min) dominate wall-clock time before `L3 real E2E` can start. Moving those four trusted merge-queue jobs onto dedicated Dockerized self-hosted runners with container-local caches and running 2 isolated stacks inside each of the two long standard shards brings all four jobs into a ~9–12 min band without exposing self-hosted runners to untrusted `pull_request` (or fork) runs or splitting any spec file.

## Changes

### Merge-queue self-hosted routing & container-local cache
- **`.ci/tier-policy.mjs`**:
  - Export `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER = ['self-hosted', 'Linux', 'X64', 'sciencediscovery']`.
  - Compute `self_hosted_merge_queue = event === 'merge_group' && selfHostedMergeQueue === true` and `ut_runner` (`SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER` when enabled, otherwise `'ubuntu-latest'`). Non-`merge_group` events (`pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`, `workflow_call`, `schedule`, `push`) always fail closed to `'ubuntu-latest'`.
- **`.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`**:
  - Export `HEAVY_MOCKED_SHARDS` (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`) and `buildMockedMatrix()`.
  - Emit `runner`, `self_hosted`, and `local_concurrency` (`2` for `standard-config`/`standard-journeys`, `1` for `research`/`governed`/`literature`) per shard.
- **`.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`**:
  - Manage a `flock`-serialized, content-hashed read-only JiuwenSwarm installation under `${SD_CI_CACHE_DIR:-/ci-cache}/jiuwenswarm/<key>/src`.
  - Strip `.git` and pre-install `pytest>=8.3.5` (for `check:swarm-contract`) while holding the lock so concurrent UT/E2E jobs never mutate the shared venv and `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` takes its pre-installed read-only fast path while every job keeps its own isolated `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` under `CI_RUNTIME_DIR`.
  - Export only `JIUWENSWARM_SRC` to `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**:
  - Wire `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` through `policy` -> `e2e-plan` / `ut` / `e2e`.
  - Raise mocked `e2e` `max-parallel` from `4` to `5` and pass `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY: ${{ matrix.local_concurrency }}`.
  - Skip cross-region `actions/cache` round trips (pnpm, uv, Playwright Chromium, JiuwenSwarm) only when a job is routed to a self-hosted runner, replacing JiuwenSwarm cache restore with `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`.
  - Make `Provision the bubblewrap sandbox` idempotent in `ut` and `e2e` by probing `bwrap --unshare-user --ro-bind / / --dev /dev true` before invoking `sudo apt-get` / `sudo sysctl`.
- **`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`**:
  - Export `sharedCacheEnv()` and honor pre-set `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `npm_config_cache`, and `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` (matching existing `UV_CACHE_DIR` handling) while preserving exact workspace-local fallbacks when unset.

### In-runner 2-stack local parallelism (`standard-config` & `standard-journeys`)
- **`test/support/tagged/execution.mjs`**:
  - Export `PARALLEL_MOCKED_SHARDS`, `mockedLocalConcurrency()`, `splitEntriesByFile()`, `mockedExecutionLanes()`, and `mockedSlotEnvironment()`.
  - Balance whole spec files across 2 lanes (never splitting a spec file across stacks); for `standard-config`, keep `mocked-standard-config-fresh` in its own pristine stack and keep the 9 JiuwenSwarm supplemental checks exclusively on `mocked-standard-config-global`. Single-file PR selections and non-standard shards (`research`, `governed`, `literature`) remain single-stack.
- **`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`**:
  - Execute `mockedExecutionLanes()` concurrently via `Promise.all` with disjoint loopback port blocks (`4410`/`4420`, `4411`/`4421`, `4510`/`4520`, `17774`/`17784`, desktop Vite `4178`/`4179`), separate `CI_RUNTIME_DIR`, `JIUWENSWARM_HOME`, and Vite cache dirs. Default remains `1` (serial) for local `pnpm ci:e2e`.
- **`.ci/run-e2e.sh`**:
  - Serialize JiuwenSwarm port allocation across concurrent local stacks via `CI_E2E_SWARM_START_LOCK` (`flock`), explicitly closing fd 8 (`8>&-`) on child commands so daemonized processes never inherit the lock descriptor; avoid redundant `ln -sfn` rewrites on `test/node_modules`.
- **`test/helpers/desktop-evolve.ts` & `apps/desktop/vite.config.ts`**:
  - Honor `E2E_DESKTOP_PORT` (default `4178`) and `E2E_DESKTOP_VITE_CACHE_DIR` so concurrent desktop-entry specs never collide on Vite port or `.vite` cache.
- **`.ci/mocked-report.mjs`**:
  - Audit all `mocked-*` sub-lane directories in shard artifacts so any unexpected `jiuwenswarm-checks.json` outside the single designated check batch fails with `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`.
- **`.ci/README.md`, `.ci/mocked-shards.test.mjs`, `.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`**:
  - Document the toggle, `max-parallel: 5`, and `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`, and add unit, CLI, workflow contract, reconciliation, and hermetic shell tests.

## Safety & Rollout

- **Default off for self-hosted routing**: While `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` is unset, all PR and merge-queue jobs stay on `ubuntu-latest`. Clearing or changing the variable rolls back immediately with no workflow edit.
- **Event boundary**: `pull_request` (including forks), `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, `push`, light mocked shards (`governed`, `literature`), `ST`, desktop jobs, packaging, and real E2E jobs never route to self-hosted runners even when `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true`.
- **Strong isolation**: Each local E2E lane runs its own isolated service stack and Playwright `workers: 1`; `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=1` reverts any run to serial execution.

Fixes #1352.

`health()` trusted only the unauthenticated `/health`, so a token mismatch kept Settings at `运行正常` while every query answered `401`. The old by-node-type probe scanned the graph, whose 503 budget refusal read as "Cannot connect". The probe is now O(1), with a mixed-version fallback.

## Changes
- Sidecar `GET /internal/ping` (Bearer) returns `{status:"ok"}` without touching graph data.
- `health()` reads `/health`, then pings: 401/403 → unauthorized; 404/405 (older sidecar) re-checks with the authenticated by-node-type read; a known `memory_graph_query_limit` refusal keeps `/health`; any other failure → degraded.
- Query, subgraph, web-page-hash and search reads map 401/403 to `memory_graph_unauthorized`; the web-page content route keeps every failure reason a 502. Settings and card/provenance show `凭据被拒绝` / "Credentials rejected".
- Provenance review treats that reason as inconclusive.

pr:1372.body:
## What changed
- `设置 › 运行环境` now passes `{ client, key: "runner-catalog" }` to `useLoaded`, reusing the existing per-client `settings-cache`: a revisit paints the last catalog while the refresh runs behind it.
- `LoadGate` accepts an optional `skeleton`, used only on a cache miss. Pages without one keep the current loading line, and the error/retry plus "stale value under a visible failure" behaviour is unchanged.
- First paint is now layout-shaped: three metric cards and four table rows for `模型用量`, two Runner card rows for `运行环境`. Both regions use `role="status"`, `aria-busy` and a localized label, hide the blocks from assistive tech, and stop the shimmer under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Prefetch is deliberately omitted: without single-flight dedupe plus a freshness check it would only repeat the same two heavy reads.

## Verification
- Desktop unit suite: 1504 passed / 0 failed (137 suites), including new first-paint skeleton, cached-Runner paint and cross-client isolation cases.
- Baseline contrast on `e61b1d29` with the same test files: 55 passed / 3 failed — the new skeleton assertions fail there, so the tests distinguish the fix from the defect.
- New mocked E2E journeys hold `/api/runners` and `/api/usage/analytics`: skeleton visible on the first visit, remembered card/summary after switching away and back. 2/2 pass here; both fail on baseline at the skeleton assertion. Full `settings-interactions.spec.ts`: 38/38.
- `pnpm typecheck` clean, desktop build clean, and the other `LoadGate` panes (技能/网络/代理/配额) keep their unchanged loading line: 67/67.

## Remaining risk
Endpoint cost is unchanged: a first click still waits on live Runner probes or server-side usage aggregation, so ~1 s / ~1.5 s remains when no answer is cached. The skeleton and the loaded content are close but not pixel-identical, so a small layout shift remains on landing.

pr:1378.body: The settings › Skills surfaces were rebuilt against the 2.5 design handoff: the list, both add flows, the package page, the file editor and the confirmations now follow the frames instead of the earlier row list. The editor also needed routes the control plane did not have — raw SKILL.md read/write, file delete and directory rename — so they are part of this change. ## List page - Source tabs (全部 / 我的 / 官方) with counts, a three-column card grid (456px cards at 1920, two / one column below 1500 / 1150), colored marks, per-card switches and the actions menu. - Search matches names only and marks the matching run in the card title; a clear control restores the list. The bulk switches cover the rows the current tab and search show, not every package on the machine. - The scope note is removed; the add menu is the handoff's compact list. - The bulk pair sits on the tab row, one line with the tabs, the search field and 添加技能 at the default window and above (1400px); narrower windows wrap the row onto a second line, and either way the search gives up width so the add button stays inside the pane. ## Add flows - Upload and GitHub import are dialogs over the list (550px, 30% scrim), not sub-pages. Upload shows the notice, drop zone, file row and cancel/OK; GitHub keeps inspection and selection inside the dialog and then shows the job's `done / total` progress until it ends. - Import outcomes are top-right notices (success, progress, failure with retry), replacing the old inline banner. ## Package page - 基本信息 renders the package document; 技能详情 puts a file tree (264px) beside the open file, reads other files on demand, understands links inside the document, and offers copy/download. - Management packages rename a file or folder with a double press on its name. - SKILL.md leads the tree; root files sit before folders, files before folders at every level. ## Editor - The full document is edited as raw text (frontmatter included) under the handoff's blue frame, with create file, create folder, upload, rename and delete on the tree; the local empty-folder case never calls the API. - Leaving with unsaved changes and deleting a file use the page's own 2-4/2-5 dialogs; saving and leaving land on the package page's 技能详情 tab. ## Backend - `GET/PUT /api/skills/:id/skill-md` — raw SKILL.md read/write. - `DELETE /api/skills/:id/files/:path` — delete a file or a folder prefix. - `POST /api/skills/:id/files/:path/rename` — rename a file or folder. - Every write re-validates the package and carries the revision it read, so a concurrent edit is a conflict rather than an overwrite. ## Visual evidence Captured at 1440x900 against a local stack (`13c-metabolic-flux`); Chinese on the left, English on the right. The six list frames above are the exception: they were re-captured on `15197acc` (the commit that moves the bulk pair into the toolbar) at 1440, 1200 and 1024 in both languages, from the desktop's mocked E2E harness rather than the stack — the stack's JiuwenSwarm runtime cannot be provisioned on this host (`scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` fails to resolve `openjiuwen[codex]`), and the pair only renders when the backend is JiuwenSwarm. The harness serves the repository's own `skills/` packages, so those frames show 17 skills (4 我的 / 13 官方) instead of the stack's 35, with the same UI and stylesheet as the rest. ### List: tabs, search and the bulk switches Narrow windows, showing the grid collapse (Chinese on the left, English on the right): 1200px lays the cards out two to a row, 1024px gives each card a row of its own. ### 添加技能: the upload dialog ### 添加技能: the GitHub import dialog ### The package page: file tree and the open file ### The editor ### 2-4 delete confirmation ### 2-5 unsaved changes ## Validation CI Actions run `45545105860` on `24164d46`: **all jobs succeeded** — policy, L1 (static checks), ST, UT, binary releases (aarch64 and x86_64), Docker image, and the mocked E2E shards `standard-config` and `standard-journeys`. Desktop UI-ST, macOS and Windows installers are skipped by the workflow on this change. Head `15197acc` passed every check; head `61c4f37e` adds the test reconciliation below and starts a new run. The merge-queue build over `main` + `15197acc` (`f3e7b913`, 09:35Z) runs the full standard plan (75 specs), which this head's own L2 slices do not select, and it failed `journey-desktop-specialist-toggle` step 1 in both locales: that step required 添加技能 and 新增专家 to share a `right`/`top`. The rebuilt Skills page follows the handoff and keeps 添加技能 on the toolbar line, so the shared-position rule is retired; `61c4f37e` compares the paint, height and radius that still have to agree and asserts the action shares the toolbar row with the tabs. #1445 moves the Specialists header to the same pattern, so the same-row check will cover both pages there. The same build also saw a `journey-restore-research` click timeout in `standard-journeys`; nothing here touches that surface, and it is the spec #1427 rewrites. Local runs on this head: `apps/desktop` **1559 passed / 0 failed**, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` passes, the settings E2E specs **39 passed**, `services/api` skill tests **28 passed**, `pnpm build` passes. `61c4f37e` changes only `test/journey-desktop-specialist-toggle.spec.ts`: `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`, `check-e2e-meta` (131 specs, 0 errors) and `sync-e2e --check` pass, and the new assertion measured 0px centre offset between the tabs and 添加技能 at 1440 in the desktop harness. The journey itself needs the isolated stack, which this host cannot provision — the merge-queue run is what exercises it. The local layer runner could not complete every layer on this host, and each blocker was attributed: - UT: `uv sync --project services/paper --locked` wants to re-lock the root `uv.lock` under uv 0.12.14; the same failure reproduces on unmodified `main` (`d13cead9`), so it is pre-existing. CI's UT passed. - ST locally: 69 executed / 67 passed / 2 failed. The failure is `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` downloading its pinned Python runtime from GitHub (`fetch-runtime.mjs`); it is the external download. CI's ST passed. - Mocked E2E layer locally: BLOCKED in preparation because `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` cannot resolve `openjiuwen[codex]` on this host (193 planned / 0 executed). CI's mocked E2E shards passed. - The changed journey was run directly against a local stack: PASS (below). Review follow-up on this head: a page-level message is cleared when the reader moves to another page, so a refusal from the package page does not follow them into the editor; a test drives the refused switch and then the back control. ## E2E user journeys PASS — `journey-desktop-skill-import-edit.spec.ts` against a local stack (API `127.0.0.1:4310`, desktop entry `127.0.0.1:4178`), tested head `2aa4fdcc`: **1 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped in 24.4s**. Steps and outcomes: - Upload through 添加技能 → 上传技能 dialog: the dialog closes into the success notice and the card appears — passed. - Package page: opens on 基本信息, the 技能详情 tab shows the file tree and SKILL.md — passed. - Editor from the row menu: 退出编辑 / 保存 are visible, the full SKILL.md is editable — passed. - Rewrite the body and save: returns to 技能详情, the API reads the rewritten paragraph and the package's heading and MIT licence are intact — passed. - Export the package as a ZIP — passed. - Delete through the workspace confirmation — passed. The mocked E2E layer itself was blocked in preparation (see Validation); this journey was run directly with the same pinned Playwright environment and the local stack. ## Release Release category: release:feature (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer: the contributor does not have write access to apply it) User impact: the whole Settings › Skills surface changes; imports move to dialogs, package pages gain a file tree, and the file editor can edit the full SKILL.md and package files. Compatibility and migration: none; the new routes are additive. Skill packages keep their on-disk format.

- Keep card, details and form service switches synchronized. Session defaults remain independent in details; built-in sources keep their supported default-selection control.
- Add Try it to open a fresh conversation with the chosen MCP and current model, without sending a message or granting extra permissions.
- Preserve HTTP/SSE/STDIO, exact legacy arguments, stored credentials, OAuth start/cancel/open/clear, actual tool previews, latest-check feedback and named deletion confirmation.

### Regression test design

- Search and switch catalog categories; apply a filtered bulk operation, refuse one write, and retry without rewriting successful or hidden services.
- Persist both service-enable directions, reopen the editor and reload; keep session defaults independent and recover refused writes or cancelled edits.
- Retain HTTP OAuth configuration and the stored client-secret sentinel, as well as exact STDIO argument arrays and stored environment/header credentials.
- Fill manual or JSON file/paste configurations, edit before confirming, validate hidden batch entries, and retry partial imports without duplicates.
- Keep the JSON caret in the source through repeated valid parses; hand focus to filled fields only after file upload.
- Show refused authorization/clear-grant operations inside the visible details dialog and allow retry.
- Verify first/last keyboard entry and wraparound, Escape/focus return, modal focus containment and busy locks.
- Recover a blocked OAuth popup, cancel or clear authorization, and retain the open-page action's plain styling and new-tab/opener-isolation attributes.
- Open a source-specific trial conversation without sending. The separate SDK Echo journey then explicitly sends a prompt, verifies the invocation/result, persists edits, cancels/confirms deletion and checks reference cleanup.
- Inspect English/Chinese layouts and smaller windows while retaining Skills and Specialists behavior.

pr:1386.body:
Eight edge cases can lose data during recovery, cause inconsistent research state, or change how the desktop and web apps present results. This change adds focused regression coverage for each case.

## Persistence and run history

- Repair the local graph journal tail before new records are appended. A torn final record is truncated, including invalid partial UTF-8. A valid final record without a newline is kept and terminated so the next append stays separate.
- Skip malformed run-stream JSONL records during replay. Require a non-negative safe integer sequence, a string timestamp, and an event object with a string type.

## Tool execution and context

- Propagate parallel tool rejections with `undefined` or `null` after draining in-flight calls, and stop scheduling new calls. Register both regression cases with literal titles so the tagged UT collector can discover them.
- Reject sparse arrays with an error identifying the missing index. Explicit `null` entries remain valid.

## Desktop and web

- Preserve literal comparisons in paper titles and abstracts. Remove common HTML and JATS inline and structural tags, handle escaped tags with quoted attributes, and split escaped blocks into paragraphs.
- Keep CSV artifact row keys unique even when generated IDs would collide with explicit IDs that appear later in the import.
- Keep the latest Idea Research snapshot when a list response races a stream update, so paused research stays paused and the Continue button remains available.

## Account check-ins

- Validate the daily reward and streak settings at startup and document the accepted environment variable format. Keep the existing defaults and legacy bonus-period setting.

## Validation

- On `c17479d718765c219bba22c3f279e320cfaeec85`, 70 focused checks passed in review: 19 desktop paper-text, 48 web CSV, and 3 Idea Research card tests. The new regression test delays the list response until after the stream reports `paused` and verifies that the Continue button remains available.
- GitHub Actions passed L1, UT, ST, and the [merge gate](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45585984445/job/139122562993) on this head.
- Before rebasing, the tagged Node collector on `f12d1c25` collected 7,563 test descriptors from the 756 files in the fork CI request. The two scheduler regression callbacks both passed. This was a focused check of the earlier revision.

## E2E user journeys

- The previously failing Idea Tree journey passed in an isolated local stack and in the [GitHub L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config) rerun](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45585984445/job/139112952177) for `c17479d718765c219bba22c3f279e320cfaeec85`. The journey verifies pause, manual resume, and three rounds of iteration. The [journey report and screenshots](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45585984445/artifacts/15009777596) are available in the CI artifact.
- Chromium component checks verified the desktop provenance card and CSV row selection with fixed inputs. Full-stack journeys for CSV import, desktop paper display, run replay, and account check-in remain unverified.

## UI screenshots

Captured in Chromium using the repository's actual React components and styles with fixed evidence and CSV inputs. The desktop screenshots open the evidence card's provenance tab. The CSV screenshots open the Data table tab and click the same `sample#4` record with value `10`.

### Desktop evidence card

Before the review follow-up (`63b7bd13`), the paper card displays literal JATS tags. After the follow-up, the same input displays as two readable paragraphs, preserving `<LOD`, `>0`, and the text from the inline tags.

**Before**

![Desktop paper card before the follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8929ec3a-92af-4b10-9b3c-738e0b2aa8eb)

**After**

![Desktop paper card after the follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4111d6c6-027c-4d75-aa48-56343d47e904)

### Web CSV data table

Before the PR (`c3a2305a` parser), clicking one row highlights a second row with the same internal key. After the PR, only the clicked record is highlighted.

**Before**

![Web CSV table before the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc7be5c1-aa5c-4c05-9b84-30164cca6a28)

**After**

![Web CSV table after the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3979dc9-eeaa-4f54-b293-e25a23105a31)

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`

User impact: CSV artifact rows retain distinct identities, paper text keeps literal comparisons, and saved research state and run history recover more reliably. The Idea Research card stays paused and keeps Continue available after a delayed refresh. Invalid check-in settings fail at startup with a configuration error.

Compatibility and migration: No data migration is required. Use non-negative decimal integers such as `0` or `100` for check-in settings. Unset an unused variable to use its default. Blank values, signed values, and scientific notation cause a startup configuration error.

pr:1387.body:
The 科学记忆 status line read `/api/health` once at mount and again only on 重新检查, so a memory service restarted while 设置 stayed open kept showing 连接失败 until the page was reloaded (Issue #1384).

## Change
`apps/desktop/src/views/MemoryStatus.tsx` (which owns the reading; `MemorySettings.tsx` only passes the switch) now re-reads every `MEMORY_STATUS_POLL_MS` = 15 s while memory is enabled. The next read is scheduled only after the previous one answers, so a slow service cannot stack requests; the timer is cleared on unmount and nothing is asked while the switch is off. A background read keeps the last answer on screen; only the first read and 重新检查 show 检查中, and a press reads at once. The stale "There is no timer" comment now states this contract.

## Tests
- New `apps/desktop/tests/memory-status-refresh.test.tsx` (3 cases, mock clock): degraded→healthy reads 运行正常 with no remount or press, an in-flight read is never joined by another, unmount stops the timer, and `enabled=false` asks nothing.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/scientific-memory.spec.ts`: the mocked journey asserts the same recovery in the browser; its stale "press, not a timer" comment is corrected.

## Validation
- desktop `pnpm test`: 1503 pass / 0 fail; desktop and repo `typecheck`: pass.
- desktop mocked Playwright `scientific-memory.spec.ts`: 12 passed / 0 failed, recovery case 17.6 s.
- With the timer scheduling removed, the new unit case fails (`1 !== 2`) and the E2E recovery assertion times out; both pass with the fix.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: 0 of 8404 planned cases executed here — preflight `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE` (bubblewrap absent, cannot install without root).

## E2E user journey
PASS — desktop mocked browser: 设置 › 科学记忆, switch on → degraded → healthy → 运行正常 without reload or press; 重新检查 reads at once; switch off stops the reads.

## Visual evidence
Mocked desktop harness (`apps/desktop/e2e`, deterministic `/api/**` fixture), viewport 1500×950 — the environment the Issue reports — first in zh-CN, then the same two moments in English. One page and one settings pane throughout: nothing is reloaded, navigated or pressed between each pair of shots.

1. `连接失败｜重新检查` while the fixture answers `memoryGraph: "degraded"`:

![科学记忆 with the memory service down](https://agent-ci-infra-bot.llmbots.co/pr-media/0d44adeedacec9b83414c0e59b069977e7cb6ff82bb1edd144ac986840d2fcf1)

2. The same pane 15.4 s later, after only the mocked `/api/health` answer changed to `healthy`:

![科学记忆 recovered while the pane stayed open](https://agent-ci-infra-bot.llmbots.co/pr-media/5f96fba65b5d725caa83ae2a0ce5ce3fd81579fbf09bfb43e1a76fca9973e1b2)

Measured in that run: URL before/after `http://127.0.0.1:4175/` (unchanged), navigation entries `1 → 1` (no reload), `/api/health` reads `3 → 4` (exactly one background interval), and 重新检查 was never clicked.

### The same two moments in English

Same harness and viewport, same pane position, with the app's own locale key (`LOCALE_STORAGE_KEY` set to `en`, the mechanism `settings-interactions.spec.ts` uses for its English pass).

3. `Cannot connect｜Check again` while the fixture answers `memoryGraph: "degraded"`:

![Scientific memory with the memory service down](https://agent-ci-infra-bot.llmbots.co/pr-media/2d6dd49c66be7b2c258751ead2ba3f74840fadffca7dd7583a033048f9974ab6)

4. The same pane 15.4 s later, after only the mocked `/api/health` answer changed to `healthy`, with the same `Check again` control beside the reading:

![Scientific memory recovered while the pane stayed open](https://agent-ci-infra-bot.llmbots.co/pr-media/0c6b589881376a06ae3f5ac5764b90b87d6a159cebe3ca8193192378355681c0)

Measured in that run: recovery 15,375 ms, URL before/after `http://127.0.0.1:4175/` (unchanged), navigation entries `1 → 1` (no reload), `/api/health` reads `3 → 4` (one background interval), viewport 1500×950, and `Check again` was never clicked. Heading, row and right-aligned reading sit exactly where they do in the zh-CN pair, so the two pairs can be compared frame to frame.

On the two non-blocking notes: (a) a pane left open issues one bounded read per 15 s interval, only while the switch is on, and the timer is cleared on unmount or when it goes off — the run above needed a single extra read to show recovery; (b) importing `MEMORY_STATUS_POLL_MS` into the spec follows the existing `apps/desktop/e2e/settings-interactions.spec.ts` precedent, which imports `LOCALE_STORAGE_KEY` from `src/state/storage.js`. No behaviour changed in this round.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: a recovered memory service reads 运行正常 while the page stays open.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Closes #1384

`域名白名单` reads as a hard boundary, but an approved network request widens one execution's policy, and after a denial the agent can still reach the host by host execution, outside the sandbox. Copy only: the Issue's first option (disclose the widening) plus the second (host-execution consequence).

Settings help and both cards now state the starting-policy scope, the one-execution widening (continued approval for the run stops the card), that a denial edits nothing, that 完全访问 / Always allow approves without a card, and that host execution ignores the policy.

Issue #1397: `readNumber()` made invalid text `undefined`; `maxTokens` became `null` and depth/nodes accepted `0`. This revision also enforces the store's ranges and protects late edits.

## What changed
- Ranges match `services/api/src/store/settings.ts`: depth 1–20, nodes 2–10000, tokens >= 1. Out-of-range values are refused, the note names the range, Save is disabled; inputs carry `max={20}` / `min={2} max={10000}`. Empty tokens is still `null`; empty depth/nodes is refused.
- Refused text stays visible with `aria-invalid`, a red border and a `role="alert"` note linked by `aria-describedby`. `badInput` (`1e999` -> `value=""`) is refused, not empty; `onInput` lets a refused field return to "no cap".
- Every edit (numbers, selects, prompts) bumps an edit generation; a reload or PUT response after an edit no longer reseeds the draft or fields, and a PUT response applies only if no edit happened in flight. Fixes a post-save-reload 9 being shown but saved as 7.

Stale comments now describe the live `design.css` flex shell, and both hide rules: `shell.css` at 1100px and below (`display: none !important`, still live) and `design.css` at 820px.

pr:1419.body:
`最大深度`/`最大节点数` rendered the parsed model value and patched it only when the text already parsed, so `""`, `-` and `1.` were dropped at that keystroke and the controlled input restored the old digit.

## What changed
- All three boxes edit a local text draft, committed on blur or Enter (`commitsOnEnter`, so an IME Enter is not taken).
- Empty text has one meaning per box: the token cap commits the API's `null`; depth/nodes are required, so empty, out-of-range or fractional text is refused with `aria-invalid` and a note that `aria-describedby` points at, and Save is disabled.
- Ranges follow the store: depth 1-20, nodes 2-10000, tokens 1..Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, all checked with `Number.isSafeInteger`.
- The native `input` event is handled too, so Chromium's `badInput` (`1e999` reports `value=""`) is refused instead of read as "no cap", and the box stays clearable.
- Editing or a refusal clears the previous "saved" note; en/zh strings added.

Not a duplicate of #1397/#1409 (invalid value saved as "no cap"/0 versus boxes that cannot be edited). Both touch the same helper, so the second to land needs a rebase; this refuses invalid commits, covering that outcome too.

pr:1427.body:
Several reproduced failures caused incomplete exports, stalled previews, incorrect CLI exit codes, or incorrect handling of caller input. This PR fixes those paths and adds regression coverage.

## Evidence export and PDF extraction

- Use both source and identifier for scientific-memory database records in research packages, including edge references. Records from different sources can share an identifier and survive export and reimport.
- Continue desktop writes from the actual byte offset and discard the temporary file on failure or stalled writes.
- Retry pending custom Web export previews independently of the defaults, cancel stale requests when selections change, and offer a retry when the wait budget expires.
- Use the actual PDF page bounding box when clipping images so offset MediaBoxes retain visible images.

## CLI, model requests, and test teardown

- Reconcile early CLI stream closes with persisted run state and resume from the last durable SSE ID. Report failure when no terminal result can be confirmed.
- Share CLI option-value parsing between the environment-file pre-scan and normal parsing so literal `--env-file` content reaches the run unchanged.
- Count structured contributed text against the same context budget as plain text.
- Honor seconds and HTTP dates in `Retry-After` and preserve the provider's wait when forwarding the delay.
- Close the continuation-test broker and store before removing the Windows test fixture directory to prevent SQLite `EBUSY` errors.

## UI screenshots

The screenshots show the **Export Research Package** dialog in a local browser with the custom preview endpoint returning HTTP 202.

**Preview pending.** The dialog retries automatically while the export buttons are disabled.

![Custom file preview pending while the dialog retries](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5673ca5c-c110-499d-924f-4890b71d5916)

**Preview timed out.** After 10 seconds, the dialog shows a timeout message and a Retry button.

![Custom file preview timed out with a Retry button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55a9351a-e23c-4f9b-a5b0-dc930ffe766e)

## Validation

The branch is based on upstream `main` at `991ba2cc5d33fd9ac49f6b1289c8db156e4cc837`. Git range-diff reported both patches unchanged after rebasing. No local tests were rerun for this submission. Local layer counts for `ci:l1`, `ci:ut`, `ci:st`, and `ci:e2e` are unavailable for the submitted head.

During development before the rebase, `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `git diff --check` passed. Targeted verification recorded 212 passing cases: 95 Web dialog, model, context, and launcher tests, 77 Web/API research-package tests, 10 desktop export-sink tests, 26 local memory-graph tests, 3 PDF tests, and 1 Windows continuation integration test.

## E2E user journeys

The following checks used the pre-rebase candidate `c3315b6b6c31bddc1a2e18191dcd6d12cab82c53`. Chromium used an isolated local API, Runner, and memory-graph stack on Ubuntu WSL2. The CLI checks used the launcher with a loopback HTTP fixture.

| Interface and scenario | Expected | Observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser: restore a research package and export a custom selection after HTTP 202 | Automatically retry and download the revised selection | PASS. The dialog recovered automatically and the downloaded package matched the expected included and omitted file counts |
| CLI: close the stream before its terminal event | Recover available results and fail if terminal state stays unresolved | PASS. Replay recovered text and files and exited 0. An unresolved run exited 1. An event without an ID did not advance the replay cursor |
| CLI: pass literal `--env-file` content with and without a separate environment file | Preserve the content and load the explicit environment file when present | PASS. Both requests contained the literal text and used the expected fixture credentials |

Browser command: `CI_E2E_BACKEND=legacy CI_E2E_SPEC=journey-restore-research.spec.ts CI_E2E_GREP='complete research package import' bash .ci/run-e2e.sh mocked` (1 passed, 0 failed, 0 blocked, 0 skipped).

The two CLI fixture scenarios passed with 0 failed, blocked, or skipped. The checked-in launcher regression suite is available through `node --import tsx --test services/launcher/src/run.test.ts`. Coverage for the other changed paths is limited to the targeted checks above.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`

Users get intact exports, recoverable previews and CLI run results, correct PDF image extraction, consistent context limits, and provider-compliant retry timing. No configuration or data migration is required.
