items.body:
Closes #1251

Search Sessions, projects and artifacts from the desktop client — #1251's search, opened from the column's title row.

**No longer stacked.** `#1250` is merged, so the diff is this PR's own delta only.

## The owner's decision, quoted

On 2026-11-26 the code owner asked for this shape, in these words:

> 「我需要你把搜索的放大镜图标放到左上角的科研会话那个高度，然后放在侧边栏的右侧，在"收起侧栏"图标左边一点的位置，注意控制间距，不要离得太远了。点击放大镜之后，在屏幕中央出现弹窗，弹窗上支持输入搜索内容，弹窗最底部支持筛选类型：全部，项目，会话，产物（我不确定还有没有别的，如果有，你就自己加）。如果用户选择的是全部，搜索结果要按照类型做分类，按照时间由新到旧排序。」

The owner also withdrew #1251's fourth criterion — the narrowing (仅当前项目 / 仅运行中 /
有产物 / 时间窗口, the choice surviving a reload) — on 2026-11-26 at 22:18 CST. That is why this
delivery is smaller than the criterion list, and the record is in the repository rather than in
this description alone: criterion 4 is struck through in [#1251](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1251)
under *Withdrawn scope*, and the decision — what, who, when — is written out in
[this comment](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/1251#issuecomment-7194112097) on the issue.

## What the column does

**搜索 is a magnifier in the title row, not a row in the list.** It sits beside 收起侧栏,
8px from it, and opens a dialog in the middle of the window: the field, the hits and the
kinds, with the page behind it dimmed. Ctrl/Cmd+K opens the same dialog, Escape closes it.

**The field holds the caret when the dialog opens**, so the keys work without a click:
`Escape` closes, `↑`/`↓` walk the hits in the order drawn, `Enter` opens the one under the
cursor. Opening a hit closes the dialog and hands the hit to the workspace, which opens the
Session, Project or artifact it names.

**The dialog's footer is its only filter:** 全部, 项目, 会话, 产物. 全部 groups the hits
by kind in that order, and every group is newest first; a kind shows only itself. Ordering
is read from the rows themselves — `WorkbenchSearchResult` now carries `updatedAt` (a
Session's own stamp, an artifact's, or for a Project the stamp of its newest Session) —
because the route promises no order of its own.

**Search covers active Sessions.** An archived Session is not searchable and neither are
its artifacts; an imported read-only snapshot **is** searchable — 活跃 is archived versus
live, not writable versus read-only (the owner's answer, recorded here so the choice can
be checked).

**The narrowings are gone.** 项目范围 / 运行中 / 有产物 / 指定时间 used to hang off the
search row; with the row removed there is nowhere for them to live, and the owner's
decision was to drop the feature rather than move it. The column lists every active
Session again, and the stored preference, its module and its tests are gone with it. The
copy those controls used — twenty `sidebar.*` keys, both dictionaries — is gone too, so a
reader cannot find the labels of a control that no longer exists.

## What this does **not** claim

- The field searches names and titles, not message bodies; the route says so, and the empty state repeats it rather than implying a full-text search.
- The dialog is mounted by the column, as the search row was: with the column collapsed or the workbench panel open, neither the magnifier nor Ctrl/Cmd+K reaches search. That is the reach the row had, not a new limit — but it is a limit.
- A kind cannot count the kinds it is not showing. Under 全部 the note counts what the answer held back; under a kind it says that more exist, without a number.

## Verification

Run in WSL (Ubuntu, linux-amd64, Node v22.23.4) against this head's tree:

- `tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit` — clean; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` — clean.
- Desktop suite — **1612 tests / 1612 pass**, including the dialog's own cases (`tests/search-dialog.test.tsx`: the kinds keep 项目 → 会话 → 产物 and sort newest first inside each group, a kind shows only itself, the footer is the only filter, an empty answer / a failure / an unfinished list each say their own thing, a kind's note counts no other kind, and an untouched field asks for a query). `tests/sidebar.test.tsx` holds the title-row magnifier and asserts the column draws no search row and no field.
- `apps/desktop/e2e/search-dialog.spec.ts` — **3 cases, pass** in the mocked desktop gate (`node .ci/run-desktop-e2e.mjs mocked`, local run): the magnifier opens the dialog and the caret is in the field, 全部 draws 项目 → 会话 → 产物 with the newest first, Ctrl/Cmd+K reaches the same dialog, `↓ ↓` then `Enter` reads the Session the hit names, Escape closes, and a kind's note drops the number. Nothing in that file drives React state; it is the page, which is why it caught the field's missing `ref`.
- `services/api/src/workbench/index.test.ts` — 4 cases pass, including the one this
  branch's additive `updatedAt` invalidated (it asserted a Project hit by deep equality) and
  a new case for the stamp rule: a Session and an artifact know their own, a Project takes
  its newest Session's, and a Project with no Sessions falls back to its birth.
- `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs` — 231 tests, all pass, so the policy still selects this change's desktop spec.
- `test/source-test-map.json` — the dialog's entry now names both its unit file and the new spec; the deleted capture harness and the deleted filter modules are gone from the map.

The required checks on the previous head were green (`merge-gate`, `UT`, `ST`, `L1`, `L2`,
`Docker image`, `Freeze mocked E2E matrix`, `Desktop UI-ST and mocked E2E`, `Coverage`, both
`Binary release` legs); this head's checks are still running at the time of writing — the
Checks tab is the place to read them. `CodeCheck (GitCode)` is the mirror's own label and
not a required check: 未定位、非必需，需有权限者查看.

## Screenshots

**UI:** the **code owner has looked at these captures and accepted this version** (2026-11-26).
A later change to these frames would need the same look again — a code-only approval is not
enough for UI.

Rendered from `688a155c`, the head this PR asks to approve, in one capture run against that
tree, in the bundle the desktop gate builds, driven by the suite's own harness
(`installMockApi` from `apps/desktop/e2e/fixtures.ts`, plus a stubbed `GET /api/search`) at
viewport 1440×940 with `deviceScaleFactor: 2`, one browser context per locale with
`sciencediscovery-desktop:locale` set before the first paint. Ten frames: the column's title
row, and the dialog as it opens, grouped under 全部, and filtered to each kind.

The frames describe this head: the only change since `688a155c` is
`services/api/src/workbench/index.test.ts`.

All ten images live in **one** storage commit,
`b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48`; the previous set's directory was removed in the
same commit, so the branch holds one set.

| | 中文 | English |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. The title row** — 科研会话, then the 搜索 magnifier and the collapse toggle, 8px apart | ![title zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48/docs/screenshots/1290/688a155c/1290-zh-1-title-row.png) | ![title en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48/docs/screenshots/1290/688a155c/1290-en-1-title-row.png) |
| **2. The dialog opens** — 搜索 over the dimmed page, the caret already in the field | ![open zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48/docs/screenshots/1290/688a155c/1290-zh-2-dialog.png) | ![open en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48/docs/screenshots/1290/688a155c/1290-en-2-dialog.png) |
| **3. 全部** — 项目 → 会话 → 产物, newest first inside each group | ![all zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48/docs/screenshots/1290/688a155c/1290-zh-3-all.png) | ![all en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48/docs/screenshots/1290/688a155c/1290-en-3-all.png) |
| **4. 项目** — the same query, only the Projects, and the note that more exist | ![projects zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48/docs/screenshots/1290/688a155c/1290-zh-4-projects.png) | ![projects en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48/docs/screenshots/1290/688a155c/1290-en-4-projects.png) |
| **5. 产物** — and only the artifacts | ![artifacts zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48/docs/screenshots/1290/688a155c/1290-zh-5-artifacts.png) | ![artifacts en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/b308cea3a01dbb71e347bcbef2197f60c946ce48/docs/screenshots/1290/688a155c/1290-en-5-artifacts.png) |

What the frames do not claim:

- The hits are the fixture's, and the archived Session's artifact is missing from the answer on purpose: the column drops it before drawing anything.
- The dialog is a component, not a second page: it reads the same `GET /api/search` the row used to.
- Frames 2, 4 and 5 are the ones that moved in this set: the field now holds the caret on opening, and a kind's note no longer borrows 全部's count.

items.body:
## What changes

The first-run wizard's data-directory page probes the input on a 400ms debounce, and its writability check was `ensureWritableDir` — `mkdirSync(recursive)` plus a write probe. Every half-typed value therefore created real directories on the user's disk: typing `D:\ai\sd\data` left `D:\ai` and `D:\ai\sd` behind whenever the path was retyped or abandoned, and page-load auto-probing pre-created the default `%LocalAppDATA%\ScienceDiscovery` before any user choice. This is the same litter class as problems W8 (half-typed relative paths resolving under the CWD) — W8's guards covered the CWD and the install root, but not intermediate values of legitimate absolute paths.

- `application/src/wizard-data-dir.ts`: add `nearestExistingDir` (walks up like `freeBytesForPath`) and `probeWritableWithoutMkdir` — the write probe now lands in the nearest EXISTING ancestor and is deleted immediately, so input-time probing never creates anything. `ensureWritableDir` is unchanged and becomes the confirm-time primitive.
- `application/src/main.ts`: `wizard-confirm-dir` runs `ensureWritableDir` after the read-only checks pass and before saving wizard state — the chosen dir first exists when the user confirms (matching the page copy), and a file squatting on the target fails here with a truthful message instead of after the state was saved.
- `application/test/wizard-data-dir.test.ts`: 5 new cases.

## Impact to review

Behaviour change is confined to the wizard's data-directory page:

- Input-time probing (typing, browse-pick, page-load default) no longer creates directories — it was the bug.
- Directory creation moves to confirm time. The page copy "确认后将在选定的目录准备运行环境" now matches the actual timing.
- One accepted weakening: "a file occupies the target path" is no longer discovered during typing; it reads as generic 不可写 on the check page (the ancestor probe writes into the file and fails) and fails at confirm time with "目录创建失败（请检查权限或杀毒软件）" — before any wizard state is saved.
- W8 (relative-path CWD guard) and W16 (install-root collision ordering) behaviour and tests are unchanged and green.

## Validation

- `application` unit tests: `wizard-data-dir.test.ts` 28/28 including the new cases — probing a half-typed path leaves no directories behind (`existsSync` asserted false for every intermediate value); probing an existing dir is idempotent; a file on the target reads as unwritable; `nearestExistingDir` anchor semantics; `probeWritableWithoutMkdir` rejects relative/drive-relative input without touching the filesystem.
- Wizard core files (`wizard-data-dir` / `wizard-state` / `wizard-dom` / `uninstall-data`): 57 pass / 0 fail / 1 pre-existing skip.
- `tsc -p application/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- Full `application` suite: 362/367; the single failure (`updater.test.ts`, missing `electron-updater` package in the local environment) reproduces on the untouched main baseline — environment-level, unrelated to this change.

## E2E user journeys

Manual journey covered by the new unit cases; a packaged-install journey re-run is planned with the next build (the wizard flow itself is unchanged step-for-step, only the side-effect timing moved). UT-level: typing `<tmp>\ai\sd\data` with 400ms pauses asserts zero residue on disk; retyping to a different path asserts no leftovers from the abandoned attempt.

## Release

Release category: release:patch
User impact: No data migration; existing installs keep their wizard state. New and re-onboarded users no longer get junk directories from half-typed paths, and the chosen data directory is created only on explicit confirmation.
Compatibility: `ensureWritableDir` remains exported and its self-defence (never mkdir a relative path) is intact; callers outside the wizard flow are unaffected.

items.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
items.body:
Desktop Skill imports installed packages without saying whether the package was switched on, and a Git import could install a repository the form no longer showed. Main has since redesigned this surface into dialogs and notices, so the fixes are expressed in that design rather than rebased on top of the old one.

## F1 — a stale page could import another repository
`SkillGitImportView` owns its results by generation: every field edit, reset and new inspection invalidates and aborts a pending page. A page whose repository/commit differs from the rows on screen is discarded, and import refuses a source the displayed rows were not read from, asking for a fresh inspection.

## F2 — upload hid the activation failure
The upload dialog keeps the package's activation outcome. When the switch is refused the dialog stays open with the reason and a 启用 retry that repeats only the enable request, so recovery never uploads the package again; a successful retry closes it on the usual success notice.

## F3 — git auto-enable failures were swallowed
`enableCreatedSkills` reports per-package failures and, separately, a failed skill-state read, and a failed run is no longer cached, so a retry really re-issues the read and the switches. The notice belongs to the job that produced it: it has its own identity and close, survives dismissing the import/progress notice, and a later import that switches its own packages on cleanly leaves it in place. Its retry only re-enables.

## F5 — activation skipped, reported as a failed save
When the catalog page has not loaded, the switch state is read directly and the package is enabled instead of inferring "no switches" and reporting a failed save for a write that never happened.

## Validation
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop exec tsx --import ./tests/support/css-preload.mjs --test tests/skills-settings.test.tsx tests/skills-import-edit.test.tsx tests/git-skill-import-job.test.ts` → 60 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` → 1650 passed, 0 failed; `pnpm typecheck` and the desktop build pass.
- The regression cases fail on the pre-fix sources (8 of 45), and the new job-identity case fails against the previous unconditional activation notice.

## Not covered
Finding 3 / F4 (the in-memory job/activation lifecycle) is deliberately untouched: it still needs the product decision requested on the Issue, and no client-refresh journey is claimed or required.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: a refused activation is reported, outlives the import notice and any later successful import, and is retryable without reimporting; a Git import can no longer install a repository the fields no longer name.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Closes #1442

### 测试

```
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop exec tsx --import ./tests/support/css-preload.mjs --test tests/skills-settings.test.tsx tests/skills-import-edit.test.tsx tests/git-skill-import-job.test.ts
```

## What changed
- `search_finished` names the populations apart: `attempts` (every selection that spent a round, failed calls included), `generated` (distinct new programs, seed excluded), `evaluated` (scored candidates) and `archiveNodes` (baseline included). `candidates` keeps its baseline-inclusive meaning; older events omit the new fields.
- The engine's shortfall log and `summariseRun` measure the plan against attempts, so a 6-round run with one failed call no longer reads as "made 5 of 6".
- `expanded.depth` comes from the `parent_id` chain (root 0, unknown parent 0) in all three emitters; failed/empty attempts use their selected parent's depth. `iteration`/`nodeIndex` are unchanged.
- OpenEvolve publishes only `gateScore`; it no longer copies it into `rolloutScore`. Old persisted events are not migrated; readers fall back, as the schema documents.
- The API fold reconciles a stored run's `candidates` with `attempts` at the terminal event, and the web view judges the shortfall on `attempts`.

items.author: ink999107
items.body:
## What

Three fixes on the desktop Review Specialist card.

**A Deep review no longer asks for a Deep review.** When the Deep pass ended without a verdict, the card kept the Quick pass's claim-support row, so it told the reader to run the level they had just run. The gap row now reports what the Deep attempt itself produced. The stage-level "语义" row is gone: `smartStatus` is one verdict for the whole stage, so it repeated the gap above it and contradicted the per-claim source rows below it.

**Warnings are amber again.** Rows for `warning` findings were painted red while their own text called them a reminder. Red now means a critical finding, a contradiction, or an incomplete delivery; warnings are counted separately in the header, as the web client already splits them.

**The card renders at the end of the turn it reviewed.** A checkpoint message is persisted when the review starts — mid-turn, before the run writes its answer — so the stored order drew the card under the question and above the work it is a verdict on. Cards are now drawn after their turn's answer. A card written by the running turn is held until that turn ends; a card from an earlier turn, or a review the reader started from the session menu, is drawn at once.

The visible wording follows: the check tooltip now names Deep review rather than "the source service", and the unreachable "source verification reached no conclusion" string (and its body) is removed with the stage row it described.

## Validation

- `apps/desktop` unit suite: 1600 pass / 0 fail
- Desktop e2e (`reviewer.spec.ts` + `conversation.spec.ts`, Chromium, `/api/**` mocked): 16 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped
- `pnpm typecheck` across the workspace: clean

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the card's content, tone and placement as far as the mocked suite reaches: the 14 `reviewer.spec.ts` journeys cover the Quick/Deep outcome matrix, the Deep gap and tone, and the card arriving on its own after the coordinator finishes; `conversation.spec.ts` covers compose/answer/replay.

The new end-of-turn placement is asserted by unit tests (`apps/desktop/tests/conversation.test.tsx`, 7 cases including the boundaries: card after its turn's answer, card above the next turn, a checkpoint written before the first question, two checkpoints in one turn, live-turn card held until the turn ends with the manual review exempt, a card whose write time is unreadable drawn rather than hidden, earlier-turn card drawn while the next turn streams) — the mocked fixtures do not model a checkpoint persisted mid-run, so no browser journey covers that ordering yet.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer — this fork has no write access to upstream labels)
User impact: a Deep review card now says what the Deep pass actually produced instead of asking for a Deep review; warnings are amber rather than red; the card appears under the turn's answer instead of under the question.
Compatibility and migration: none.

A criterion may be called `score` (the control plane's default), yet domains merged raw measurements and the normalised aggregate under that key: raw 0.6 became 0.3, the baseline reference stayed empty so `relative_to_baseline` normalised each candidate against itself, and reporters filtered `score` out (`criteria: {}`).

## Changes
- New `outcome.py` owns the reserved names and shape: `score` (aggregate), `criteria` (normalised per criterion, the event payload), `rawCriteria` (measurements). `metrics[<id>]` stays raw for non-colliding ids.
- `script_domain`, `scorecard_domain`, `test_gate_domain` and `judge_domain` build through it; `score`/`seconds` keep their raw value.
- Both engines seed baselines from `rawCriteria` and publish the normalised map in `evaluated.criteria`; probes read the same.
- Scope: `dataset_metric` and `test_gate` had the same collision and use the helper. The probe's `custom_script` branch is wired: it fills a baseline reference before scoring the damaged copy, so acceptance bullet 3 is met there, not narrowed to `dataset_metric`. `_probe_gated` wiring is included too (latent today; proposals force identity for `test_gate`).
- `score` is not rejected; existing evaluators and stored runs keep working.

## Verification
`test_outcome.py` (15): `score` clamp [0,2] on raw 0.6 keeps raw 0.6 and aggregate 0.3 in all three domains; a differently named criterion; `seconds`; both probes; both reporters; plus engine-level PUCT/OpenEvolve tests (root raw 0.6, candidate raw 1.2 -> reward/criteria 0.3333), which fail if either seeding line reverts. Pre-fix: 14 failed / 1 passed; fixed: 15 passed.

`pnpm evolve:test`: 428 passed, 27 failed — all `SandboxUnavailable` (no bwrap here) and the same 27 fail on unmodified main. `pnpm ci:ut`/`ci:st` planned 8565/69, executed 0 (jiuwenswarm backend unavailable).

## Risk
`evaluated.criteria` now carries the documented normalised values; raw values live in `metrics.rawCriteria`.

Release category: release:fix

Closes #1458

Apply the updated MCP design to the desktop settings page. Scope is MCP only; Skills and Specialists retain current main behavior and UI.

- Add All / My / Official catalog tabs, name/description search, responsive cards, and filtered bulk enable/disable with partial-failure retry.
- Use centered create, edit and details dialogs. The single dark Add dropdown offers manual entry or JSON file/paste prefilling in the same editable confirmation form.
- Keep card, details and form service switches synchronized. Session defaults remain independent in details; built-in sources keep their supported default-selection control.
- Add Try it to open a fresh conversation with the chosen MCP and current model, without sending a message or granting extra permissions.
- Preserve HTTP/SSE/STDIO, exact legacy arguments, stored credentials, OAuth start/cancel/open/clear, actual tool previews, latest-check feedback and named deletion confirmation.

### Regression test design

- Search and switch catalog categories; apply a filtered bulk operation, refuse one write, and retry without rewriting successful or hidden services.
- Persist both service-enable directions, reopen the editor and reload; keep session defaults independent and recover refused writes or cancelled edits.
- Retain HTTP OAuth configuration and the stored client-secret sentinel, as well as exact STDIO argument arrays and stored environment/header credentials.
- Fill manual or JSON file/paste configurations, edit before confirming, validate hidden batch entries, and retry partial imports without duplicates.
- Keep the JSON caret in the source through repeated valid parses; hand focus to filled fields only after file upload.
- Show refused authorization/clear-grant operations inside the visible details dialog and allow retry.
- Verify first/last keyboard entry and wraparound, Escape/focus return, modal focus containment and busy locks.
- Recover a blocked OAuth popup, cancel or clear authorization, and retain the open-page action's plain styling and new-tab/opener-isolation attributes.
- Open a source-specific trial conversation without sending. The separate SDK Echo journey then explicitly sends a prompt, verifies the invocation/result, persists edits, cancels/confirms deletion and checks reference cleanup.
- Inspect English/Chinese layouts and smaller windows while retaining Skills and Specialists behavior.

items.body:
`state_for()` settled restart orphans on every read: `list`, `get` and `events` (once per streamed frame) all call it, so reading even an archived, read-only Session rewrote the research to `interrupted`, stamped the restart reason and closed its running activities.

## Changes
- `state_for()` is now a pure read of the in-process engine state or the stored file; it never calls `store().save()`.
- New `reconcile_orphaned_researches()` runs the verdict once: `running`/`pausing` researches become `interrupted` with the existing reason, running activities become `stopped` with `finishedAt`/`error`, saved, logged and counted. It skips ids a live engine owns and leaves paused/completed records byte-identical.
- `server.py` calls it from a FastAPI `lifespan` startup hook, so the verdict lands at the restart instead of on the first read; a failure is logged without blocking boot.
- Read-only API semantics unchanged (`list`/`get`/`defaults` may read a read-only Session; mutations still use `assertSessionWritable`); no multi-worker assumption added.

## Validation
`pytest services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py services/evolve/tests/test_server.py -q` → 69 passed, 0 failed. New tests: list/get/events leave the file byte-identical with status `running` (failing against the old write); reconciliation settles only `running`/`pausing` (second pass 0, live engine skipped, log asserted); the server test boots via `TestClient(module.app)`, so removing the `lifespan=` wiring makes it fail.

Full evolve UT `pnpm evolve:test` → 416 passed, 27 failed; the same 27 fail on unmodified main (413 passed, 27 failed): this host has no bubblewrap and all 27 are sandbox tests untouched here. CI provisions it.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED locally: the stack needs the bubblewrap sandbox this host lacks; the mocked browser layer runs in CI.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: reads no longer change a research; a restart still settles orphans, at boot.
Compatibility: none.

Closes #1456

### Tests

```
uv run --project services/evolve --extra test --extra candidates pytest services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py services/evolve/tests/test_server.py -q
```

## Summary

1. Routes only **merge queue (`merge_group`)** runs of **`UT`** and the three heavy **L2 mocked E2E shards (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`)** to self-hosted Docker runners (`[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`), gated behind the repository variable `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'` (default off).
2. Enables **in-runner 2-stack local parallelism (`CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`)** for the two long standard mocked E2E shards (`standard-config` and `standard-journeys`) so each job runs two fully isolated local stacks in parallel (disjoint loopback ports, runtime directories, `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` roots, desktop Vite port/cache directories, and Playwright `workers: 1`), cutting L2 end-to-end wall time roughly in half on both self-hosted and GitHub-hosted runners.

Closes #1360

## Motivation

In merge-queue runs, `UT` (~13 min) and the three heavy L2 mocked E2E shards (`standard-config` ~20 min, `standard-journeys` ~20 min plus ~3.5 min queued behind `max-parallel: 4`, `research` ~10 min) dominate wall-clock time before `L3 real E2E` can start. Moving those four trusted merge-queue jobs onto dedicated Dockerized self-hosted runners with container-local caches and running 2 isolated stacks inside each of the two long standard shards brings all four jobs into a ~9–12 min band without exposing self-hosted runners to untrusted `pull_request` (or fork) runs or splitting any spec file.

## Changes

### Merge-queue self-hosted routing & container-local cache
- **`.ci/tier-policy.mjs`**:
  - Export `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER = ['self-hosted', 'Linux', 'X64', 'sciencediscovery']`.
  - Compute `self_hosted_merge_queue = event === 'merge_group' && selfHostedMergeQueue === true` and `ut_runner` (`SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER` when enabled, otherwise `'ubuntu-latest'`). Non-`merge_group` events (`pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`, `workflow_call`, `schedule`, `push`) always fail closed to `'ubuntu-latest'`.
- **`.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`**:
  - Export `HEAVY_MOCKED_SHARDS` (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`) and `buildMockedMatrix()`.
  - Emit `runner`, `self_hosted`, and `local_concurrency` (`2` for `standard-config`/`standard-journeys`, `1` for `research`/`governed`/`literature`) per shard.
- **`.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`**:
  - Manage a `flock`-serialized, content-hashed read-only JiuwenSwarm installation under `${SD_CI_CACHE_DIR:-/ci-cache}/jiuwenswarm/<key>/src`.
  - Strip `.git` and pre-install `pytest>=8.3.5` (for `check:swarm-contract`) while holding the lock so concurrent UT/E2E jobs never mutate the shared venv and `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` takes its pre-installed read-only fast path while every job keeps its own isolated `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` under `CI_RUNTIME_DIR`.
  - Export only `JIUWENSWARM_SRC` to `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**:
  - Wire `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` through `policy` -> `e2e-plan` / `ut` / `e2e`.
  - Raise mocked `e2e` `max-parallel` from `4` to `5` and pass `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY: ${{ matrix.local_concurrency }}`.
  - Skip cross-region `actions/cache` round trips (pnpm, uv, Playwright Chromium, JiuwenSwarm) only when a job is routed to a self-hosted runner, replacing JiuwenSwarm cache restore with `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`.
  - Make `Provision the bubblewrap sandbox` idempotent in `ut` and `e2e` by probing `bwrap --unshare-user --ro-bind / / --dev /dev true` before invoking `sudo apt-get` / `sudo sysctl`.
- **`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`**:
  - Export `sharedCacheEnv()` and honor pre-set `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `npm_config_cache`, and `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` (matching existing `UV_CACHE_DIR` handling) while preserving exact workspace-local fallbacks when unset.

### In-runner 2-stack local parallelism (`standard-config` & `standard-journeys`)
- **`test/support/tagged/execution.mjs`**:
  - Export `PARALLEL_MOCKED_SHARDS`, `mockedLocalConcurrency()`, `splitEntriesByFile()`, `mockedExecutionLanes()`, and `mockedSlotEnvironment()`.
  - Balance whole spec files across 2 lanes (never splitting a spec file across stacks); for `standard-config`, keep `mocked-standard-config-fresh` in its own pristine stack and keep the 9 JiuwenSwarm supplemental checks exclusively on `mocked-standard-config-global`. Single-file PR selections and non-standard shards (`research`, `governed`, `literature`) remain single-stack.
- **`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`**:
  - Execute `mockedExecutionLanes()` concurrently via `Promise.all` with disjoint loopback port blocks (`4410`/`4420`, `4411`/`4421`, `4510`/`4520`, `17774`/`17784`, desktop Vite `4178`/`4179`), separate `CI_RUNTIME_DIR`, `JIUWENSWARM_HOME`, and Vite cache dirs. Default remains `1` (serial) for local `pnpm ci:e2e`.
- **`.ci/run-e2e.sh`**:
  - Serialize JiuwenSwarm port allocation across concurrent local stacks via `CI_E2E_SWARM_START_LOCK` (`flock`), explicitly closing fd 8 (`8>&-`) on child commands so daemonized processes never inherit the lock descriptor; avoid redundant `ln -sfn` rewrites on `test/node_modules`.
- **`test/helpers/desktop-evolve.ts` & `apps/desktop/vite.config.ts`**:
  - Honor `E2E_DESKTOP_PORT` (default `4178`) and `E2E_DESKTOP_VITE_CACHE_DIR` so concurrent desktop-entry specs never collide on Vite port or `.vite` cache.
- **`.ci/mocked-report.mjs`**:
  - Audit all `mocked-*` sub-lane directories in shard artifacts so any unexpected `jiuwenswarm-checks.json` outside the single designated check batch fails with `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`.
- **`.ci/README.md`, `.ci/mocked-shards.test.mjs`, `.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`**:
  - Document the toggle, `max-parallel: 5`, and `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`, and add unit, CLI, workflow contract, reconciliation, and hermetic shell tests.

## Safety & Rollout

- **Default off for self-hosted routing**: While `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` is unset, all PR and merge-queue jobs stay on `ubuntu-latest`. Clearing or changing the variable rolls back immediately with no workflow edit.
- **Event boundary**: `pull_request` (including forks), `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, `push`, light mocked shards (`governed`, `literature`), `ST`, desktop jobs, packaging, and real E2E jobs never route to self-hosted runners even when `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true`.
- **Strong isolation**: Each local E2E lane runs its own isolated service stack and Playwright `workers: 1`; `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=1` reverts any run to serial execution.

## Verification

### Local static & unit checks
- `node --test .ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`: **8/8 passed** (0 failed, 0 skipped)
- `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`: **228/228 passed** (0 failed, 0 skipped)
- `bash -n .ci/run-e2e.sh`, `bash -n .ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`, YAML validation on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: **passed**
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check`: **passed** (11 cases, 20 tags, 4 layers)
- `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`: **passed** (143 Markdown files checked)
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: **passed** (392 package source files checked)
- `CI_ENFORCE_SOURCE_MAP=1 node .ci/changed-path-check.mjs`: **passed** (0/0 mapped)
- `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: **passed** (127 spec files, 0 errors)

### Full 4-way concurrent self-hosted Docker benchmark (`bc801d94d`, 16 vCPU / 60.6 GiB host)
All 4 target merge-queue jobs executed concurrently in isolated `sd-actions-runner:local` containers with `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2` on `standard-config` and `standard-journeys`:
- **`UT`** (`merge` + `--coverage`): **8345/8345 passed** in **561s (9m21s)**
- **`L2 E2E (research)`** (1 stack): **21/21 passed** in **554s (9m14s)**
- **`L2 E2E (standard-journeys)`** (2 stacks: 44 + 44): **88/88 passed** in **674s (11m14s)** (down from 17m44s single-stack / ~23m48s GitHub Actions incl. queue)
- **`L2 E2E (standard-config)`** (2 stacks: 32 + 9 Swarm checks, 4 fresh + 37 global): **73/73 passed + 9/9 JiuwenSwarm checks passed** in **735s (12m15s)** (down from 17m29s single-stack / 20m10s GitHub Actions)
- **Host resource profile (4-container concurrent window)**: CPU avg **60.4%** (9.67 / 16 vCPU, P95 80.6%), RAM peak **15.18 GiB / 60.6 GiB** (25%, 45.4 GiB free).

A report's `[evidenceN]` chip opened 科学记忆 scoped to the report's Session, and the persisted chip references carried no owning Session. Citing a node created in an earlier Session of the same project therefore always showed "This memory was not found", implying the record was deleted.

## Changes
- Card-side fallback: read the citation's scope first; when nothing matches and the citation names no Session, read once unscoped and use the hit's `sessionId` for provenance. Budget refusals and an unreachable or disabled service stay "unavailable", never "missing".
- The unscoped read is limited to `GLOBALLY_UNIQUE_ID_LABELS` (`Artifact`, `Evidence`, `SourceFile`), whose node id is the record's own key. `DbRecord` is excluded on purpose: its id is the bare `identifier` and the graph keys those nodes by `(session_id, source, identifier)`, so a citation that names no Session returns `unlocated` instead of accepting a same-id record from another Session. The stale "Node ids are globally unique" comment now states this actual semantics.
- A page the sidecar cut short is not proof that nothing exists. `resolveCitation` carries `truncated` out of the scoped and the unscoped read alike and returns the new `unlocated` outcome instead of `missing`; `missing` is now reachable only from a page the sidecar did not cap.
- `memory.notFoundBody` (en/zh) now only says no record matches the citation; an outage keeps its own message, and `unlocated` has its own copy (`memory.unlocatedTitle` / `unlocatedBody`, en/zh) so it never renders the not-found sentence.
- New citations carry the owning Session: the sidecar's `cited_targets`/`chip_map` gain `session_id`, `toChipMap()` copies it, and the report reference persists it. Artifact chips keep none because the artifact dialog resolves them through the project.

## Validation
All numbers below were produced in the task checkout at head `c5ac07e1141e911971859730c8fe9973eb426968` (tree `aa11afc5302aec0f80fd67c2391f9f66524f81f3`), after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; each names the local log it comes from. The previous description's 1424/1424 figure belonged to the old head `76bf461c` and is not reused here.

- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` — 1435 planned / 1435 executed / 1435 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped, 136 suites (log: `.tmp/desktop-test.log`).
- `pnpm typecheck` — exit 0 (log: `.tmp/typecheck.log`).
- Regression tests against the previous implementation: with only the changed source files restored to `76bf461c` and the new tests kept, the two touched test files give 37 tests / 30 passed / 7 failed, failing exactly on the truncated-page cases (scoped, widened, own-Session, already-unscoped) and the foreign same-id `DbRecord` cases (log: `.tmp/prefix-run.log`).
- Sandboxed layers: `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` still cannot preflight in the task environment — `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE`, no user namespaces, planned 8148/63/189 and executed 0. They are reported as **not run locally**, not as passing; the sandbox-free equivalent is the build + desktop UT + typecheck above, and the containerised layers come from this PR's CI.
- GitHub Actions [run 45170452369](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45170452369) on this head (`c5ac07e1`): `conclusion=success`. Select CI policy, L1, UT, ST, Docker image and Binary release (x86_64/aarch64) succeeded; L4/L5, mocked E2E and the macOS installer are skipped by policy for this change.

## Evidence
Captured in the desktop UI (Chromium 1280×800 CSS viewport at DPR 2) through the desktop E2E mocked control plane. The report lives in `session-1` and cites `[evidence1]`; that Evidence node belongs to another Session, `session-2`. The mock answers the scoped node-type read with no hits and the unscoped read with the node — the shape this fix handles. The capture workspace is tree-identical to `c5ac07e` (`git diff c5ac07e` empty, each changed file hashing the same), so the frames match this head; the capture spec was throwaway and is not committed.

Refs #1239 (evidence part — see scope below).

## Summary

Nightly run 44361037291, shard `research-11`: the managed Python base setup reached terminal `failed` and J5 was BLOCKED with no executed case. The failure transcript existed in the API response (`setup.error` / `components.conda.error`) but J5 and J3 built their BLOCKED reason from `setup.state` + `setup.message` only, so the transcript never reached the journey report and the next occurrence could not be attributed to an external channel/network problem or to a repository defect.

This PR carries that transcript into the BLOCKED reason. It does **not** investigate the Nightly setup failure itself — that failure is still unconfirmed as a repository defect (same commit, same run, J3 passed the readiness assertion in the L2 job), and it cannot be fixed until a transcript is captured.

## What changed

- `test/helpers/environment-setup.ts`: widened `EnvironmentSetup` with optional `error` and `components` (matching `packages/schema/src/environment.ts:451-485`), and added one shared formatter `formatEnvironmentSetupBlockedReason(setup)`. It returns the existing `state: message` text, appends a length-bounded `setup.error`, and appends `conda: <components.conda.error>` only when it differs from `setup.error`. The bound is 1200 chars, the same as the `#1108` precedent (`MANAGED_SHELL_REASON_LIMIT`).
- `test/journey-real-request.spec.ts` (J5) and `test/journey-prepare-environment.spec.ts` (J3): the BLOCKED reason now goes through the formatter.
- `test/helpers/journeys.ts`: `environmentSetup()` return type widened to the exported `EnvironmentSetup` (no runtime change).
- `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts`: 6 new cases (see below).

A failed setup remains BLOCKED; no pass/fail semantics change. Test helpers/specs only — no runner, API, or workflow change.

## Proof package

1. **Base SHA:** upstream `main` @ `59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608` (merge commit of #1236). Reproduced and fixed on this commit.
2. **Reproduction before the fix:** an out-of-tree probe feeds a failed setup (with `error` and `components.conda.error`) through `waitForEnvironmentSetup` and builds J5's reason exactly as the spec did. The object carries both error fields, but the reason is only `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: Conda environment setup failed)` — the transcript is absent (`LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: false`, `ECONNRESET: false`).
3. **After the fix:** the same probe through the formatter prints the transcript in the reason (`LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: true`, `ECONNRESET: true`), and an identical conda error is printed once. New unit tests fail on base (the formatter does not exist there) and pass after: `node --test test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` → **17/17 pass** (11 pre-existing + 6 new).
4. **Control case:** a setup without `error` renders byte-identically to before — covered for `error` absent, `null`, `""`, whitespace-only, `components: {}`, and `components: { conda: {} }`. The skip condition (`setup.state !== "ready"`) and J3's `.toBe("ready")` assertion are untouched.
5. **Regression scope:**
   - `node --test test/helpers/*.unit.ts`: 53 tests, 50 pass, 3 fail. The 3 failures are file-level load errors (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: test/e2e-auth.js`, generated by the E2E global setup and absent from this checkout). Verified pre-existing via `git stash`: same 3 files fail on the clean base (47 tests, 44 pass). No new failure from this diff.
   - `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: exit 0.
   - Not run: the full `pnpm ci:ut` layer (same `e2e-auth.js` limitation), the real E2E J5 (needs a paid Nightly / live stack), and the mocked J3 E2E (needs bubblewrap, not installed on this VM). The new unit tests are the verification for this evidence-only change.
6. **Diff scope:** 5 files, +137/−7. No derived files, snapshots, or docs to regenerate; no docs pin the old reason text.
7. **Risks checked and excluded:**
   - Secrets: `setup.error` is already credential-redacted at the source (`redactNetworkError` in `environment-store.ts:1458`, and `failSetup` is the sole writer of both `setup.error` and component errors), and the journey report redacts the BLOCKED reason (`journey-report.ts:377-380`). Appending the transcript adds no new secret channel.
   - Bound: both transcripts pass through the 1200-char bound; worst case ≈ 2.5k chars total in the reason.
   - Micromamba: a micromamba failure reaches the reason via `setup.error` (its failure is terminal for that attempt, so `lastSetupError` is the micromamba error); no information is lost by not appending `components.micromamba.error` separately.
   - The differing-conda branch is defensive: `failSetup` writes the same string to both fields, so today they are identical or the component one is null. It is kept (bounded, tested) so a future store change reporting a distinct per-component transcript still surfaces it.
   - Known limitation (follow-up, not this PR): a multi-line reason renders imperfectly in the journey report — `journey-report.ts:458` blockquotes only the first line in `report.md`, and the HTML `<blockquote>` collapses line breaks. No content is lost in either format; fixing the renderer touches shared report code and is left as a follow-up.

Refs #1239.

## E2E user journeys

- J5 (real E2E): BLOCKED / not run — needs a paid Nightly run / live stack with real model credentials; the new unit tests are the verification for this evidence-only change.
- J3 (mocked E2E): BLOCKED / not run — needs bubblewrap and a running stack, neither available on this VM.
- Unit: `test/helpers/environment-setup.unit.ts` 17/17 pass (see Validation above).

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none — test helpers/specs only; the next Nightly run's BLOCKED reason will carry the setup failure transcript.
Compatibility and migration: none

---

Note for the maintainer: I cannot apply the `release:internal` label myself (403), and I did not use auto-merge. Could you please add the `release:internal` label and add this PR to the merge queue when it is ready?

## Review follow-up
Path-only resolution prefers the calling Session's own Artifact, then a cross-Session candidate where `ARTIFACT_SESSION_CONFLICT` still applies. After `new_artifact: true`, the next path-only declaration appends to that Session's chain. The regression test covers the own-chain v2, a bystander 409, and no empty `base_version_id`. `docs/en/developer-docs/cas.md` documents the condition.

## Linear history on current main

# 学科知识引擎：摄取/生长/消解/消费全链 + 会话绑库与反幻觉运行时

> 与 GitCode MR [!125](https://gitcode.com/openJiuwen/sciencediscovery/merge_requests/125) 内容一致（对应 GitCode issue #86）。

把「学科知识」做成 SD 的一等资产：文献与结构化源摄取为带锚点溯源的知识图谱，图谱可离线生长、实体消解、社区聚类；对话内绑定知识库（kb scope）后，图谱成为受约束的知识来源，输出必须引用锚点，与证据账本 / 新颖性检查 / 引用核验构成多层反幻觉链路。

**283 文件，+50.8k，4 个按路径分组的 commit**（KE 核心 / agent 运行时 / Web / 技能与测试）。

---

## 新增功能

### 1. 知识引擎核心（`packages/knowledge-engine` + `services/api/src/knowledge-engine`）

- **存储域**：SQLite（知识库/文档/锚点/实体/边/社区/合并/作业/引用/公式），带迁移机制；算法核与存储分离，可独立评测
- **摄取**：LaTeX-first arXiv 通路（tar.gz 解包 + `\input` 递归内联）、JATS XML、视觉增强 PDF 解析；溯源门抽取——每个抽取结论挂文档锚点
- **生长**：离线 grow job，MMR + anchor-aware 多样本选择、收敛信号、结构化反思 directive 反哺下一轮
- **实体消解**：在线门 + 离线 job、物理合并与回滚（`ke_entity_merges`）、louvain 社区、根实体、社区报告
- **消费面**：`kb_search` / `kb_expand` / `doc_grep` 工具、entity_unified_search、三级文档阅读器（全文/结构/锚点）、引用 API（意图徽章 supporting / contrasting / mentioning + Similar / References / Cited-By）
- **REST**：`/api/ke/*` 全套 + 前端知识引擎页（cytoscape 图谱画布、生长控制面板、阅读器、引用面板）

### 2. 会话绑库（kb scope）

- session 设置新增 `kbScopeKbIds` / `kbScopeWebSearch` 运行时覆盖项；composer 底部选择器一键绑定/解绑，写路径为 fresh-GET 读改写，避免并发选择器互相回滚
- resident-summary 上下文贡献者持续注入**在库**图谱摘要（成熟度分级）；范围外知识库对工具面与摘要均不可见（防泄漏包装）
- 系统 prompt m8.3.1：上下文时钟、kb-scope 自管理指引、反编造纪律句——均在既有 5000 字符保护段预算内

### 3. 反幻觉与研究运行时

- 三级注入：证据账本（`evidence_ledger`）、新颖性检查（`novelty_check`）、引用核验（`verify_citation`）；KE 工具输出逐字文本打 nonce 不可信围栏
- finish-gate 收尾审计：技能声明 `metadata.pre-finish-audit` 即在收尾前注入审计 directive，有界续跑（≤2 次）
- 研究世界模型 `research_state`：目标钉住 / 计划生命周期 / 未决问题 / 已排除路径防复活 / 已试去重，JSON 文件锁崩溃可恢复
- 审批门计划生命周期（`packages/plan-mode`）：`propose_plan` / `revise_plan` 工具、约束级审批、版本绑定决策、决策日志；与上游 `update_plan` 快照机制共存（`AgentRunBindings` 同时携带 `planRepository` 与 `planStore`）
- stall-guard：模型调用无进展按空闲窗踢出重试（≤3 次），外层空闲看门狗兜底
- 记忆图谱镜像 `observeSessionPlan`；MCP 配置文件内容签名失效（保留上游按服务器签名比较，叠加文件级变更检测）

### 4. 技能包与评测

- 15 个方法论技能：knowledge-engine-explore/grow、evidence-notes、hypothesis-tournament、tree-search、robin-chain、virtual-lab、idea-debate、systematic-review、precise-qa、long-form-writing/audit、progressive-report、report-writer、table-analysis（多数声明 pre-finish-audit）
- 评测套件 `scripts/ke-*-eval.mjs`：growth delta-recall、discoverer 诚信维度、pairwise、citation（ALCE 三指标）、resolution、bench 539 题；`skill-test-runner` + ER 数据集构建器
- KE 旅程 E2E 9 条 + kb-scope / finish-gate 旅程，ke-stub 离线可跑

## 验证

Linux（Ubuntu WSL2），分支 `pr/knowledge-engine`（基于 upstream/main 最新 `ef65b6f`，4 个按路径分组的 commit）。

- 29 个 workspace 项目全量构建通过（含 web vite build）；`architecture:check` 通过（293 文件）
- 触及包测试全绿：workspace 119/119、context 50/50、tools 61/61、runtime-core 36/36、memory 35/35、schema 12/12、plan 5/5、plan-mode 2/2
- **services/api 全量套件 1020 tests / 1019 pass / 0 fail**（`node --test dist/*.test.js dist/**/*.test.js`，123s 干净退出）
- 与纯 upstream/main 对照树同环境跑 server.test.js 验证无回归：upstream 86/86，本分支 86/86；期间修复了三处合并引入的问题（MCP transport 双重 close、内置技能清单落位、保护段预算超限），并把 KE sqlite 连接补上服务器关闭回收（否则每个 boot 泄漏 db+wal+shm 句柄并在进程退出时挂起 drain）
- 双计划系统共存验证：propose_plan 审批门与 update_plan 快照在同 run 注册、互不干扰（context-assembly 集成测试覆盖）

items.body:
## What does this PR do / why do we need it

Implements the **full three-layer plan** for natural-language program evolution (GitHub issue #310): turn `/evolve-design` from a hidden slash command into something a natural-language sentence can trigger, with the framework actively recommending a tree-search evolution and the interaction staying natural-language end to end.

Today `/evolve-design` is a hidden slash command: a user must already know the prefix to start an evolution search, and the only visible entry is a button in the artifact detail modal that fills the composer with `/evolve-design make the artifact X better: ` (still requiring manual completion). The interaction is command-shaped, not natural-language.

### Layer 1 — Composer intent recognition (frontend)

- **`apps/web/src/evolve/intent.ts`** (new): pure `detectEvolveIntent(message)` — true only when an improvement verb pairs with an evolvable target (`program` / `code` / `algorithm` / `function` / `model` / `script` / `artifact` …). Non-evolvable targets (`formatting` / `layout` / `description` / `explanation`) never match, and bare "better" with no target never matches. `isEvolveDesignCommand()` separates the explicit slash command from natural language.
- **`EvolveSuggestionBar`** (new): a low-intrusion confirmation bar. Detection only *offers*; the user must explicitly accept before the algorithm picker opens — an evolution search spends real budget (mutations + sandboxed evaluations), so a false positive is worse than a missed suggestion.
- **`App.tsx`**: an explicit `/evolve-design` command opens the algorithm picker directly (existing behavior preserved); a natural-language intent shows the confirmation bar first, and only an accepted suggestion opens the picker. Both flags reset when the message leaves evolve intent.

### Layer 2 — Agent-driven recommendation (backend)

- **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts`**: the `create_evolve_run` tool description now tells the agent to **recommend** an evolution search when the user asks in natural language to improve a program / code / algorithm / model / result against a measurable target — not only when they type `/evolve-design`. The agent phrases it as a plain suggestion ("this looks like a search-shaped problem; want me to run an automated search that keeps the best-scoring variant?") and starts only after the user confirms. This builds on the evolve-design skill, whose description already lists natural-language triggers.

### Layer 3 — Visible entry points (frontend)

- **Composer**: a new sparkle "program evolution" button fills a natural-language prompt (`Improve the program: ` / `改进一下这个程序：`) instead of a slash command; `detectEvolveIntent` recognises it and offers the suggestion bar.
- **Artifact detail modal**: the evolve button now fills a natural-language seed prompt (`Make the artifact X better: ` / `让产物 X 变得更好：`) instead of the `/evolve-design ...` command text.
- **`intent.ts`**: adds `artifact` / `产物` as evolvable targets and `变得更好` as an improvement verb so both seed prompts are recognised.

### Why confirmation before the picker?

A search spends real budget. Detection is a guess, so it must only offer; the user's explicit accept is the gate. This is the core false-positive guard — a user saying "优化一下" while discussing formatting is never routed into an expensive search.

### Why verb+target pairing?

Intent detection is deliberately narrow: `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `这个更好` / `make this better` all stay silent; only sentences pointing at an evolvable target (program / code / algorithm) match.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Closes #310.

## Review follow-up (2026-10-29)

- Closing keyword corrected to plain `Closes #310`; the earlier markdown-link form left GitHub's `closingIssuesReferences` empty, so the merge would not have auto-closed the issue.
- Blocking item "CI green on this tip" is already satisfied **on this tip**: run [40645827814](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40645827814) (attempt 2) is `success`, 17 checks success (L1, ST, UT, Coverage, merge-gate, 5x L2, Freeze mocked E2E, CodeCheck); L3/L4-L5/Docker/Binary are `skipped` by policy.
- Remaining blocker is the human one: re-approval and the `needs-human` product-risk decision. The tip is unchanged (`070820a6`), so no CI re-run was triggered by this edit; the label is left untouched.

## Test Plan and Test result

Verification commit: `f9fe5846` (9 files, +192/-5, single commit, based on GitHub main `cc974a14`)

- Web typecheck: `tsc --noEmit` passed, 0 errors
- Web unit tests: **107 passed / 0 failed** (includes 8 new evolve-intent tests)
- Web vite build: passed
- evolve package typecheck + tests: passed

Intent recognition behaviour verified:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `improve the program` / `优化一下这个程序` / `让程序跑得更好` | triggers |
| `Make the artifact X better` / `让产物 X 变得更好` | triggers (seed prompts) |
| `make this better` / `这个更好` | no trigger (no explicit evolvable target) |
| `优化一下界面布局` / `improve workflow steps` / `改进一下说明文字` | no trigger (non-evolvable target) |
| `the first one is better` | no trigger (ordinary conversation) |
| explicit `/evolve-design` command | opens the picker directly, no confirmation bar (existing behavior preserved) |

## Self-checklist

- [x] **Design**: follows the issue's three-layer plan; confirmation-bar guard and narrow verb+target detection address false positives and budget protection
- [x] **Tests**: `evolve-intent.test.tsx` (8 tests) ships with this PR; typecheck and web unit tests pass
- [x] **Verification**: behaviour matrix recorded above with the verification commit
- [x] **Interface**: no public API change; reuses the existing `/api/evolve/runs` chain, `EvolveToolRuntime` and `EvolveAlgorithmPicker`
- [x] **Docs**: no website-doc change required for this frontend layer

## Review follow-up (sciencediscovery-bot review 5697796828, 2026-10-30)

Both points from that review are closed in code, not in prose. The branch was rebased onto today's `main` (`4e4837a9`) with no conflicts, and now carries three commits: the feature commit, the red test commit `85a78ad8`, and the fix `54889783`. New tip: `54889783e4831af67df7df517f7bd65912ea1da4`. Diff against `4e4837a9`: 15 files, +846/−14 (the two new files are the gate and its tests).

### 1. `requestConfirmation` is required, and the gate itself fails closed

- **`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:587`** — `EvolveTurnContext.requestConfirmation` is now required (`RequestEvolveConfirmation`, declared at `:203`), so any new evolve construction site that forgets it is a compile error instead of a silent spend. `tsc -p services/api` is what enforces it.
- **`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts:385-387`** — the `turn.approvalMode !== "ask_for_dangerous"` fallback is gone; the runtime asks the gate and returns its refusal.
- **`services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts:88-97`** — when the callback is absent (only reachable from a caller outside the type system: an untyped script, a stale build, a test double), the gate returns
  `{ confirmed: false, refusedBecause: "confirmation unavailable: this turn has no approval path, so the evolution search was not started" }`.
  **Caller-visible behaviour:** `createEvolveRun` returns that string as its `refusedBecause`; the tool layer hands it to the agent, which relays it; no run is created, no discrimination probe runs, no budget is spent. It is the same data-not-exception shape as the existing "not confirmed by the user" refusal.
- **Why required rather than only fail-closed:** the field is what makes the *next* construction site safe at compile time; the runtime guard alone would only cover callers the type system never sees, and those must still be refused rather than allowed.

On `always_allow`: with the gate wired, an `always_allow` session still short-circuits inside `store.requestPermission` (`services/api/src/store.ts:5532`) — that is the product's meaning of the mode for every privileged action (`run_shell`, `direct_code`, …). The defect the review named was the *absent* gate falling back to that mode; a missing gate can no longer start a search. Making evolve pop a card in `always_allow` would make it stricter than every other privileged action, which is a permission-model decision rather than this PR's change.

### 2. Grant matching is by `resource`, so the resource now names the search

Read, not inferred:

- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5545-5552`** — `const matcherResource = permissionMatcherResource(action, resource)`, then `permissionGrants.find(grant => grant.action === action && (grant.resource === matcherResource || grant.resource === resource) && grant.state === "active" && grant.scope !== "once" && (global / project / conversation / session …))`. A standing grant is matched by **action + resource**, and non-`once` scopes are reusable.
- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5621-5629`** — deciding `allow_matching` creates a grant with `resource: permissionMatcherResource(request.action, request.resource)` and `scope: "session"`.
- **`packages/governance/src/permission-policy.ts:56-62`** — for `code` the matcher resource is the resource verbatim, so any suffix survives matching.
- **`services/api/src/store.ts:5471-5485`** — `authorizeByJiuwenSwarm` does look a record up by `toolCallId`, but only to avoid double-booking the decision row; it is not the grant lookup.

So the old `evolve-search:<sessionId>` really did let one "allow matching" click cover every later search in the session. Fixed at **`services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts:64-76`**: the key is now `evolve-search:<sessionId>:<fresh id>`, one per attempt — the card approves the search the user was shown and nothing after it, and even a retried call asks again. Wording follows the implementation in **`packages/evolve/src/index.ts:361`** ("That card approves one search: a later search in the same conversation raises its own card") and in the card label **`apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts:449`** / **`:3422`** ("this evolution search only" / "仅限本次演进搜索").

### Revert proof (fix reverted on the same tree, then restored)

```
$ git checkout 85a78ad8 -- services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts
$ cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts
not ok 1 - a turn with no approval path refuses the search instead of allowing it
not ok 2 - each search attempt gets its own grant key, even for a repeated call
not ok 3 - a grant from one search does not authorize the next search in the same session
not ok 4 - the gate asks with the call's identity and the search it is paying for
# tests 4
# pass 0
# fail 4
$ git checkout 54889783 -- services/api/src/evolution/confirmation.ts   # restored
```

The red commit `85a78ad8` carries the same four tests, failing on the unfixed gate. Test 3 drives the real `SessionStore`: it decides `allow_matching` on the first search's resource, shows the same search is then allowed, and asserts the next search is still pending (a card).

### Ran on this tip

- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts` → **4/4 pass**
- `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/evolution/*.test.ts` → **165/165 pass**
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` → **exit 0** (this is the check that enforces the required field)
- `cd packages/evolve && node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` → **10/10 pass**; `tsc -p packages/evolve` → **exit 0**
- `cd apps/web && tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` → **1183/1183 pass**; `tsc -p apps/web` → **exit 0**

**Not run:** L2/L3, Docker and binary layers, and the full `pnpm check`.

CI: pushing a new tip re-triggers the pull-request gates for it; the previous tip's green run does not carry over to `54889783`.

## Low finding follow-up (sciencediscovery-bot review 5706765348, inline 4419359334)

`PermissionDecisionActions` no longer offers **Allow same type** for an `evolve-search:` request. Each evolution search asks with a fresh single-use key (`evolve-search:<session>:<uuid>`), and a `code` grant is matched on the whole resource, so a same-type grant could never authorize a later search: the button promised a decision the backend drops, and it printed the attempt id in the help text and left a dead grant in `PermissionGrantManager`. That card now offers **Allow once** or **Deny**; ordinary `code` requests keep the button.

`RunTimeline` shows the localized scope (`permissions.evolveResource`) in its details **Resource** row instead of the raw per-attempt resource, matching the collapsed card that already hid it.

Coverage: `apps/web/tests/Permissions.test.tsx` and `apps/web/tests/RunTimeline.test.tsx` assert the evolve confirmation has one secondary action, no "Allow same type", and no `evolve-search:` string in the rendered markup. Reverting the two component files turns exactly those two tests red (`# tests 81 / # pass 79 / # fail 2`); restoring them returns 81/81.

Ran: `apps/web` `tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx` **1185/1185**; `tsc -p apps/web` exit 0; `services/api` `node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts` **4/4**.
Not run: full `pnpm check`, L2/L3, Docker/binary.

## Typecheck-gate fix

Deleting the type field left two test literals setting it; only the root `tsconfig.tests.json` checks extraneous properties (`tsc -p services/api` does not include test files), so the local run missed it.

Ran: `pnpm --recursive typecheck` exit 0; `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` exit 0; `tsc -p services/api` exit 0; `node --import tsx --test src/evolution/confirmation.test.ts` 4/4.

## Summary

Make provider token accounting a diagnostic instead of a real-E2E pass criterion, and keep the usage shapes it depends on pinned by deterministic tests. Functional task/delivery/quality assertions are unchanged.

## Rebased onto `main` (2026-11-07, `b9e5367`)

The branch had been open since 2026-10-14 and was 699 commits behind; it conflicted in three files. After the rebase:

- **The protocol-aware parser is no longer part of this diff.** `normalizeUsage` moved to `packages/model/src/usage.ts` on `main` and already takes the request's dialect, reading `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` for Chat Completions and `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` for Responses ahead of the aliases, with a conflict diagnostic. The reported bug - a probe returning `completion_tokens: 31` next to an extra `output_tokens: 0`, which the shared normalizer used to prefer - is already fixed there, so `packages/model/src/client.ts` is untouched by this PR.
- **One design choice from the original branch was not carried over.** The original parser dropped the fallback to the other dialect's fields and to `total_tokens` arithmetic entirely. `main`'s version keeps a dialect-first-then-fallback design and documents it; overriding that here would be a behaviour change on shared accounting that the maintainers already settled. The assertions that encoded the stricter rule were dropped with it rather than left failing.
- What is left is this PR's other half plus its regression coverage: the documented CI policy, the journey that stops gating on usage, and the mixed/missing-accounting cases exercised end to end.

## Changes

- `.ci/README.md` - provider usage is diagnostic evidence, not an E2E success or scoring gate; missing accounting is not evidence of zero cost; protocol parsing correctness stays enforced by deterministic tests.
- `test/journey-basic-real-api.spec.ts` - the usage step attaches the ledger instead of asserting `inputTokens`/`outputTokens` are positive, and reads the route directly so a route that cannot answer still fails the case.
- `packages/model/src/client.test.ts` - a chat completion whose usage carries conflicting aliases reports the dialect's counts (35/31/66), and a stream without usage still completes with `usage: undefined`.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts` - the gateway forwards the protocol's usage unchanged and serves the turn with none, in both streamed and non-streamed responses.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/model/src/client.test.ts` | 48/48 pass |
| `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.test.ts` | 61/62 pass; the one failure is the pre-existing `0o600` vs `0o666` file-mode assertion (Windows, fails on `main` here too) |
| `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/model build`, `@sciencediscovery/api build` | clean |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | clean |
| `markdownlint-cli2 .ci/README.md` | 0 issues |

Tests are tagged `os:linux`; ran locally with the platform filter in `test/support/tagged/compat.mjs` temporarily disabled and reverted, uncommitted. The seven paid real journeys and the nightly suite have not been rerun.

items.author: Thibaultjaigu
items.body:
Users who route through Requesty currently have to set it up as a custom OpenAI compatible provider by hand. This adds it as a built-in preset alongside OpenRouter, with the same shape: OpenAI chat completions, `GET /models` discovery, and a models.dev mapping for catalog facts and prices.

## Preset
`packages/schema/src/model-provider-presets.ts` gets a `requesty` entry right after OpenRouter: base URL `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, `apiVariant: "openai"`, `modelDiscovery: "openai-models"`, docs `https://docs.requesty.ai`, key page `https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys`. `ModelProviderPresetId` in `model-provider.ts` gains `"requesty"`. The wizard and settings UI read the preset list, so nothing else changes there. Requesty is not made a default anywhere.

## models.dev mapping
models.dev publishes a `requesty` provider whose `api` is `https://router.requesty.ai/v1`, so the host check in `pricesApplyToPreset` accepts its prices for this preset. It is mapped after OpenRouter, in the aggregator block, so first publish wins still hands capability facts to the vendor listings. The ordering test in `packages/model/src/models-dev.test.ts` now counts `requesty` as an aggregator so a misplaced insert would fail it.

## How to test
Pick Requesty in the connect wizard, paste a key from https://app.requesty.ai/api-keys, and choose a listed model such as `openai/gpt-4o-mini` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. For EU routing, edit the base URL to `https://router.eu.requesty.ai/v1`.

## Validation
Run on macOS arm64 at ae150eb, with deps installed only for `@sciencediscovery/model` and its workspace dependencies.
- `pnpm typecheck` in `packages/schema` and `packages/model`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: OK, 276 package source files checked.
- Package unit tests with `node --test "src/**/*.test.ts"`: schema 12 passed / 0 failed, model 45 passed / 0 failed (including "every aggregator mapping sits after every vendor mapping"). These files are tagged `os:linux`, so on macOS I ran them with `process.platform` reported as linux; nothing else was changed.
- Live check through the package's own code: `listProviderModels` with the preset's `baseUrl` and discovery strategy returned 762 models including `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, and `streamModelTurn` with the preset's protocol and variant streamed a reply from `openai/gpt-4o-mini` with usage reported.
- Not run: `pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e` and `apps/web` tests. The UT and E2E layers need a bubblewrap sandbox on Linux, which this macOS host does not have.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED on this host (no Linux sandbox for the local stack). The change adds one entry to a list the connect wizard already renders, and the live check above covers the provider's discovery and chat path. Happy to add or rerun a journey if you want one for this.

## Release
Release category: release:feature (label pending a maintainer, I cannot apply labels)
User impact: Requesty appears as a provider preset in the model connect wizard.
Compatibility and migration: none.

Disclosure: I work at Requesty. Happy to adjust anything to match project conventions.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Pull requests from `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` stay mergeable when `license/cla` has appeared and is not `success`. If that check never appears, the merge gate does not fail because of it. For every other author, including other bots, an appeared non-success check fails the gate. `license/cla` is not added to the ruleset required checks: a required check that never runs would block pull requests the CLA app did not mark.

## CLA policy
The merge gate calls `claGate` after the existing job aggregation. The workflow only fetches commit statuses and the pull request author.

The newest status whose context is exactly `license/cla` on the head SHA wins (GitHub lists statuses newest first). An absent context passes. `success` passes. `pending`, `failure`, `error`, and any other non-success state fail, unless the pull request author has `type` `Bot` and login exactly `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. The comparison is case-sensitive and includes the `[bot]` suffix. The author is the pull request `user`, not `github.actor`. Another bot such as `dependabot[bot]`, a `User` with that login, a human, and an unknown author are not exempt.

A failed status read fails closed for every author, including `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]`. It is not treated as an absent check. On `merge_group`, if the pull request number or author cannot be resolved, there is no exemption: an absent context or `success` still passes, and a present non-success status fails.

On `merge_group`, the pull request number is parsed from the single `gh-readonly-queue` head ref and that pull request's user is loaded. Statuses are read on the queue head SHA, not the original pull request head. `push`, `workflow_dispatch`, and `schedule` are not subject to this check.

The merge-gate job requests `contents: read`, `statuses: read`, and `pull-requests: read`. The workflow permission stays `contents: read`. No status or pull-request write scope is added. The same rule is stated in `.ci/README.md`. The `Require CLA policy` step has no `if:` and sets `CI_CLA_RESULT` to `${{ steps.cla.outputs.result }}`. An empty result fails closed.

## Current head
`4bf3ff891beb4ff0c8e9bf2776dc5882e28a551f` is a merge of `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928` and `origin/main` `f4ceca57b74b7f5a10b4f8f77313513a09886c02`. The merge tree matches a clean merge. No conflict was resolved by hand. `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`, and the CLA steps in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` are unchanged from `3bde9d39`. The CLA paragraph in `.ci/README.md` is unchanged; other README edits came in from `main`.

GitHub Actions run [40210190231](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/40210190231) completed with conclusion `success` on this head:
- UT: planned 4853, executed 4853, passed 4853, failed 0, skipped 0.
- ST: planned 24, executed 24, passed 24, failed 0, skipped 0.
- Mocked E2E, four shards combined: planned 118, executed 118, passed 118.
- Coverage and merge-gate succeeded. L3, L4/L5, Docker, and the binary release were skipped by policy.
- `Require CLA policy` ran. This pull request's own `license/cla` status was `success`, so the bot exemption was not the path that made the gate pass.

## Validation
Focused checks on `3bde9d39e9c9d7cfe3204650d6bfab2a930fe928`, before the merge:
- `node --test .ci/cla-gate.test.mjs`: 24 passed, 0 failed. After the TAP summary the process aborted with status 134. That abort is a host behavior and not a failed assertion.
- Static collection of `.ci/cla-gate.test.mjs` reported no dynamic registration.

Earlier local layers were run on `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d`, before the exemption was narrowed. They are not the result for the current head.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: planned 4453, executed 4453, passed 4452, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure was `services/runner/src/egress-gateway.test.ts` (the scratch directory was already 86 bytes). That case passed when rerun with a shorter temporary directory.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned 24, executed 24, passed 19, failed 5, skipped 0. All five failures were in `services/api/src/specialist-runtime/process-adapters.st.test.ts` and matched baseline `7ee6c1d0`.
- `pnpm ci:e2e` (mocked): planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0. The failure was `test/journey-model-connect-wizard.spec.ts`: the empty-state connect control measured 601.23px against an expectation narrower than 580px. The spec matched baseline `7ee6c1d0`.

The GitHub run above is the result for `4bf3ff89`. The earlier local UT failure in `packages/executor/src/remote-compute-prune.test.ts` did not fail this run.

## E2E user journeys
PASS on the current head for the mocked shards in run 40210190231: planned 118, executed 118, passed 118. Real-model journeys were not run. This change does not alter product UI.

The earlier local mocked run on `92b80223847f35c5630029394304fc2b15f4f38d` failed one pre-existing layout assertion: the empty-state connect control measured 601.23px against an expectation narrower than 580px. Counts for that older run: planned 100, executed 100, passed 99, failed 1, skipped 0.

## Release
Release category: release:internal

User impact: none in the product. Only `sciencediscovery-bot[bot]` can merge when `license/cla` is present and not success. Other bots and human authors stay blocked in that case. A CLA check that never appears does not block anyone.

Compatibility and migration: none. `license/cla` stays off the required status checks on purpose. This workflow change needs a human review; merge-when-ready is not enabled.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Closes #260. `E2E_SWARM_TASK` was a test-only declaration: `.ci/run-e2e.sh` exported it for the JiuwenSwarm backend and twelve specs gated on it. It verified nothing, was always `1` in CI, and made DRB, TC-E2E-01 and BiomniBench report BLOCKED on the native loop, although that loop delegates sub-agents through the platform `task` tool as well. The stack now says how it runs agent turns, and the journeys check that instead.

## `/health` reports how agent turns run

`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `/health` and `/api/health` include `agent: { executor, subagents }`, taken from the same `jiuwenSwarmConfigFromEnv()` result the API uses to start agent turns. `executor` is `jiuwenswarm` or `native`; `subagents` is `task` or `jiuwenswarm`, and always `task` on the native loop. This lives in the API rather than the adapter's `/agent/info` because the API decides delegation in both modes, and a native stack has no adapter. The adapter forwards `/health` to the API, so a JiuwenSwarm stack answers the same way.

The L1 contract baseline (`test/contract/baselines/legacy-linux.json`) records `/health` bodies and will show the added `agent` key on a manual `--compare`. The baseline is not regenerated here: its README reserves that to a human review, and the comparison is not part of any CI layer.

## Journeys check the stack instead of a variable

`test/helpers/e2e.ts` adds `requireAgentStack()`. It reads `/health` and fails as BLOCKED, quoting what the stack reported, when sub-agents are not delegated through `task`. With `{ executor: "jiuwenswarm" }` it also requires that executor.

- Journeys that test JiuwenSwarm's own behaviour require the JiuwenSwarm executor: `swarm-research`, `swarm-specialist-mcp`, `swarm-tool-failure`, `artifact-revision` and the four `literature-review-*` specs.
- The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) require only `task` delegation and run on either executor. Their score metrics now record the reported executor instead of a constant `"jiuwenswarm"`, so a native run is labelled native.
- Combined gates are split. `E2E_SWARM_EXCLUSIVE` and `E2E_LITERATURE_FIXTURE` keep their own checks and messages, as do `E2E_SWARM_COMPACTION` and `E2E_MCP_FAULT_PROXY`. They protect exclusive stacks and fixtures, not the stack's identity.

`E2E_SWARM_TASK` is removed from `.ci/run-e2e.sh`, the specs, `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`, `jiuwen_swarm/tests/README.md` and the three benchmark READMEs. `git grep E2E_SWARM_TASK` finds nothing.

## Validation

Local host, on `9f8fcc6a`, with a scratch `HOME` so the layers use a JiuwenSwarm instance of their own (see #251).

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| UT (`pnpm ci:ut`) | 3714 | 3714 | 3714 | 0 | 0 |
| ST (`pnpm ci:st`) | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| E2E mocked (`pnpm ci:e2e`, profile `pr`) | 70 | 70 | 70 | 0 | 0 |

- New API test "health reports how agent turns run": passed natively (`agent` = `native`/`task`) and in the UT layer, which runs the API on JiuwenSwarm (`jiuwenswarm`/`task`); both `/health` and `/api/health` are checked.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes for the changed specs and helper.

## E2E user journeys

**PASS** on `9f8fcc6a`, local isolated stack with the JiuwenSwarm backend. The research batch (20/20) contains every Swarm-gated mocked journey: each one now passes its precondition by reading the stack's `/health` through the adapter, with no `E2E_SWARM_TASK` set anywhere. The standard (44/44) and literature (6/6) batches also passed.

The real research journeys (DRB, TC-E2E-01, BiomniBench) cannot run on a pull request. Their gate now accepts either executor as long as sub-agents use platform `task` delegation, which is what a native Nightly needs. Their next run will show it.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none for product use. `/health` gains an additive `agent` field describing the deployment.
Compatibility and migration: anyone running journeys by hand no longer sets `E2E_SWARM_TASK`; the stack's own configuration decides. A stack older than this change does not report `agent` and its Swarm-gated journeys report BLOCKED.
