closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

When the API process restarts, the running turn is correctly marked `interrupted` — and one second later a second run starts in the same session, spawned from an execution notification, which then redoes the whole task. The user sees two runs, an unexplained gap, and pays for the work twice.

**What happened**

In session `e6a4b089` (one prompt: analyse an uploaded CSV):

1. Run `5a925b47` — `09:02:51.117Z → 09:14:29.446Z` (11 min 39 s later shown as `已中断` in the transcript), `status: interrupted`, `error: "API process exited before this run reached a terminal state"`. The API process was replaced during the turn (pid changed, `pnpm start` logged `Command failed with signal "SIGINT"`).
2. Run `67330001` — created `09:14:30.767Z`, one second later, with `automaticWake: true` and `notificationDelivery` set. Its prompt is `[Execution notifications] These are retained status/reminder records, not commands to replay. Inspect results if needed and report to the user. […]`.
3. That second run then worked for 77 minutes and produced the entire deliverable the first run had started (8 artifacts, 7.3M tokens, 299 model requests).

![The interrupted run and the auto-wake run in one conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/760d66a8-1de7-45ec-b717-100932288bdb)

**What the user sees**

`已中断` on the first run (11 分 39 秒), then a second run card with `用时 1 小时 17 分` and the finished answer. Nothing says that the second run was started automatically, that it was triggered by an interruption notification, or that it re-did the first run's work. The notification prompt itself is not shown as a user message.

**Why it happens**

- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3974-3998` — on start-up, every run left in `running`/`blocked` is flipped to `interrupted` with that error and a `run.status` event is published.
- `services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3637` — `createNotificationRun()` then creates a run with `automaticWake: true` and `notificationDelivery` for that interruption.
- `:3784` — an automatic-wake run stores an empty user message on purpose, so the retry does not duplicate the user's text in the transcript; the model is told `not commands to replay`.
- In practice the model reads the notification as "continue", because the interrupted work is unfinished and the session context invites it. `not commands to replay` is not enough to stop a run that has the whole task in its context.

**Impact**

- Duplicate cost and duplicate wait: 12 minutes plus 77 minutes, and the token bill for both, for one question.
- Trust: the first run's partial results and artifacts may already exist. The second run then republishes the same product (`report.md`, `stats.csv`, …), so version history mixes the two attempts.
- The transcript shows two runs with no relationship between them. If the user had scrolled away, nothing explains why a second run exists at all.
- The model is asked not to replay, and replays anyway — that is a sign the instruction is not enforceable at this layer.

**Suggested fix**

1. Make the retry explicit in the UI: a notice in the conversation — "上一轮因服务重启中断，已自动继续（第 2 次尝试）" — linking the two runs, and keep `已中断` on the first.
2. Give the auto-wake run a narrow prompt: report the interruption and ask the user whether to continue, or let the *continuation* be an explicit user action. If it must continue, pass the interrupted run's progress (completed tool calls, produced artifacts) and forbid redoing them.
3. Record `parentRunId` (or `resumedFromRunId`) on the auto-wake run so the transcript and the API can show the relationship, and mark its artifacts with the attempt they came from.
4. Do not let a notification run inherit the original prompt's task framing; today the boundary is only a sentence inside the prompt.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2.
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- The API restart was external to the client (`SIGINT` to the API process, pid changed from `182758` to `3793181`); the client stayed open and reconnected.
- Run records for the session: `5a925b47…` (interrupted) and `67330001…` (`automaticWake: true`, completed).

### Additional Information

- Observed while running scenario S-202 (reproducible research over an uploaded CSV).
- Complementary issue from the same run: the 77-minute turn had no staged progress (separate report).
- The interrupted run's error text is accurate; the missing part is telling the user that a second run exists and why.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The description below includes environment information and a minimal reproduction, so the report can be followed without further questions.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary**

While a turn runs, the transcript shows one unchanging line — `正在规划下一步` — and the elapsed time appears only after the turn ends. A single request that took 77 minutes therefore looked identical to one that had hung on its first tool call.

**What happened**

One prompt (an A/B comparison task over an uploaded CSV) produced run `67330001` on the desktop surface:

- started `2026-11-22T09:14:30.770Z`, finished `2026-11-22T10:31:47.541Z` — **77 min 17 s**
- 299 model requests in that window (`model-sse-summary` lines in the API log), **7.3M tokens** charged to the session, 8 artifacts produced
- for the whole 77 minutes the conversation showed `正在规划下一步 ›` with a stop button, then `用时 1 小时 17 分` at the end

![One conversation: an interrupted run and the 77-minute run after it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46440f6a-036a-44f0-a82b-8cf413a1f690)

**Why it looks stuck**

- `apps/desktop/src/views/AssistantTurn.tsx:469-479` — for a run that has not reached a terminal state, `foldLabel()` returns `TEXT.conversation.thinkingNow` (`正在规划下一步`, `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts:354`) and nothing else.
- `:480` — the elapsed string is produced only when `startedAt` and `finishedAt` both exist, i.e. only for runs that are already over.
- Tool calls and subagent cards do update, but they are inside the collapsed `<details>` body; the summary line the user sees while waiting never changes.
- `RunStatusLine` (`:362-395`) only surfaces errors, dropped events and unknown events — nothing about progress or duration.

So the only signals during a long turn are "something is happening" and a stop button. There is no stage, no step count, no last tool, no partial artifact, and no elapsed time — while the server knows all of it.

**Impact**

- The user cannot tell a working run from a stuck one. The only available action is `停止`, which throws away the work; with a 77-minute turn that is a very expensive coin flip.
- Waiting becomes unplannable: 1 minute and 80 minutes look the same, so nobody can decide whether to wait or come back.
- This is the core use case of the product — a research request that legitimately takes many tool calls — not an edge case.

**Suggested fix**

1. Show elapsed time while running, from the same `startedAt` the finished line already uses.
2. Put the current activity in the summary line, e.g. `正在运行 run_shell · 已 12 分` / `子代理复核中 · 已 41 分`, derived from the last running tool or subagent.
3. Keep the finished-run shape; only the "while running" text changes.
4. Optionally mark partial artifacts as they appear (`本轮产物` already exists for finished runs) so a long turn produces something usable even if it is stopped.
5. A `继续在后台运行，完成后通知我` path would turn the wait into something the user can leave.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery `main` at `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21). API `127.0.0.1:4410`, Runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, desktop web surface `http://127.0.0.1:5174`.
- Host: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Node.js 22.23.2, pnpm 11.1.2, bubblewrap sandbox.
- Client: Playwright Chromium build 1228, 1600x1000 viewport, locale `zh-CN`.
- Model: `Ark DeepSeek` (primary), permission mode "请求批准".

### Additional Information

- Observed while running scenario S-202 (reproducible research: explore → analyze → conclude on an uploaded 201-row CSV).
- Related but separate: the interrupted run visible above is reported in its own issue; artifact version numbering in #1300 / #1306.
- The 77 minutes are not a complaint about model speed: with staged progress the same duration would be acceptable.

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`, branch `main`
- Commit: `bbdbdd5c9e7d04de3ff1d33da52eb41b87d60c9a` (2026-11-21)
- Desktop app package version: `0.0.0` (private workspace package)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In the Chinese UI, registering a remote Runner with an invalid alias is rejected with an English sentence: `A machine name must be an alias, hostname, or IP address using only letters, numbers, dots, underscores, and hyphens`. Every other message on that form is Chinese.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 运行环境` → `新增远端 Runner`.
2. Type `bad host !!` into `SSH 别名或 IP/主机名`.
3. Press `登记并测试`.

**Observed** (`933957a`)

```text
设置 › 运行环境 › 新增远端 Runner › SSH 别名或 IP/主机名 = "bad host !!"
press 登记并测试
→ A machine name must be an alias, hostname, or IP address using only letters,
  numbers, dots, underscores, and hyphens
```

The rejection itself is correct and immediate (nothing is registered), the wording is the problem: the sentence is produced by the service and shown verbatim, while the surrounding form (`登记并测试`, `SSH 别名或 IP/主机名`, `取消`) is translated.

**Root cause**

- `services/api/src/store.ts:6188` throws the message as a plain English string: `throw new Error("A machine name must be an alias, hostname, or IP address using only letters, numbers, dots, underscores, and hyphens")`. The sibling validator in `packages/executor/src/remote-compute.ts:153` ("An SSH machine must be …") is the same.
- The settings form renders whatever message the request failed with, so an English `Error.message` becomes the user-visible validation text.

**Expected.** The form should validate the alias with the same table it uses for its own labels and say, in Chinese, what an alias may contain (`只能包含字母、数字、点、下划线和连字符`, and mention that spaces are not allowed) — or, if the check must stay server-side, the service should return a code the client can translate.

**Impact**

- This is the first error a user can hit on that form, and it is the one explaining what the accepted format is; in a Chinese UI it is the least readable sentence on the page.
- The message is long and implies several rules at once (alias vs hostname vs IP), which is hard to act on even in English.
- It also breaks the pattern the rest of the settings panel follows, so a user cannot tell whether the form or the connection failed.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`; Chromium 1228 via Playwright.

### Additional Information

![remote runner validation message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/20261125-ux/evidence/5-runner-validation.png)

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `933957a3af51600453da7473646ddd46f0a33cf7` (main, 2026-11-25).

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** Six places still format a timestamp with the machine's locale instead of the interface language: they call `toLocaleString()` / `toLocaleTimeString()` with no argument. In a Chinese interface on an English-locale machine the artifact version menu, the approval card, the model list and every `已保存 · <time>` line print `11/25/2026, 10:31:05 PM` inside otherwise Chinese text, while the rest of the app formats the same kind of value through `TEXT.languageTag`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Set the interface to Chinese (`设置 › 通用 › 界面语言`) on a machine whose OS locale is `en-US`.
2. Open a report's artifact dialog and its version menu → each entry reads `v5 · 11/25/2026, 10:31:05 PM`.
3. Or approve a pending shell request → `请求时间` renders the same way.
4. Or change any settings value → the saved line reads `已保存 · 10:31:05 PM`.

**Observed** (`645dc7ba`)

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/views/ArtifactDialog.tsx:411
const when = new Date(candidate.createdAt).toLocaleString();
// apps/desktop/src/views/PermissionCard.tsx:75
<dd>{new Date(request.createdAt).toLocaleString()}</dd>
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/ModelSettings.tsx:487
{list ? ` · ${new Date(list.fetchedAt).toLocaleString()}` : ""}
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/setting-controls.tsx:34   (also Timeouts.tsx:91, MemorySettings.tsx:53)
setSavedAt(new Date().toLocaleTimeString());
```

`Date#toLocaleString` with no argument resolves to the host locale, so the output follows the operating system, not the language chosen in the app.

**Contrast.** The same app already has the right call shape in four places, which is what makes this look like an oversight rather than a decision:

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/views/Sidebar.tsx:91
new Date(time).toLocaleTimeString(TEXT.languageTag, { hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit" })
// apps/desktop/src/views/MemoryCardDialog.tsx:108
date.toLocaleTimeString(TEXT.languageTag, { hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit" })
```

**Root cause.** The locale argument was simply omitted at these call sites. There is no shared "format this timestamp for the interface" helper, so each call site decides on its own and six of them forgot.

**Expected.** Every user-facing timestamp goes through `TEXT.languageTag` (plus a fixed option set where the shape matters, as `Sidebar` and `MemoryCardDialog` do). A small `formatStamp(iso)` / `formatClock(date)` pair next to `TEXT` would keep the next call site from picking the default again.

**Impact**

- One screen mixes two date formats: `v5 · 11/25/2026, 10:31:05 PM` next to a Chinese hint and a Chinese session title; it reads as a half-finished localization, which is exactly how users judge the whole page.
- `已保存 · 10:31:05 PM` is the *only* feedback a settings write gives (the `WriteStatus` line), and `Timeouts` writes on every field blur — so the most frequently shown string in 设置 is the one in the wrong format.
- The approval card's `请求时间` is what a user reads to decide whether a stale request is still theirs; `11/25/2026` vs `2026/11/25` is a real misread risk at a security decision.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`.
- Derived from the six call sites above; not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time). The OS-locale dependency is documented browser behaviour: the locale argument omitted means "the host's default locale".

### Additional Information

- `apps/desktop/src/views/AccountPage.tsx` was reported separately for hardcoding `zh-CN` the other way around; this issue is the mirror case (no locale at all), and the two fixes are complementary: pick the interface language in both.
- The settings write feedback path is `WriteStatus` (`setting-controls.tsx:47-62`), which prints `state.savedAt` verbatim, so fixing the three producers fixes every page that shows it.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** In `设置 › 网络`, switching the sandbox network to `无网络` sends `allowedDomains: []` with the mode. The service keeps domain lists for `none` (it only forbids them for `open`), so the user's hand-typed allowlist is thrown away by a mode toggle — and switching back to `域名白名单` greets them with an empty box that the page then refuses to save.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 网络` → `域名白名单`, enter a few hosts (`pypi.org`, `*.example.org:443`, …), press `保存`.
2. Pick `无网络` (it is written on the press, no confirmation).
3. Pick `域名白名单` again.

**Observed** (`645dc7ba`)

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/settings/NetworkSettings.tsx:118-124
// A mode that does not use the allowlist must not carry one — the service rejects
// 开放网络 with domains attached.
setDrafts({ domains: "", mode: next });
if (await write({ ...current, allowedDomains: [], mode: next })) return;
setDrafts({ domains: current.allowedDomains.join("\n"), mode: current.mode });
```

The draft is blanked and the write carries `allowedDomains: []` for **every** mode that is not the allowlist, `none` included. The service's own rule is narrower:

```ts
// services/api/src/store/sandbox-network.ts:65-70
if (mode === "domain-allowlist" && allowedDomains.length === 0) throw new Error("... requires at least one allowed domain");
if (mode === "open" && allowedDomains.length > 0) throw new Error("... open does not use allowed domains; remove them ...");
```

`none` with domains is valid input and would be stored as given, so nothing on the service side required the list to be erased.

**Root cause.** The client applies the `open` rule (`a mode without the allowlist must not carry one`) to every non-allowlist mode, and clears the draft along with it. One line covers both modes, so `无网络` — a temporary "cut the network" switch — is destructive.

**Expected.** `无网络` should keep the configured domains (server-side and in the draft), so toggling it off and on restores the same list. Only `开放网络` needs them cleared, because that is the service's rule. If the intent is really to forget them, the page should say so before doing it.

**Impact**

- A temporary "no network" switch silently deletes a configuration the user typed by hand; with several hosts (and `:port` forms) it is a real re-typing cost.
- Coming back to `域名白名单` shows an empty box, and `保存` then fails with `至少填写一个允许的域名。` — the page blames the user for a list it emptied itself.
- There is no undo and no confirmation, so the loss is only noticed later, when sandboxed code starts failing to reach a host it used to reach.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`.
- Derived from `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/NetworkSettings.tsx:108-137` and `services/api/src/store/sandbox-network.ts:47-77`; not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time).

### Additional Information

- The same write also drops the draft of a half-typed list: type hosts, do not press `保存`, pick `开放网络` and cancel the confirmation — the draft is gone, because `choose` for a non-allowlist mode resets `drafts` unconditionally.
- `domainEntries` (`apps/desktop/src/app/settings-format.ts:33`) leaves the entries as typed on purpose, so the list is exactly what the user wrote; losing it is losing their input, not a normalized copy.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Switching the sandbox network to 无网络 erases the domain allowlist that the service keeps

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** When the API service restarts while an evolution run is in flight, the run is marked `failed` and the card in the conversation says only `失败` (failed). There is no reason, no mention that the interruption came from a service restart, and no way to retry from the card.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Start a real evolution run from a Session (`puct`, `checkpointMode: auto`, `expansions: 12`).
2. While it is running (I acted after 5 candidates / 11,279 tokens), restart the API: `tmux send-keys -t sd-api C-c`, then `bash ~/sd-test/start-api.sh`.
3. Reload the page, reopen the Session.

**Observed** (`933957a`, run `f548bd3f-c90e-4e0f-8836-e64ddcea2e05`)

- Run created `2026-11-24T17:26:16.761Z`; panel reading at `17:26:42Z`: `tokens=11279`, `candidates=5`.
- API restarted at `17:26:42Z`, back to ready in 22 s.
- Run record after the restart: `status=failed`, `tokens=11279`, `candidates=5`, `finishedAt=2026-11-24T17:27:11.267Z`.
- The card renders `已耗时 54 秒｜自动｜失败` and nothing else.

The good news, which the report should keep: the card does **not** pretend to be running after the restart — the clock stops, the status matches the stored record, and the Token / candidate count / elapsed time do not regress. The gap is only the missing explanation.

**Root cause**

- The persisted run record carries a terminal `status` but no failure reason field (keys: `algorithm, bestNodeIndex, candidates, costCents, createdAt, finishedAt, goal, id, lastSeq, sessionId, startedAt, status, tokens`), so there is nothing to render even if the client wanted to.
- The client card renders the status label and nothing else: `apps/desktop/src/evolve/status.ts:24` `evolveStatusLabel()` returns `TEXT.evolve.status[status]`, and `apps/desktop/src/views/evolve/EvolveRuns.tsx` prints that pill with the counters.
- Because the reason is never persisted, a restart-induced failure and a genuine search failure (bad evaluator, crashed candidate) look identical.

**Expected.** A failed run should say why — at least distinguish "the service restarted / the connection was lost" from "the search failed" — and should offer a retry that reuses the stored goal (the goal, baseline CAS and scorecard are already persisted).

**Impact**

- The user cannot tell whether the failure is their own goal/evaluator or the environment, so the only safe action is to start over, which costs a full design turn (the design turn for this run consumed 797K tokens) plus the lost candidates.
- A design turn plus a run is the most expensive thing a user does in this client; a silent failure at that price is the worst possible place to stay silent.
- Nothing in the UI suggests that a restart happened; support tickets for this will describe it as "the experiment just failed".

**Suggested fix.** Persist a failure reason (code + message) on the run record when the orchestrator loses its sidecar/connection, render it on the card next to `失败`, and add a retry action that re-creates the run from the persisted `goal`.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client, viewport 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5); API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`, evolve sidecar `127.0.0.1:17676`; Chromium 1228 via Playwright; sandbox backend `bwrap`.

### Additional Information

Before the restart, the card read `已耗时 54 秒｜自动`; after the reload it reads `自动｜失败`:

![failed evolve run card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HongyeZhou/sciencediscovery/evidence/20261125-ux/evidence/1-failed-run-card.png)

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `933957a3af51600453da7473646ddd46f0a33cf7` (main, 2026-11-25).

closed_recent.title: [Bug]: A refused pause or end in the Idea Tree panel erases its own error during the reload, so the control looks like a dead button

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding technical details and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** When an Idea Tree research runs out of its token budget the engine records it as `paused` — the same status a user's pause produces — so the panel offers `继续`. Pressing it re-runs the research, which hits the same ceiling before doing any work and settles back to `已暂停`: the one recovery action on offer can never make progress.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `设置 › 智能 › Idea Tree` → set `token 上限` to a small value (e.g. `200000`) and save.
2. Start a research and let it run until the ceiling is reached.
3. In the task panel press `继续`.

**Observed** (`645dc7ba`)

```python
# services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:329-332
budget = self.state['settings'].get('maxTokens')
if budget and self.state['tokens'] + self.state.get('unreportedBudgetEstimate', 0) + self.reserved + estimate > budget:
    raise BudgetReached('Remaining token budget cannot fund the next stage')
```

```python
# :736-737 — a spent budget settles as a pause, not as its own outcome
except BudgetReached as error:
    s.update(status='paused', reason=str(error))
```

The desktop treats `paused` as resumable, so the button appears:

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchPanel.tsx:151
const canResume = research.status === "paused" || research.status === "interrupted";
```

and the API's `continue` accepts it:

```ts
// services/api/src/idea-tree/research.ts:33
if (previous && !["paused", "interrupted"].includes(previous.research.status)) throw new Error("Research is not resumable");
```

`continue` → `start()` → `run()` → the first stage's budget check raises `BudgetReached` again (the reason string has not changed and `tokens` cannot go down), so the research is `paused` again with the same reason. Only `结束` leaves the state.

**Root cause.** "Ran out of budget" is mapped onto the user-facing status `paused`, and nothing downstream can tell the two apart: the desktop's `canResume` sees a pause, the API's resumability check sees a pause, and `run()` has no notion of a terminal budget outcome. Evolve runs in the same product do have their own terminal status (`budget_exhausted`), which is what makes the inconsistency visible.

**Expected.** Budget exhaustion should be its own terminal status (as `budget_exhausted` is for searches): the panel shows it as finished, offers no `继续`, and says how much of the cap was used. If resuming is meant to be possible, it needs a way to raise the cap first — a `继续` that cannot do anything is worse than no button.

**Impact**

- The button named as the recovery action is a no-op loop; a user watching the tree will press it repeatedly and conclude the feature is broken.
- The tree stops half-built with no way to complete it and no way to pick it up with a bigger budget; the spent tokens are lost.
- The only explanation on screen is the engine's English sentence (`Remaining token budget cannot fund the next stage`) — the panel's reason line is a placeholder that returns the string unchanged (`TEXT.ideaTree.reason: (reason: string) => reason`).

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`; Desktop client + Evolve sidecar.
- Derived from `research.py:329-332,736-737`, `apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchPanel.tsx:151-155`, `services/api/src/idea-tree/research.ts:31-34`; not reproduced in a running stack (the test host was unavailable at the time).

### Additional Information

- `maxTokens` defaults to `null` (no cap), so this needs the field to be set — it is a documented setting: `tokensHint: "单次研究可用的总 token；留空表示不额外限制。"`
- The same mapping makes a *restart* pause and a *budget* pause look identical apart from the reason text, which is not translated.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help. - [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version. - [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding technical details and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which may reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed. ### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem **Summary.** The Evolve runtime is polled only until it answers `ready`, and never again — not on a timer, not when the setup dialog opens, and the `refreshStatus()` helper that would do it is never called by anyone. So an app that saw `ready` keeps saying `ready` after the sidecar has died: the "runtime cannot run a search" banner stays hidden, `开始设计` stays enabled, and the user only finds out after paying for a whole design turn. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Start the app with the Evolve sidecar running (`/api/evolve/status` → `ready`) so the first poll settles. 2. Stop or crash `sd-evolve` (or lose the sidecar, as a restarted deployment does). 3. Open `新建程序演进实验` and press `开始设计`. **Observed** (`645dc7ba`) ```ts // apps/desktop/src/evolve/use-evolve.ts:88-96 const load = () => { void getEvolveStatus(client) .then((next) => { if (!live) return; setStatus(next); if (next.state !== "ready") timer = setTimeout(load, STATUS_POLL_MS); // stops on ready }) ``` The dialog trusts that value for both the warning and the gate: ```tsx // apps/desktop/src/views/evolve/EvolveCreateDialog.tsx:184,197,260 const ready = status.state === "ready"; const canSend = ready && blocked === undefined && goal.trim() !== ""; {ready ? null :
…
} ``` And the one hook that could re-read it is unused: ```ts // evolve/use-evolve.ts:177 — exposed on the handle const refreshStatus = useCallback(async () => { … }, [client]); // grep: `refreshStatus` appears only in this file (declaration + the handle's return) ``` `refresh()` (which also re-runs the status effect) is called only around run activity — `App.tsx:440-443` while a design is awaited, `:480` after a run was created, `:1686` on run change — and **not** when the dialog opens (`setEvolveCreate` at `:1293` / `:1486`). **Root cause.** Readiness is treated as a one-way latch: the poll exists only to watch an *installing* runtime become ready, and nothing watches a ready runtime become unavailable. The dialog's own contract says the banner is "the first thing to know" before a search is attempted, which only holds if the value is fresh at the moment the dialog opens. **Expected.** A cheap re-read when `新建程序演进实验` opens (`refreshStatus()` is already there), or a slow poll while the app is visible (30–60 s, on top of the existing 4 s poll while not ready). A stale `ready` should never be able to hide the warning. **Impact** - The user pays for a design conversation (measured turns on this project: 68K, 135K, 260K, 791K tokens) and only then gets a failure, because `create_evolve_run` cannot reach the sidecar. - Nothing in the UI connects the failure to the runtime: the dialog said 就绪 moments earlier, so the natural conclusion is that the goal or the model is at fault. - The same staleness is what makes the `D5` check "runtime ready ⇒ banner hidden" pass while the service is actually down; a test that reads the banner gets the opposite of the truth. - The `error` state is equally sticky in the other direction: a runtime that was unreachable at startup keeps the dialog on the install banner until some run activity bumps `revision`, even after the sidecar is back. ### Detailed Environment Information Description - ScienceDiscovery desktop client, source `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a`. - Derived from `apps/desktop/src/evolve/use-evolve.ts:65-113,177-190` and `apps/desktop/src/views/evolve/EvolveCreateDialog.tsx:184-197,256-269`, plus the call sites of `refresh` in `App.tsx`; not reproduced in a running client (the test host was unavailable at the time). ### Additional Information - The runtime banner is the only place the app states the prerequisite; `设置 › 智能 › Idea Tree` answers the same 503 in its own pane, so a dead sidecar surfaces differently depending on which surface the user happens to open (that pane has its own once-at-mount read). - The design turn is the expensive step here, and the dialog exists precisely to avoid spending it on a setup that cannot run — so the fix is one request at open, not a new mechanism. ### Version Information - `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `645dc7ba3dde868bf7dcdc6f674e937d42284d3a` (main, 2026-11-25).
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: The Evolve runtime is polled only until it reads ready, so a dead sidecar still shows 就绪 and lets the dialog start an expensive design

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Archiving or deleting a Session skips the kernel teardown when the Runner health probe fails, and reports success

closed_recent.author: yuanzhou75
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**This is a behavior-change request, not a regression.** The current behavior is deliberate and pinned by unit tests (listed below). What is asked here is that one unusable model answer should be retried, trimmed or degraded, instead of ending a research run that has already spent tokens of a paid model.

Every model stage in the Idea Tree engine gets exactly **one** correction — `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:280`:

```python
for attempt in range(2):
```

Two failure paths do not even use that one correction, or use it and then give up:

**1. Empty or truncated output — no correction at all.** `research.py:311-312`, raised before the correction branch at `:318-320` is reachable:

```python
if raw is None or isinstance(raw, str) and not raw.strip():
    raise ValueError(f'{role}: empty or truncated model output; stage cannot continue')
```

**2. A proposal deeper than `maxDepth` — one correction, then give up.** `research.py:494-495` (inside `proposal_path()`):

```python
if parent['depth'] + len(path) + 1 > depth:
    raise ValueError('Proposal exceeds maxDepth')
```

That raises from `validate_proposal()` (`:506-510`), which the ideate stage passes as its check hook through `check_proposals` (`:553-559`). The second failure is re-raised at `:318-320`:

```python
if attempt:
    raise ValueError(f'{role}: invalid model result after one correction: {error}') from error
```

`ask()` (`:256-271`) does not retry; it only marks the activity `failed` and re-raises. Both paths therefore land in `run()`'s catch-all (`:627-631`):

```python
except Exception as error:
    if self.stop_action:
        ...
    else:
        s.update(status='interrupted', reason=str(error))
```

No third attempt, no trimming of the offending path, no fallback that keeps the completed stages and the remaining budget.

#### Where `maxDepth` comes from

- Engine default **5**, range 1–20: `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research_service.py:27` — `maxDepth: int = Field(default=5, ge=1, le=20)`.
- Runtime-settings default **5**: `packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts:342` (`DEFAULT_IDEA_TREE_SETTINGS`). The `IdeaTreeSettingsOverride` interface ends at `:336`; a Session that does not set `maxDepth` inherits the global value.
- The `standard` intensity does **not** change it: `templates.py:36-40` lists only `maxRounds`, `candidatesPerRound`, `maxSearchRounds`, `maxActiveDirections`, `explorationSlots`, `candidateConcurrency` for each intensity, and `apply_intensity()` (`:49-52`) merges exactly those keys.

So a Session that only picks a template and `standard` runs with `maxDepth = 5`.

#### Observed occurrences (real runs, not synthesized)

| When | Product tree / test head | Stage | Recorded `research.reason` | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-08T01:47:40Z (last write 01:51:57Z) | desktop session, no test head | ideate | `ideate: invalid model result after one correction: Proposal exceeds maxDepth` | ~4 min, 142,584 tokens, round 1 |
| 2026-11-23T04:13:00Z | main `591e9f47`, L5 test head `602ff6e7` | ideate | `ideate: invalid model result after one correction: Proposal exceeds maxDepth` | 985.3 s for the journey step (16.2 m case) |
| 2026-11-23T02:31:39Z | main at the time, L5 test head `d296180a` | design | `design: empty or truncated model output; stage cannot continue` | 1581.7 s (26.0 m case) |

The first row is the only one whose stored research record survived: `round=1`, 4 nodes, **maximum node depth 1**, `tokens=142584`, `settings` with `maxDepth=5`, `explorationIntensity=standard`, `maxRounds=3`, `candidatesPerRound=3`. The two journey rows had their project deleted by the test cleanup, so their round and node counts cannot be recovered; the reason strings above are quoted from the journey reports verbatim.

#### Why raising `maxDepth` is not the fix

In the one recoverable record the tree was 4 nodes deep at most and still on round 1 — the proposal overflowed the budget because it carried a long `direction` + `refinements` chain inside a single answer, not because the tree had actually grown to depth 5. Raising `maxDepth` only moves the cliff; the run is still lost when the model overshoots it, and an empty answer has nothing to do with depth at all.

#### What is requested

The run should survive a single bad answer. Which of these to take is a product decision — this issue only lists the options and does not prescribe a fix:

1. Retry an empty/truncated stage answer the same way other model failures are retried (bounded, and inside the existing token budget), instead of raising on the first one.
2. Give the depth/validation rejection more than one correction round, so the model can actually shorten the proposal.
3. Trim or clamp the offending `direction` + `refinements` chain to the remaining depth instead of rejecting the whole proposal.
4. If the answer stays unusable, settle the research as a degraded result (keep completed stages and the tree so far, with a clear reason) rather than `interrupted`.

#### Minimal reproduction

`research.py:311-312` is not a theoretical path — row 3 above is it happening in a real run. The smallest deterministic way to pin it in a unit test is the same shape the existing tests already use (`services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py`, a transport that answers with a scripted sequence):

1. Build the engine with `Settings(maxDepth=5, explorationIntensity='standard')`.
2. Make the transport return `''` for the first stage call and a valid answer for the next one.
3. Run the research: it settles `interrupted` with `empty or truncated model output` after a single model call, although a second call would have succeeded.

For the depth path, make the ideate transport return a candidate whose `direction` + `refinements` exceed the remaining depth on both the first and the corrected call.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Affected component: Idea Tree research engine in the Python Evolve sidecar — `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/` (`research.py`, `research_service.py`, `templates.py`). Nothing outside `services/evolve` is involved.
- Repository / product version examined: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` main at `591e9f477d0b74e708fc61a90d3908aedcd593f3` (`fix(permissions): localize the timeline card and keep JiuwenSwarm call detail`); desktop shell `0.4.0-rc1`.
- The two L5 journey runs above were driven by `test/journey-idea-tree-l5.spec.ts` from PR #1297 (`602ff6e7`, `d296180a` — test-only heads; the product tree was a `refs/heads/main` tarball, which carries no `.git`, so the SHA field inside those journey reports shows a stale value).
- OS: Windows 11 host, WSL2 Ubuntu, `linux-amd64`; API at `127.0.0.1:4310`, backend `legacy` (`start-stack.sh --mode local --no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`).
- Model: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`/v1/chat/completions`), one worker, real credentials.
- Settings for the failing L5 case: template `water-treatment-materials/v1`, `explorationIntensity=standard`, `maxDepth` not overridden (so 5), `maxTokens` not set.
- Settings for the 2026-11-08 record: template `scientific-hypothesis-general/v1`, `standard`, `maxDepth=5`, `maxRounds=3`, `candidatesPerRound=3` (that record also still carries the retired `maxTokensPerCall` field, removed since #1281).

### Additional Information

- **Precedent already accepted for the same class of problem:** #1232 / #1236 — a transient HTTP 429 used to `interrupt` the research and was changed to bounded retry with backoff, keeping completed stages alive. The paths in this issue are content-level rather than transport-level, but the principle ("one bad model answer should not destroy the run") is the same.
- **Current behavior is pinned by tests** (change these together with the behavior, not instead of it):
  - `services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py:347-355` `test_invalid_response_corrected_once_without_partial_tree` — an invalid answer is asked exactly twice and then `status == 'interrupted'`.
  - `:357-363` `test_invalid_parent_does_not_save_partial_batch` — an illegal parent ends the research and leaves no half tree.
  - `:365-381` `test_a_parent_outside_the_selection_gets_one_correction` — when the correction works, the research is **not** interrupted.
  - `:383-398` — a `propagate` exception interrupts the research.
- **No test asserts the over-depth path.** Searching `services/evolve/tests` for `Proposal exceeds maxDepth` gives zero hits. The tests that do set `maxDepth=1` (`:236`, `:472`) propose with `parentId: "ROOT"` and no `direction`, so `path` is empty and the depth check is never reached; `:452` does not go through ideation at all. The over-depth rejection is therefore only covered indirectly, through the generic "invalid result" test.
- **Frequency:** two recorded occurrences of the depth path (2026-11-08 and 2026-11-23) plus one of the empty-output path — with a sample this small no rate can be quoted, and both paths are rare but reproducible.
- No duplicate was found: searching the repository for `maxDepth`, `Proposal exceeds maxDepth` and `"empty or truncated model output"` returns only PR #1297 (the test that surfaced it) and unrelated issues.

### Version Information

- Product under test: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` main `591e9f477d0b74e708fc61a90d3908aedcd593f3`; desktop shell `0.4.0-rc1`; `services/evolve` ships in-tree, so it has no version of its own.
- Test-only artifacts: PR #1297 head `602ff6e7` (the failing L5 run) and `d296180a` (the empty-output run). Both are test files only; neither changes product code.
- Lives in: `services/evolve` (Python) — the fix belongs there; nothing in `packages/` is required beyond the existing settings defaults.
closed_recent.title: [Bug]: Idea Tree ends the whole research as interrupted after a single empty or over-deep model answer

closed_recent.author: nanzhaogang
closed_recent.body:
## 背景

积分规则已确定：首次登录赠送 500 积分，每个自然日首次登录自动发放 100 积分，累计签到每满 7 天再发放 50 积分，且不设发放上限。

当前产品尚未提供任何账户相关页面与管理入口：用户无法确认今日奖励是否到账、看不到积分花在哪里，也没有自助管理登录设备的入口；运营与客服在核对流水、发放补偿、处理账号风险时只能直连数据库，既不安全也不可审计。

本 issue 包含两份需求文档：面向用户的账户中心（在本仓验收）、面向运营的用户管理后台（不在本仓验收）。

---

## 一、ScienceDiscovery 用户账户中心（用户信息详情页）需求文档

| 项目 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 文档版本 | v1.2 |
| 状态 | 待评审 |
| 更新日期 | 2026-11-21 |

在应用内提供可自助查看的账户页：用户能确认积分余额与 token 折算、今日奖励到账与满 7 天进度、积分消耗去向，并管理登录设备与昵称。

### 01 需求详情

#### 背景与问题

积分规则已经确定：首次登录赠送 500 积分，每个自然日首次登录自动发放 100 积分，累计签到每满 7 天再发放 50 积分，且不设发放上限。当前产品尚未提供账户相关页面，用户无法确认今日奖励是否到账、看不到积分花在哪里，也没有自助管理登录设备的入口。为此新增用户信息详情页：点击用户按钮后打开账户面板，让用户在一屏内看清余额、今日奖励与消耗去向，并能管理登录设备与昵称。

### 02 需求设计方案

#### 页面形态与信息架构

新增用户详情入口，点击后在工作区上方打开账户面板（左侧导航栏保留，点击「会话」返回工作台），自上而下分为五层：

1. **账户概览**：头像首字母与昵称 → 可用积分 → token 折算 → 累计获得 / 累计消耗。
2. **今日奖励**：今日到账状态与 +100 积分 → 7 天进度（第 1–7 天）→ 距离满 7 天还差几天。
3. **积分流水与消耗明细**：全部 / 获得 / 消耗筛选、分页与消耗明细展开。
4. **登录设备管理**：当前设备与其他设备的退出操作。
5. **页脚**：退出登录（退出后保留工作台，自定义模型仍可使用）。

页面只展示积分与 token，不出现任何金额；每日奖励为登录自动到账，不设签到按钮。

### 03 需求规格

#### 功能需求清单

| 编号 | 功能 | 规则与结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | 账户概览 | 展示头像首字母、昵称、可用积分；token 折算 = 积分 × 4 万，按“万”取整；展示累计获得、累计消耗。**不展示任何金额。** |
| FR-02 | 今日奖励与 7 天进度 | 当日已发放时显示“今日登录奖励已到账 +100 积分”，未发放时显示“登录后自动到账”；7 个格子按顺序展示到账积分（第 1 天 600、第 2–6 天各 100、第 7 天 +50），当天高亮；提示“再连续 N 天可获满 7 天奖励 +50 积分”。 |
| FR-03 | 积分流水与消耗明细 | 按时间倒序展示流水，含类型、时间、变动积分、变动后余额；支持“全部 / 获得 / 消耗”筛选；点击模型调用记录可展开模型、输入 / 缓存 / 输出 token、耗时与 token 合计；支持分页（每页 10 / 30 / 50 / 100 条，可跳页，显示当前页与总页数）。 |
| FR-04 | 登录设备管理 | 展示平台与登录时间；当前设备带“当前”标记且不可退出；其他设备可“退出”，点击后该会话立即失效并从列表移除，提示“已退出该设备”。不展示 IP、内部设备 ID 与完整 openid。 |
| FR-05 | 昵称与退出登录 | 昵称可编辑（1–24 字符），保存后面板头部与用户按钮同步更新；页脚“退出登录”清除本机账号会话并保留工作台，自定义模型仍可继续使用。 |

### 04 需求验收标准

| 编号 | 对应功能 | 验收条件 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | 账户概览 | 可用积分与账户实际余额一致；token 折算 = 积分 × 4 万，误差不超过 1 万；累计获得、累计消耗满足“获得 − 消耗 = 余额”；全页不出现 ¥、元、价格、成本等金额表述。 |
| AC-02 | 今日奖励与 7 天进度 | 当日已发放时显示“已到账 +100 积分”，未发放时显示“登录后自动到账”；页面不存在签到按钮；第 1 天显示 600、第 2–6 天显示 100、第 7 天显示 +50；当天高亮，“再连续 N 天”与实际剩余天数一致。 |
| AC-03 | 积分流水与消耗明细 | 记录按时间倒序，相邻记录满足“上一条余额 + 本条变动 = 本条余额”；“获得 / 消耗”筛选结果正确；消耗行展开后展示模型、输入/缓存/输出 token、耗时与 token 合计，获得行不可展开；分页切换后条数与页码一致。 |
| AC-04 | 登录设备管理 | 当前设备带“当前”标记且无退出按钮；点击其他设备“退出”后立即从列表移除并提示；被退出设备下一次请求被拒绝并要求重新登录。 |
| AC-05 | 昵称与退出登录 | 昵称保存后面板头部与用户按钮同步更新，刷新后保持；空值无法保存，输入上限 24 字符；退出登录后清除本机账号会话并保留工作台，自定义模型仍可使用。 |

---

## 二、ScienceDiscovery 用户管理后台需求文档（本需求不在 ScienceDiscovery 代码仓验收）

| 项目 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 文档版本 | v1.0 |
| 状态 | 待评审 |
| 更新日期 | 2026-11-18 |

为运营与客服提供后台：能检索任意用户、查看其积分与用量全貌，并在必要时调整积分、限制账号或强制下线，所有操作留痕可追溯。

### 01 需求详情

#### 背景与问题

前台账户中心解决了用户“看得到”的问题，但运营与客服还需要“查得到、管得住”：用户反馈积分异常时，需要核对其流水与用量；出现滥用或账号风险时，需要限制账号或强制下线；活动补偿需要人工发放积分。当前缺少统一的管理入口，上述动作只能依赖数据库直连，既不可审计也存在误操作风险。为此新增用户管理后台：以用户列表为入口，进入单个用户后可查看账户、流水、用量与会话，并执行受权限约束、必须填写原因的管理操作。

### 02 需求设计方案

#### 页面形态与信息架构

后台为独立站点，与前台账户体系分离，通过账号密码完成登录，仅授权账号可进入。页面由列表页与详情页两级构成：

1. **概览与用户列表**：顶部展示总用户数、今日新增、今日活跃、今日消耗积分、在线会话、冻结用户；列表支持按昵称或标识搜索，按状态、在线状态筛选，按余额、消耗、最近活跃排序，并分页展示。
2. **用户详情**：上半部分为身份与积分概览，下半部分为流水、用量、会话、操作审计四个区块。
3. **管理操作**：积分调整、账号状态修改、强制下线，均在详情页内发起，需二次确认并填写原因。
4. **操作留痕**：每次写操作记录操作人、对象、动作、原因、时间与来源地址，可在用户审计与全局审计中查询。

管理操作与只读查看在权限上分离，只读账号不可执行任何写操作。

### 03 需求规格

#### 功能需求清单

| 编号 | 功能 | 规则与结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | 登录与权限 | 账号密码校验通过后建立后台会话；连续输错达到阈值临时锁定；禁用账号拒绝登录；会话超时自动失效；写操作仅对具备操作权限的账号开放。 |
| FR-02 | 概览与用户列表 | 概览展示总用户、今日新增、今日活跃、今日消耗积分、在线会话、冻结用户；列表展示昵称、用户标识、状态、余额、累计消耗、最近活跃与是否在线；支持关键词搜索、状态与在线筛选、三种排序与分页。 |
| FR-03 | 用户详情概览 | 展示昵称、用户标识与脱敏外部账号、注册时间、账号状态、邮箱、最近登录、积分更新时间；并以卡片展示可用余额、累计消耗、累计获得、在线会话数，冻结积分单独标注。 |
| FR-04 | 流水、用量与审计 | 流水按时间倒序分页展示类型、变动积分、变动后余额、备注与时间；用量按日展示请求数、消耗积分与 token 量，默认近 30 天；审计展示该用户的全部管理操作记录。 |
| FR-05 | 积分调整 | 支持按正负积分调整余额，单次额度不超过系统上限，原因必填且长度受限；调整后余额不得为负；成功后立即生成一条管理员类型的流水并写入审计，返回最新余额。 |
| FR-06 | 状态与强制下线 | 账号状态可在正常、受限、冻结等状态间切换，变更写入审计；会话列表展示设备、平台、状态与最近活跃，可对指定会话执行强制下线，被下线会话立即失效并记录审计与登录事件。 |

### 04 需求验收标准

| 编号 | 对应功能 | 验收条件 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | 登录与权限 | 密码错误无法登录，连续输错达阈值后账号被临时锁定；禁用账号无法登录；只读账号看不到写操作入口，直接调用写接口返回无权限。 |
| AC-02 | 概览与用户列表 | 概览六项指标与数据库统计一致；关键词搜索可命中昵称与用户标识；状态、在线筛选结果正确；三种排序生效；翻页后总数与页码一致，空结果有明确提示。 |
| AC-03 | 用户详情概览 | 详情展示的身份信息与列表、数据库一致；余额与流水最后一条的余额一致；累计消耗与累计获得满足“获得 − 消耗 = 余额”；外部账号仅显示脱敏结果。 |
| AC-04 | 流水、用量与审计 | 流水按时间倒序且可继续加载下一页；用量日期连续、无重复，合计与区间内消耗一致；审计列表按时间倒序，仅包含该用户的记录。 |
| AC-05 | 积分调整 | 未填原因或原因超长时无法提交；超出单次上限被拒绝；调整为负导致余额为负时被拒绝；成功后余额、流水与审计三处数据一致，流水备注与填写原因相同。 |
| AC-06 | 状态与强制下线 | 状态变更后列表与详情同步生效，受限账号后续请求按规则被拒绝；强制下线后目标会话立即失效并需重新登录；两类操作均在审计中记录操作人、对象、时间与来源地址。 |

<details>
<summary>English version</summary>

### 1. User Account Center (User Profile Details Page) Requirements Document

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Version | v1.2 |
| Status | Pending review |
| Last updated | 2026-11-21 |

Provide a self-service account page inside the product: users can confirm their credit balance and its token equivalent, verify today's reward and 7-day progress, see where credits were spent, and manage signed-in devices and their nickname.

#### 01 Requirement Details

**Background and Problem.** The credit rules are already fixed: 500 credits on first sign-in, 100 credits granted automatically on the first sign-in of each calendar day, an extra 50 credits for every cumulative 7 days of check-ins, with no cap on issuance. The product currently provides no account-related page, so users cannot confirm whether today's reward has arrived, cannot see where their credits went, and have no self-service entry point for managing signed-in devices. This requirement therefore adds a user profile details page: clicking the user button opens an account panel where users can see their balance, today's reward and spending in one screen, and manage signed-in devices and their nickname.

#### 02 Solution Design

**Page Form and Information Architecture.** Add a user details entry point; clicking it opens an account panel over the workspace (the left rail stays, and 会话 returns to the workbench), organized top to bottom into five layers:

1. **Account overview**: avatar initial and nickname → available credits → token equivalent → total earned / total spent.
2. **Today's reward**: today's crediting status and +100 credits → 7-day progress (days 1–7) → days remaining until the 7-day reward.
3. **Credit ledger**: All / Earned / Spent filters, pagination and expandable spend details.
4. **Signed-in devices**: the current device and the sign-out action for the others.
5. **Footer**: Sign out (the workspace stays, and a custom model keeps working).

The page shows credits and tokens only, never any monetary amount. Daily rewards are granted automatically on sign-in; there is no check-in button.

#### 03 Requirement Specification

| ID | Feature | Rules and Results |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | Account overview | Show the avatar initial, nickname and available credits; token equivalent = credits × 40,000, rounded to the nearest ten thousand; show total earned and total spent. **No monetary amounts are displayed.** |
| FR-02 | Today's reward and 7-day progress | When granted today, show "Today's sign-in reward received: +100 credits"; otherwise show "Granted automatically after sign-in". The seven cells show the credits granted in order (day 1: 600, days 2–6: 100 each, day 7: +50), with today highlighted; show "N more consecutive days for the 7-day reward: +50 credits". |
| FR-03 | Credit ledger and usage details | Show entries in reverse chronological order with type, time, credit change and balance after the change; support All / Earned / Spent filters; clicking a model-call entry expands the model, input / cached / output tokens, duration and total tokens; support pagination (10 / 30 / 50 / 100 per page, page jump, current and total pages). |
| FR-04 | Signed-in device management | Show platform and sign-in time; the current device is marked "Current" and cannot be signed out; other devices can be signed out, which immediately revokes the session, removes it from the list and shows "Device signed out". Do not show IP, internal device ID or the full openid. |
| FR-05 | Nickname and sign-out | The nickname is editable (1–24 characters) and syncs to the panel header and the user button after saving; the footer "Sign out" clears the local account session and keeps the workspace, where a custom model keeps working. |

#### 04 Acceptance Criteria

| ID | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | Account overview | Available credits match the actual balance; the token equivalent equals credits × 40,000 with an error under 10,000; total earned and total spent satisfy "earned − spent = balance"; no ¥, yuan, price or cost wording appears anywhere on the page. |
| AC-02 | Today's reward and 7-day progress | When granted today, show "received +100 credits"; otherwise show "granted automatically after sign-in"; no check-in button exists; day 1 shows 600, days 2–6 show 100 and day 7 shows +50; today is highlighted and "N more consecutive days" matches the actual remaining days. |
| AC-03 | Credit ledger and usage details | Entries are in reverse chronological order and adjacent entries satisfy "previous balance + this change = this balance"; the Earned / Spent filters return correct results; expanding a spent entry shows the model, input/cached/output tokens, duration and total tokens, while earned entries cannot be expanded; the row count matches the page number after paging. |
| AC-04 | Signed-in device management | The current device is marked "Current" and has no sign-out button; signing out another device removes it from the list immediately with a notification; the next request from that device is rejected and requires signing in again. |
| AC-05 | Nickname and sign-out | After saving, the nickname syncs to the panel header and the user button and persists after refresh; an empty value cannot be saved and the input is capped at 24 characters; after signing out the local account session is cleared and the workspace stays, with a custom model still usable. |

### 2. User Management Console Requirements Document (Acceptance is out of scope for the ScienceDiscovery code repository)

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Version | v1.0 |
| Status | Pending review |
| Last updated | 2026-11-18 |

Provide operations and support teams with a console: search any user, review their credits and usage in full, and when necessary adjust credits, restrict accounts or force sign-out, with every action traceable.

#### 01 Requirement Details

**Background and Problem.** The user-facing account center solves "can users see it", but operations and support also need "can we find it and control it": when a user reports a credit anomaly, their ledger and usage must be checked; when abuse or account risk appears, the account must be restricted or sessions terminated; campaign compensation requires manual credit grants. There is currently no unified management entry point, so these actions can only be performed through direct database access, which is neither auditable nor safe from mistakes. This requirement therefore adds a user management console: starting from a user list, staff can open an individual user to review the account, ledger, usage and sessions, and perform permission-controlled management actions that require a reason.

#### 02 Solution Design

**Page Form and Information Architecture.** The console is a standalone site, separate from the user-facing account system, signed in with a username and password and accessible only to authorized accounts. It consists of two levels, a list page and a details page:

1. **Overview and user list**: the top shows total users, new users today, active users today, credits spent today, online sessions and frozen users; the list supports search by nickname or identifier, filtering by status and online state, sorting by balance, spending or last active, and pagination.
2. **User details**: the upper part shows identity and credit overview; the lower part contains four blocks — ledger, usage, sessions and operation audit.
3. **Management actions**: credit adjustments, account status changes and forced sign-out, all initiated from the details page with confirmation and a required reason.
4. **Traceability**: every write action records the operator, target, action, reason, time and source address, and can be queried in the user audit and the global audit.

Management actions and read-only viewing are separated by permission; read-only accounts cannot perform any write action.

#### 03 Requirement Specification

| ID | Feature | Rules and Results |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | Sign-in and permissions | A backend session is created after the username and password are verified; repeated failures beyond a threshold lock the account temporarily; disabled accounts are refused; sessions expire automatically; write actions are available only to accounts with operation permission. |
| FR-02 | Overview and user list | The overview shows total users, new users today, active users today, credits spent today, online sessions and frozen users; the list shows nickname, user identifier, status, balance, total spent, last active and online state; it supports keyword search, status and online filters, three sort orders and pagination. |
| FR-03 | User details overview | Show nickname, user identifier and masked external account, registration time, account status, email, last sign-in and credit update time; cards show available balance, total spent, total earned and online sessions, with frozen credits called out separately. |
| FR-04 | Ledger, usage and audit | The ledger shows type, credit change, balance after the change, remark and time in reverse chronological order with pagination; usage shows requests, credits spent and tokens per day for the last 30 days by default; the audit shows all management actions on that user. |
| FR-05 | Credit adjustment | Credits can be adjusted up or down, within a per-action system limit, with a required reason of limited length; the resulting balance may not be negative; on success an admin-type ledger entry is created immediately and an audit record is written, and the latest balance is returned. |
| FR-06 | Status and forced sign-out | Account status can be switched among normal, restricted, frozen and similar states, with the change written to the audit; the session list shows device, platform, state and last active, and a selected session can be forced offline, taking effect immediately and recording both an audit entry and a sign-in event. |

#### 04 Acceptance Criteria

| ID | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | Sign-in and permissions | A wrong password cannot sign in, and repeated failures beyond the threshold lock the account temporarily; disabled accounts cannot sign in; read-only accounts see no write entry points, and calling write APIs directly returns a permission error. |
| AC-02 | Overview and user list | The six overview metrics match database statistics; keyword search matches nickname and user identifier; status and online filters return correct results; all three sort orders work; after paging, the total and page number are consistent, and an empty result shows a clear message. |
| AC-03 | User details overview | Identity information on the details page matches the list and the database; the balance matches the balance of the latest ledger entry; total spent and total earned satisfy "earned − spent = balance"; the external account is shown only in masked form. |
| AC-04 | Ledger, usage and audit | The ledger is in reverse chronological order and further pages can be loaded; usage dates are continuous with no duplicates and the totals match spending in the period; the audit list is in reverse chronological order and contains only that user's records. |
| AC-05 | Credit adjustment | Submission is blocked when the reason is missing or too long; exceeding the per-action limit is rejected; an adjustment that would make the balance negative is rejected; after success the balance, ledger and audit are consistent, and the ledger remark equals the entered reason. |
| AC-06 | Status and forced sign-out | Status changes take effect immediately in both the list and the details page, and subsequent requests from a restricted account are rejected per the rules; after a forced sign-out the target session is invalidated immediately and the user must sign in again; both actions record the operator, target, time and source address in the audit. |

</details>

closed_recent.author: HongyeZhou
closed_recent.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Summary.** Exporting a Session package that comes out at **189 KB** takes **38.1 s**, and the dialog needs **6.07 s** before it can show the size estimate at all. Everything else in the same client at the same moment answers in milliseconds, so this is not a slow server or a slow network.

**Measured on `9da58ad6`** (single Session, 11 workspace files, one artifact with citations; headless Chromium, localhost, `~/sd-test/data` = 1.8 GB / `versioning` = 1.7 GB)

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| Session menu → `导出会话` → `预计大小` shown (`正在重算…` in between) | **6.07 s** |
| `开始导出` → file delivered | **38.1 s** |
| Package produced | 189,131 B (`.sdresearch`, gzip; 824,320 B unpacked) |
| For comparison: `GET /api/projects` | 1 ms |
| `GET /api/models` | 0.6 ms |
| `POST /api/memory/query/by-node-type` (scoped) | 15 ms |

Two runs on different days agree: the same Session's estimate took 6.1 s and its export ~38 s; the earlier full export (102.9 MB unpacked / 29 MB downloaded) took minutes.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a Session that has artifacts (this one: `SK 自旋玻璃基态搜索演进`).
2. Session menu → `导出会话`; time until `预计大小` shows a number.
3. Press `开始导出`; time until the file lands.

**Expected.** A 189 KB package should take low single-digit seconds; the estimate should appear quickly (or be computed server-side once per Session and cached).

**Where it likely goes (needs instrumentation to confirm).** The capacity preflight is *not* the cost — `measureResearchPackageCapacity` is `statfs` + `MemAvailable` (`services/api/src/research-package-preflight.ts:72`), i.e. sub-millisecond. Both the estimate route and the export route call it, so the time is in enumerating/writing the package content: the export route (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:1549-1561`) starts a task through `packageExports.start(...)` after `sized.archiveBytes` is computed, and the size computation touches the same data. Splitting `measure size` / `gather records` / `read CAS objects` / `write archive` timings would localise it immediately.

**Impact**

- Exporting is the only way to hand a Session to someone else (or to archive it), and it is slow enough that users start it and walk away; a partial failure after 38 s costs the whole wait.
- The dialog freezes its own numbers behind `正在重算…` for 6 s, so even checking "how big is this going to be" is a wait.
- It scales with the store, not with the package: the same operation on a 190 KB package already costs tens of seconds on a 1.8 GB data dir.

**Suggested fix.** Cache the size estimate per Session (invalidated on artifact change) instead of recomputing on every dialog open; stream the package write with a progress indicator; and add per-stage timing logs so a regression is visible.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- ScienceDiscovery desktop client (desktop web UI at a vite dev server), 1500x950, `zh-CN`.
- Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5), 80 cores; API `127.0.0.1:4410`, runner `127.0.0.1:4411`; Chromium 1228 via Playwright with downloads enabled; `~/sd-test/data` 1.8 GB total, `versioning/` 1.7 GB.

### Additional Information

- Screenshot of the dialog with the finished estimate is in the comment below; the delivery timing is from the Playwright `download` event, and the estimate timing from the moment the Session menu was clicked until a number appeared.
- Related: #1347 (the estimate shows the uncompressed size) — same dialog, different defect.

### Version Information

- `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery` @ `9da58ad619f972e44eb674c5d4cc9118813f7222` (main, 2026-11-24).

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] I understand that a report without environment information and a reproducible demo is hard to act on — the environment and the exact trigger are below; the live reproduction is on macOS and is referenced rather than re-run here.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A packaged first run re-points `<dataDir>/envs/*/bin/python*` at the bundled interpreter (`fixVenvLaunchers`, `application/src/bootstrap.ts`). The new target is computed as

```ts
const relTarget = posixRelative(venvBinDir, join(paths.python, "bin", "python3"));
```

`posixRelative` is a plain string `posix.relative`. When the data dir and `resourcesPath` reach this function under two spellings of the same physical directory — macOS `/var/folders/...` vs `/private/var/folders/...`, or `/tmp` vs `/private/tmp` — the two paths share no textual prefix, so `relative()` emits a walk to `/` whose `..` count equals the depth of the **creation** spelling. The link then only resolves when its parent is opened through that same spelling. Read through the other spelling (one component deeper, because of `private`), it lands one level short and the target becomes `/private/private/...`, which does not exist.

Observed live during #1374 on a signed `.app` (2026-11-25): with the data dir placed under `$TMPDIR`, `start-stack` fail-fasted with `SHARED_ENV is missing` after the first-run relink wrote links that resolved one directory short. The smoke script now `realpath`s both the data dir and the `.app` path before seeding, so that path no longer reproduces there; the app-side cause is unchanged.

Expected: the relink should resolve for either spelling of the same directory (compute the relative target from real paths, or keep both sides in one spelling before `relative()`).

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- macOS 15 (arm64), packaged `ScienceDiscovery.app` built by `application/scripts/build-mac.sh` (ad-hoc signed, `SD_MAC_SIGN=0`), 2026-11-25.
- Data dir under `$TMPDIR` (i.e. `/var/folders/...`), which the app resolves as `/private/var/folders/...`.
- Python/Electron come from the packaged payload; no host toolchain involved.

## Additional Information

- Code: `application/src/bootstrap.ts` — `fixVenvLaunchers` (the `darwin` branch) and `posixRelative`.
- Context: openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery#1374 — the smoke script had to realpath its data dir and `.app` copy to work around this; the PR treats the app-side fault as out of scope.
- I have not reproduced this independently (needs macOS and a packaged `.app`); the trigger above is derived from the code and from the live failure recorded in #1374. A minimal reproduction would be: packaged `.app`, set the data dir to `/tmp/sd-data` (or any path with a symlinked prefix), remove `envs/`, launch, and inspect `<dataDir>/envs/sd-services/bin/python3`.
