Written-by: Dev-2
Tip SHA: 0bb3ee16884843a09d30278a63db007ba3f4da5d
Base: a429ba1d4eca17af8cfabb9f28abe9d651e38e6c (main at push; branch rebased onto it, no overlap)

`web_fetch`/`web_search` handed search-result titles and snippets to the model with named HTML references still encoded. Only `amp`, `lt`, `gt`, `quot` and `nbsp` decoded, so a page title like `Café — a review` reached the prompt and the report verbatim, and the sources a science search cites most often (encyclopedias, European sites) are exactly the entity-heavy ones. This decodes every named reference a browser resolves, in the same single pass as before.

## What changed

- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts`: the five-name map is replaced by the full WHATWG named character reference set — 2125 semicolon-terminated names — expanded into a `Map` once at module load. `nbsp` keeps its existing ordinary-space mapping; numeric references, the single-pass rule (`&lt;` → `<`) and unknown names (`&bogus;` stays literal) are unchanged. The decoding loop is the same one-scan replace it was; only the data changed shape and moved out of this module.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html-entities.ts` (new): the table itself — a `name;code point;…` constant, 246 folded lines — under a 37-line header that states the source (WHATWG named character references via CPython's `html.entities.html5`, 2231 keys of which the 2125 semicolon forms are what this pattern accepts), the retrieval date, the exact `python3` snippet that regenerates the body, and the licence position: the standard's table reproduced as factual data — names and code points any HTML parser needs — not copied from another project's source. `html.ts` keeps the decoder and goes from 79 lines to 90 (+11); 368 is only the shape this branch's previous commit had with the table inline, and this commit moves it out. The data is 246 of the new file's 284 lines.
- `tsconfig.base.json`: one line, `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`. The import in `html.ts` keeps a `.ts` extension so `node --experimental-strip-types` — the command the issue reproduces with — resolves the sibling source instead of failing with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; that option is what lets tsc accept the specifier and still emit `./html-entities.js` (verified: the built `dist/web/native/html.js` line is `import { NAMED_ENTITIES_PACKED } from "./html-entities.js";`). It belongs in the base config rather than the package one: the root tests config used by `pnpm typecheck` extends only `tsconfig.base.json`, and with the option in `packages/data-source/tsconfig.json` alone that check fails with `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.ts(73,39): error TS5097: An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when 'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled.` From the base config both the package build and that check pass. It changes nothing else in the tree — the only `test/` file that `tsc` type-checks imports `.js` paths; the Playwright specs under `test/` are not in any tsconfig.
- `html-entities.ts` is force-added: `.gitignore`'s `data-*/` rule also matches the `packages/data-source/` directory (`git check-ignore -v` reports `.gitignore:91`). I left that rule alone to keep this PR single-purpose; say the word if you would rather have it anchored as `/data-*/` and I will open a separate issue.
- `packages/data-source/src/web/native/html.test.ts`: cases for the names in the issue (`eacute`, `mdash`, `ndash`, `hellip`, `apos`, `diams`, `rsquo`, `ldquo`/`rdquo`, Latin-1, symbols), case sensitivity, an unknown name, the single-pass rule after the table widened, and a guard that the exported table still has exactly 2125 entries plus one two-scalar value (`NotEqualTilde`), so a dropped or mis-chunked line cannot pass as a smaller table. The test file is unchanged by the move.

Size, whole PR: 4 files, 344 insertions, 8 deletions (`html-entities.ts` +284, `html.test.ts` +41/−1, `html.ts` +18/−7, `tsconfig.base.json` +1).

## Red first

Decoder tests. Command:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --import tsx --test src/web/native/html.test.ts
```

Before the fix:

```
# Subtest: decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
not ok 3 - decodes the named references a browser renders in titles and snippets
  expected: "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
  actual: 'café — 5–10 … O'Brien'
# Subtest: decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
not ok 4 - decodes names case-sensitively and leaves an unknown name literal
  expected: 'Ää'
  actual: 'Ää'
# pass 5
# fail 2
```

Table guard. The guard lands in its own commit before the export exists, so it is red on the change that adds only the test:

```
# pass 0
# fail 1
SyntaxError: The requested module './html.js' does not provide an export named 'NAMED_ENTITIES'
```

and it fails the way it is meant to when one entry is dropped from the packed constant (mutation check, one `AElig;c6;` field removed, then restored):

```
not ok 8 - keeps every entry of the generated WHATWG table
  expected: 2125
  actual: 2124
# pass 7
# fail 1
```

Green after the implementation, same command as the decoder run: `# pass 8`, `# fail 0`. The package suite goes from 74 to 75 tests with the guard: `# tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0`.

## The issue's reproduction

Command from #777:

```
$ cd packages/data-source && node --experimental-strip-types -e '
  import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(m => {
    for (const s of ["café — 5–10 … O'Brien", "&lt;b&gt; stays text", "♦ … ’"])
      console.log(JSON.stringify(s), "->", JSON.stringify(m.textOf(s)));
  })'
```

On this tip:

```
"café — 5–10 … O'Brien" -> "café — 5–10 … O'Brien"
"&lt;b&gt; stays text" -> "<b> stays text"
"♦ … ’" -> "♦ … ’"
```

The middle line is the single-pass guarantee: the decoded ampersand does not start a second scan.

## Gates

On this tip, in `packages/data-source` unless noted:

```
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json                                        # exit 0 (build)
$ npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit                               # exit 0
$ node --experimental-strip-types -e 'import("./src/web/native/html.ts").then(...)'
  café — 5–10 … O'Brien                                          # exit 0
$ npm test                                                        # # tests 75 / # pass 75 / # fail 0
$ cd ../.. && node scripts/check-architecture.mjs                 # 333 source files, boundaries OK
$ cd ../.. && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json        # exit 0
$ cd ../.. && pnpm --recursive typecheck                          # 34 packages Done, exit 0
```

`pnpm architecture:check` is **98 passed / 1 failed** on this host: `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` shells out to `.ci/run-research-python.sh race`, which needs a writable uv Python install and network (`Read-only file system` at `~/.local/share/uv/python`); it does not touch `packages/data-source`. `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` itself is green, as shown above.

## Not run

- Repo-level UT/ST/E2E, CodeCheck (GitCode) and the Docker/binary layers: CI. This PR changes one package's text extractor and its test, plus one compiler option; the package tests, both tsc configurations, the architecture check and the recursive typecheck were run locally.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
A terminal user can start an evolve search or an Idea Tree research and then only see an id. Progress and stop live on the Web cards. `evolve` and `idea` call the HTTP routes those cards already use, and they read the bearer token from the same data directory as `run`.

Fixes #50

## Commands

```text
ScienceDiscovery evolve list [--session <id>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve get <run-id> [--candidate <hash>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve watch <run-id> [--after <sequence>]
ScienceDiscovery evolve stop <run-id>

ScienceDiscovery idea list --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea get <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea watch <research-id> --session <id>
ScienceDiscovery idea pause|continue|stop <research-id> --session <id>
```

`evolve stop` posts `POST /api/evolve/runs/<id>/stop`, the dashboard Stop route. `idea stop` posts `operation: "end"`, the card's End research route. Pause and continue are only on Idea Tree, because an evolve search has no pause. `evolve list` stays global; `--session` only forwards the route's existing `sessionId` filter. There is no `run --wait`. A long run is followed with `watch`.

Output matches `run`: readable text on a terminal, and one JSON object per line when stdout is a pipe, so `jq` works. `watch` adds `reconnect` lines and a final `result` line. A failure is an `error` line.

`watch` replays, then follows live, and returns when the engine stops running. A dropped connection reconnects for about three minutes. Evolve continues after the last printed event sequence, so an event is not repeated. An Idea Tree frame is a full snapshot with no sequence, so a reconnect shows the current state and skips a frame already shown. `--after <sequence>` continues an evolve watch in a new process.

Ctrl-C stops watching and exits 130. It does not stop the engine. `stop` does that. This is different from `run`, where Ctrl-C cancels the turn `run` started.

Exit status follows `run` (0 completed, 1 failed, 130 cancelled):

| Exit status | evolve | idea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `succeeded` | `completed` |
| 130 | `stopped` | `ended` or `paused` |
| 1 | `failed` or `budget_exhausted` | `interrupted` |

A paused Idea Tree research exits 130 whether a person paused it or the token budget paused it. The engine records both as `paused`. `watch` also exits 1 when the run is missing, the token is refused, or the stream cannot be recovered.

## Validation

On `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e` (parent `9c33627b5ffc3c3ef397c114e267de6e6cc6dd10`, clean worktree):

- `node --import tsx --test services/launcher/src/engine-commands.test.ts` — 26 pass, 0 fail
- `cd services/launcher && pnpm typecheck` — no errors
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` — exit 0
- `cd services/launcher && pnpm test` — 188 pass, 0 fail (includes the CLI journey below)
- `node test/api/engine-cli-journey.mjs` — `outcome` PASS, repeated 5 times on this commit
- L1: architecture boundaries OK; CI test catalog OK; `docs:check` 0 issues; e2e metadata 0 errors (11 pre-existing legacy warnings)

`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, and `pnpm ci:e2e` were not run. The single-file binary smoke was not run; `run --help` is unchanged.

## E2E user journeys

PASS on `dada3d08c9ac343492e26e87cf95141eac92b28e`. Surface: CLI against the API process. Not a browser journey.

Command: `node test/api/engine-cli-journey.mjs`

The built CLI reads the token from the data directory. The journey uses a local fake model server and the evolve sidecar venv.

| Scenario | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Recorded evolve search: list, get, candidate source, watch, `--after`, stop, missing id | Piped output is JSON. Watch of a finished success exits 0. Resume does not replay earlier events. Stop of an already finished success stays `succeeded`. A missing id exits 1. | PASS. Watch printed 6 events and exited 0. `--after 4` printed 2 events. |
| Live evolve watch, dropped connection, then CLI stop | Event sequences stay contiguous with no repeat. Stop uses the dashboard route. The run becomes `stopped` and watch exits 130. | PASS |
| Idea Tree watch, then pause | Watch follows the running research and exits 130 once it is paused. | PASS |
| Continue that research, then stop | Stop sends the card's end operation. The research ends. | PASS |
| A second research runs to completion | Watch exits 0. | PASS |

The live evolve step mounts the real evolve route handlers and orchestrator inside the API process. The public HTTP API has no route that creates a search, and API startup marks an unfinished search failed, so that step is not a separately started product process. Its sidecar is a stub. The same SSE routes forwarded through the default JiuwenSwarm adapter were not run. The CLI calls the same paths the Web cards call.

## Release

Release category: release:feature

User impact: from a terminal, evolve searches and Idea Tree researches can be listed, inspected, watched, and stopped. Idea Tree research can also be paused and continued. The commands, options, and exit statuses are in `help` and in the English and Chinese CLI reference.

Compatibility and migration: none. Existing `run` behavior is unchanged.

## Update after merging main

Head is now `fa363435e4c2a57d6439797319a7fed0a5c7bc53`, a merge of `dada3d08` with `origin/main` `f4ceca57`. The merge keeps `--effort` and `--thinking` for `run` only, and keeps `--token` on `run`, `evolve`, and `idea`. The diff against main is still the same 13 files, +1961/−43. No `run --wait` was added.

On this head, launcher tests were 198 pass / 0 fail, including this CLI journey and the thinking tests from main. Typecheck, the test-project typecheck, and the four local L1 checks passed. GitHub Actions run 40210068505 succeeded for L1, UT, ST, Coverage, the four mocked L2 E2E jobs, and merge-gate. `CodeCheck (GitCode)` failed on both `dada3d08` and `fa363435`. The public result is only a failed status plus an OpenLibing link; that page does not include the rule, file, or line, and the MR has no line comments for it. No code was changed for that check.

## CodeCheck

`eca1478253d2ca170ee7669dfcd0266a7d8aaab0` removes the one CodeCheck finding. The rule was an unnecessary non-null assertion at `services/launcher/src/cli.ts:106`: `This assertion is unnecessary since it does not change the type of the expression`, on `invocation.engineSettings!`. The call now checks that the parsed engine settings exist and passes them on, so a missing action is a usage error. List scope, watch exit status, and stop behavior are unchanged.

GitCode pipeline `379944a082974e65b5317297e3031528` reports SCA, Anti-poison, CodeCheck, and Blacklist PASSED. On this head, GitHub `CodeCheck (GitCode)`, L1, UT, ST, Coverage, the four mocked L2 E2E jobs, merge-gate, and license/cla succeeded. Real E2E, binary, and Docker were skipped by policy.

Researchers can now inspect and retrieve structured scientific data from five built-in database connectors, then download selected files through governed artifact jobs. GEO uses actual provider file listings and bounded sample metadata queries; AlphaFold DB adds retrieval of existing predictions and confidence files. The change also strengthens ChEMBL measurement filtering, ClinVar submission preservation and experimental PDB provenance.

Refs #420. **Partial fix; keep #420 open.** This is a draft because broad verification is not green and provider failure-path coverage remains incomplete.

## Scope

- GEO: discover real matrix/SOFT/supplementary files, validate download selection, preserve study/sample/platform metadata, paginate sample annotations and avoid bulk-query timeouts. Correct accession request parameters and GEO directory buckets.
- ChEMBL: validate measurement constraints and preserve units, relations, target/molecule/assay identifiers and assay confidence. Advance pagination over scanned provider rows even when local confidence filtering returns an empty page.
- ClinVar: retrieve versioned VCV/RCV records and preserve individual SCV assertions and conflicting classifications, without inventing a consensus. Reject oversized XML explicitly.
- RCSB PDB: preserve experimental-method/revision evidence and include it with structure download candidates.
- AlphaFold DB: add existing-prediction lookup by UniProt accession and governed model/confidence downloads, with explicit predicted status and model version. This does not run prediction software.
- Reuse the existing Inspector for built-in sources, using the same broker/audit path; preserve AlphaFold selections across store reloads, refresh changed connector caches, register evidence graph tools and document all five sources in English and Chinese.

## Reproduction and acceptance evidence

Baseline: `0d31e155a206c23f6d6a0c9632e44f516b326bbe` (GitHub history). Product-validation candidate: `42a96f3f2613d34487ecc6041c61b5854b692d4c`. PR head: `bcd56b74bd9b79564e392da33e4977d94dd65034`. The final commit only relocates the unchanged connector-persistence test to avoid an append-at-end conflict with current main; production code and other tests are identical to the product-validation candidate.
The requester explicitly waived baseline reproduction for this feature. The baseline capability/gap assessment was source inspection, not a baseline live-service result. The candidate journeys below used built production API/Runner entry points, the bundled stdio MCP server, isolated Session/data state and official live providers. Agent validation used the native executor and a deterministic local model stub; it does not certify JiuwenSwarm or real-model behavior.

| Acceptance area | Candidate evidence | Status / remaining limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Five sources discoverable, enabled and callable | Production sources API, saved Session selections, five live Inspector calls; browser Inspector journey | PASS for representative paths; Agent tool execution exercised with AlphaFold, not every source |
| GEO metadata/files/verified matrix | GSE1000, sample annotations and actual directory listing; completed matrix download, SHA-256 and parsed 22,283 probe rows × 10 samples | PASS; identify expression profiling by array and avoid assuming raw counts |
| ChEMBL constrained measurements/pagination | CHEMBL203 activity query, two distinct provider pages, units/relations/assay metadata/confidence retained | PASS for representative query |
| ClinVar individual assertions/conflicts | Versioned VCV000014206 live lookup with distinct SCV submissions; structured XML/conflict fixtures | PASS for selected live record and fixture contracts; not an exhaustive clinical interpretation |
| Experimental structure and downstream reading | 1CRN completed download and checksum, parsed 327 atoms in chain A | PASS |
| Existing prediction/model/confidence | P69905 model CIF and confidence download, checksums, predicted marker/version, 142 pLDDT values | PASS |
| Evidence retained after analysis | Actual files read and analysis output persisted with source IDs/URLs/retrieval metadata | PASS in native product journey |
| Invalid/missing inputs and provider/download failures | Gateway/domain boundary tests, broker/artifact tests; invalid Inspector accession rejected and next turn usable | PARTIAL: full representative rate-limit/download-failure and all-backend coverage not established |
| Setup, supported operations and scientific limits | English/Chinese guides and reproducible examples; L1 documentation check | PASS |

## Validation

Previously executed local checks at the product-validation candidate are reported below; no unexecuted check is counted as passing. At the final PR head, the relocated persistence test was rerun (1 passed), L1 was rerun (4 planned / 4 executed / 4 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped), and `git diff --check` passed. A three-way merge-tree check against upstream main `9191d552d649612a81ec5852638020bcc1f30b7e` completed without conflicts; the merge result has not been executed. The earlier broad and product journey results remain attributed to their original tested SHA.

- `pnpm -r build`: passed. Test TypeScript check passed. `git diff --check`: passed.
- Gateway Python suite: **38 passed** (includes 10 new domain tests).
- MCP sources tests: **30 passed**.
- API MCP tests, run from the API package directory: **62 passed**.
- Artifact manager tests: **2 passed**. AlphaFold selection persistence test: **1 passed**.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: planned **4**, executed **4**, passed **4**, failed **0**, skipped **0**.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: **BLOCKED before case collection** by JiuwenSwarm/adapter startup readiness; wrapper exit 2. Case counts were not emitted.
- `pnpm ci:st`: planned **2**, executed **2**, passed **1**, failed **1**, skipped **0**. Native agent-loop smoke passed. SDK contract suite failed: 33 passed / 33 failed out of 66, with test-server startup reporting `self.server.started == False`. The exact failing `TransportTests::test_concurrent_results_remain_correlated` was rerun on both the pristine baseline and candidate with the same SDK interpreter and failed identically (1 failed each). This establishes that representative startup failure on the baseline; it does not independently attribute every SDK failure.
- `pnpm ci:e2e`: planned **71**, executed **0**, passed **0**, failed cases **0**, skipped **0**; overall layer **FAILED/BLOCKED** by stack/MCP proxy startup. No browser subset pass is claimed.

## E2E user journeys

Candidate SHA: `42a96f3f2613d34487ecc6041c61b5854b692d4c`.

1. `DOMAIN_DATABASES_LIVE=1 node --import tsx test/api/domain-databases-journey.mjs`: **PASS, 11/11 steps**. Starts production API/Runner, selects all five sources, calls each official provider through the product Inspector, completes and verifies GEO/PDB/AlphaFold downloads, reads actual artifact content, persists provenance, executes an AlphaFold tool through the Agent, rejects invalid input and completes a subsequent Session turn. Provider calls are real; model responses are local deterministic fixtures. This command requires a clean committed worktree, built packages, the gateway environment and Bubblewrap.
2. Focused browser journey `Inspect domain scientific databases`: **PASS, 1 case / 3 steps**. Five built-in sources visible, built-in Inspector schema exposed, malformed accession rejected and navigation back to GEO usable. This validates UI integration; it is separate from the blocked full JiuwenSwarm browser slice.

## Remaining work and issue disposition

Keep #420 open until JiuwenSwarm product behavior, remaining representative provider/download failure paths and the full required UT/ST/E2E gates have passing evidence or independently resolved infrastructure failures. The current branch is based on the recorded baseline; these results do not certify later upstream commits or a future merge result.

## Release

Release category: release:feature
User impact: retrieve and inspect domain database data and download traceable scientific artifacts from built-in connectors.
Compatibility and migration: no manual migration; changed connector versions invalidate old cached results. Existing permission and artifact-download approval flows remain in use.

items.author: zhaozhaozz
items.body:
Session-enabled connectors stayed listed, and the agent received none of their tools, when the MCP server was switched off or could not connect. The catalog already recorded that state. The connector list ignored it.

## Disabled servers stay out of the picker and the agent

A server that is turned off, or that never entered the resolved server table, is reported as `disabled` once a catalog has been applied. `GET /api/connectors` omits those connectors, so the composer, settings, the project form, and the specialist form no longer offer them. Tool injection is unchanged: a disabled source has no available tools, so the agent is not given `mcp__<source>__*` tools even when the session still names the connector. The MCP server settings page still shows the disabled server and its switch, so it can be turned back on. Turning it back on returns the connectors to the picker with the previous selection.

## Connection failures stay visible

An enabled server that fails to connect or to list its tools stays in the connector list. Each of its connectors carries `connectionError`: the server's error text and the time the catalog was checked. The picker shows that text under the connector. The composer control shows a failure count when a selected connector failed. A partial tool mismatch (`degraded`) and a catalog that was never refreshed are left as they were: they are not hidden, and they are not labeled as connection failures.

A direct edit of `extensions_config.json` appears after the next catalog refresh (process start, `POST /api/mcp/sources/reload`, or saving a custom server). That is the same moment the agent sees the change.

## Compatibility

When an applied catalog does not contain a server, source status is `disabled` rather than `unavailable`. The governance broker rejects a call in that case with `MCP server is disabled or not configured: <id>`. Connectors of a disabled server are absent from `GET /api/connectors`.

Related to #325.

## Validation

Recorded on `4c9baed756f8b0ebbb33eaf967197e970e07af53`.

- Typecheck for the web, api, mcp, data-source, schema, and artifact-manager packages, plus `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`: passed.
- Package tests: web 890/890, data-source 51/51, mcp-sources 28/28, schema 12/12, mcp 1/1, artifact-manager 2/2.
- `services/api`: 1128 passed, 3 failed. The failures are PDF extraction tests and exit with `spawn … ENOENT` because `services/paper/.venv` is not present in this checkout. They do not call the connector list.

items.body:
This PR adds an opt-in, user-perspective JiuwenSwarm → `antibody-design` Skill → Ascend NPU journey, alongside the lower-level mocked NPU binding test. It depends on Skill backport PR #159; duplicate Skill PR #167 was closed.

## User journey

A fresh Project/Session is created with a live model and selected 131 Runner. The driver uploads the user's two PDBs and sends a high-level request through the public Session Runs API. It does not invoke any model script, choose a Python environment, or preseed model assets. The real Agent must load the Skill, inspect/select a managed environment, push inputs, perform first-use preparation and validation, run RFdiffusion → ProteinMPNN → Protenix → screening on NPU, pull results, declare report/CSV/CIF Artifacts, and explain the result. The test observes automatic wake Runs, committed execution receipts, nonempty remote and local stage files, completed transfers, and final Artifacts. It never resubmits an accepted user Run; a pipeline retry is accepted only after the preceding execution has a confirmed, committed failure. Any `unknown`/unconfirmed execution fails the test.

The real case is tagged `npu:required`, `model:real`, `status:external`, collected but deselected by ordinary PR CI until gated NPU hardware exists. The mocked binding/ST case remains for CI.

## Real-hardware verification (2026-09-24)

- **Full-Agent E2E: PASS (1/1)** on a fresh Project `9df41ef6-e2ea-4096-8e3a-6f8f5783e546`, Session `fb3dbdac-e218-40d5-a50c-565167421e4e`, initial user Run `a62cd447-a1e6-4570-8ddc-de3937edb97d`. The Agent loaded `antibody-design` itself, selected a managed environment, pushed inputs, and completed first-use preparation `74864a72-89e7-475d-af6e-ebf34495deaf` and validation with committed zero-exit receipts. One NPU pipeline Execution `a91eb590-1457-491a-977e-be73e98ba73c` finished `completed / committed / exitCode=0` on the selected remote Runner. RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, Protenix, and screening each produced files. Report, CSV, and CIF were transferred to the Session, declared as Artifacts, and explained by the Agent across the original and an automatic wake Run.
- The full live submission used the test driver at `9afed0fa`; the final `ae556055` driver passed by **read-only observation of the same Run**, after fixing a test-only assertion that had incorrectly required three `declare_artifact` tool calls even though the Agent legitimately declares multiple Artifacts in one call. No extra NPU job was submitted for that verification. The final Agent response also names the report, CSV, and CIF. The WSL product source snapshot was labelled `89a3ac7c` and included the Skill backport.
- Earlier fresh full-Agent Run `8d3814fa-f681-4957-a647-a55c81ac06e8` is **not a pass**: first-use preparation `4eb49ef9-8c60-4708-8996-9db8fec44500` became `unknown/unconfirmed` after `fetch failed`. A first pipeline attempt then had a confirmed Runner workspace-snapshot `ENOENT` on a transient MindScience `__pycache__` file; the Agent recovered and its later NPU pipeline/output delivery succeeded, but the preparation receipt remained unconfirmed. This is a real stability risk to address separately, not a result hidden by the passing rerun.
- The older prepared-environment NPU Run `c1ba1acc-2968-417f-8714-7947ee3e1b32` is lower-level evidence only, not the full-Agent E2E result.
- `node --check`, CI contract, E2E metadata (0 errors, 11 pre-existing legacy warnings), and diff whitespace checks passed locally. The previous CI run had ST, UT, Docker, both binary builds and CLA passing; the latest push starts a fresh CI run, so its final state is not yet claimed. The hardware case is intentionally deselected in CI.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`
User impact: no runtime code change; adds regression coverage for the complete Agent-to-NPU workflow.
Compatibility: merge Skill backport PR #159 before this PR.

This PR exports the existing main-agent/independent-worker Issue-to-PR workflow as opt-in contributor tooling. Scheduling decisions stay with the main agent rather than a script-driven queue controller. It does not modify ScienceDiscovery's research agent runtime, CI policy, repository settings or the operator's running pipeline.

## Scope

- Add `.agents/skills/repo-issue-pipeline` with the coordination policy, worker contract and operational guidance: claim before admission, reproduce before implementation, full accepted-scope delivery, original-thread resume, change-driven discussion/CI/conflict maintenance, independent main-agent review and explicit human/authority boundaries.
- Export a portable one-turn Codex SDK transport with an optional executable override instead of a machine-specific CLI path. Requests explicitly acknowledge full host access; per-session locks prevent concurrent hosts, saved threads resume in their original worktree, and private session/events/final/failure records survive handoff. An incomplete or failed stream cannot be reported as successful.
- Add 16 hermetic tagged tests to the existing `scripts/*.test.mjs` discovery path, without introducing a second CI definition or requiring model tokens.
- Add English/Chinese developer overviews and contributor navigation, plus a setup guide covering private ledgers, configurable repositories/concurrency/inspection interval, resource and cost limits, continuation, systemd examples, recovery and raw-log sensitivity.

## Deliberate boundaries

This is an opt-in developer tool, not a product background service or automatic installer. No real task ledger, account, credentials, logs, host-specific services or legacy migration code are included. Cloning/installing the skill starts nothing. Workers have explicitly authorized full host access, so this must not be attached to untrusted PR/webhook execution. Worktrees are not sandboxes. Raw private logs can contain tool secrets and must not become public CI artifacts.

Periodic wake-up is documented but must be configured and verified on the target host. Completion-event wake-ups and a cross-platform daemon installer are not implemented. The main agent, not the host script, enforces the task-pool cap and repository authority. Successful SDK turns and green CI do not establish full Issue acceptance. Merging/enqueueing/releases/settings/secrets/gate changes and paid real-model tests need separate matching authority.

## Validation

- `node --test --experimental-test-coverage scripts/repo-issue-pipeline.test.mjs`: **16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Host line coverage **97.64%**, branch coverage **96.00%**, function coverage **50.00%** in this direct Node report. Do not interpret these as repository-wide coverage.
- Coverage gaps: the real SDK dynamic import/constructor and CLI signal callback wiring were not exercised through a live Codex process. CLI child-process coverage is not merged into the parent report. Factory injection verifies start/resume/options/event/failure behavior, but does not prove account/CLI compatibility or model scheduling quality. No paid Codex smoke, actual OS-signal integration or service-manager installation test was run.
- Skill metadata validation, JavaScript syntax check, architecture check and CI catalog check passed.
- Markdown lint: **0 issues**. Documentation links: **141 tracked Markdown files checked**, no broken targets.
- Full local UT/ST/browser E2E are **not claimed passed**. The clean checkout has not been provisioned with all package-local dependencies/build outputs: shared UT collection stopped at missing `react` in an existing web test. Initial pnpm entry-point checks also encountered dependency-layout verification; no shared dependency tree was purged. The host's serialized heavy-test lock was occupied by an existing worker, so this PR does not interrupt that task or start competing full-stack runs. Full CI remains pending.

## E2E user journeys

ScienceDiscovery product E2E: **not applicable to the changed product path**, because there is no application UI/API/agent-runtime behavior change. Full browser-suite execution is nevertheless unverified as noted above. The new contributor tool is covered by offline request-to-session/output tests; a real Codex-account-to-fork-PR journey remains an explicit integration gap and must not be represented as a mocked product E2E pass.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: optional contributor tooling only; no automatic process or new application dependency.

Compatibility and migration: none for application users. SDK dependencies are isolated in the skill's optional host package. Existing private pipeline state is neither imported nor modified.

## Follow-up: Issue-as-Interface + OSS ops skills

Added on top of `repo-issue-pipeline` (commit `01f1df6`):

- **IAI delivery:** `issue-as-interface-contract`, `issue-review-agent-ready`, `iai-developer-patrol`, `iai-worker-implement`, `iai-reviewer-patrol`, `iai-reviewer-execute`, `magpie-pr-review-pipeline`
- **OSS ops (parallel):** `oss-ops-newcomer-gfi`, `oss-ops-stale-sweep`, `oss-ops-maintainer-stats`, `oss-ops-repo-health`
- **Docs:** [zh](docs/zh/developer-docs/issue-as-interface.md) / [en](docs/en/developer-docs/issue-as-interface.md) (+ links from CONTRIBUTING and issue-pipeline pages)

Still opt-in documentation/skills only — installing does not start bots. Reviewer execute authority is skill text for hosts that enable it; this PR does not merge or change CI policy.

Saved artifacts can disappear from a Desktop conversation when a terminal run's event history is pruned or unavailable. This increment recovers those cards and lets readers expand additional files in place.

Refs #1202.

## Increment on #1257

#1257 already delivered the card presentation, per-run grouping, subagent lineage walk, kind ordering and exact-version panel preview. This branch retains those implementations. The superseded full-width list and shared-schema selector from the old #1228 head are removed from the PR diff.

- Retain terminal SessionRun rows independently of replay, using the existing Session/epoch guards and bounded cache.
- Attach one strip to a replayed answer, a stored answer, or the run's status after its starting message when no answer survives. Do not synthesize empty turns without eligible outputs.
- Recover missing subagent lineage from the existing catalog; cache successful reads and retry failures on the next outputs refresh, including another version from the same child. Ignore stale Session/client reads.
- Keep main's five-card selection; expand remaining files, including intermediate kinds, within the same strip, with collapse and a panel action.
- Keep known queued/running/blocked outputs hidden even after the event connection closes. Preserve terminal failure/cancellation and usage presentation.

- Keep keyboard focus inside the disclosure after Enter on either toggle; both controls identify the same list with `aria-controls` and expose `aria-expanded`. The browser regression asserts focus and the list association in both directions.

No new endpoint, schema change or second grouping/rendering implementation. Design: [English](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/1a717200a99a9fe7bb530995e2eabeb31330aa15/docs/en/design/desktop-artifact-recovery.md) / [中文](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/1a717200a99a9fe7bb530995e2eabeb31330aa15/docs/zh/design/desktop-artifact-recovery.md) (files included in this PR). Current head `e2c4015c1831c2fe2bab76e432a443ba82f21deb` adds only the 12 PNG files; executable application code is identical to that tested source. The implementation remains linear on main `a8573558f8c372854079a65906171b3a543b6fb7`, with no merge commit. Old head `12dedcb94` is preserved in a local backup branch.

| Desktop conversation, artifact recovery and panel browser journeys | **18 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** |
| zh-CN / English screenshot journeys | **2 passed**, producing the 12 images below |
| Architecture boundaries / design Markdown | Passed on the integrated implementation |

The browser journeys render the actual Desktop app in the isolated WSL Vite harness (private port 14275), with page-owned API fixtures and no live LLM calls. The broader repository run used the incremental parent `afe401d47` before the active-status and keyboard-focus follow-ups; the tested source above was then revalidated with the complete Desktop suite and browser journeys above. Repository E2E was also retried on the final head.

- `pnpm test`: after building the required native Runner SEA, **37 passed / 1 failed** in the binary stage. The same command on unmodified main `a8573558` reproduces the same failure: standalone Runner SEA cannot find `@sciencediscovery/network/src/index.mjs`. The recursive package stage is not reached, so this is not a claim of a complete passing repository test run.
- `pnpm ci:ut`: **planned 8124 / executed 8124 / passed 8115 / failed 9 / skipped 0**. Failures are in CI policy, RACE, Evolve, API usage, Runner timeout/cursor and tagged-selftest cases. Main replay reproduced the RACE 120-second timeout and Unicode log-cursor 60-second timeout; other failures are not all attributed to main. The separate main replay also lacked its Evolve sidecar environment, so that result is not proof of an equivalent product failure.

Both runs recorded a roughly 600-second Evolve-distribution worker and one unreported planned case. The failure sets differ and are not claimed to be fully attributed or resolved.
- `pnpm ci:e2e`: the initial download failed with `ECONNRESET`; a subsequent run had stack-provisioning failures and the configured `.e2e/browsers` path lacked its headless executable. These failures remain visible for review/CI follow-up. No assertion, selector or gate was weakened to obtain a green result; no unrelated backend/packaging changes are included.

recent_closed_unmerged.body:
The repository already contains skills, specialists and connectors, but they are only discoverable by reading the tree, and a research session package (`.sdresearch`) has no home at all once it is produced. This adds the hub. A build-time exporter projects the tracked sources into download artifacts and an import catalogue; the database is the source of the site's browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`); nginx serves the site beside the API, so page, catalogue and downloads share one origin. Accounts, uploads, version history, review and short-lived download links live behind `/api/v1`, modelled on the openJiuwen Agentic Hub reference, and the importer carries the existing catalogue across.

Earlier this was two pull requests (#1225 and #1243); they now ship as one change, because the site switch and the importer only make sense with the service.

## The site (`apps/hub`)

Five tabs — skills, team skills, specialists, connectors and session packages — share one category tree, a searchable list and a detail view. Routes are real paths (`/skills/<id>`, `/teams/<id>`, `/sessions/<id>`), so a refresh or a shared link resolves to the same asset. Every asset exposes its README and a download. The UI is bilingual (zh/en) and follows the Agentic Hub reference: gradient hero, per-tab counts, segmented tabs, a pill search, an icon-led rail that becomes a chip strip below 900 px, and the reference's 1600 px container with a 1536 px detail card.

Downloads open the browser's save dialog where the browser has one (Chrome and Edge), so the file goes to the folder the person picks; the bytes come from a same-origin `/api/v1/artifacts/{id}/content` endpoint, which a private bucket needs no CORS rule for, and the plain navigation to the presigned URL remains the fallback. Session headers show a localized run time and the model the package recorded; obvious placeholders such as `local-*` are not shown as if they were a model.

Detail pages carry the tile, name, category, version pill and the primary download; beneath them a reading column (description, Readme and Files tabs) sits beside a "Basic information" card that shows only fields the catalog carries. Files is a two-pane browser: the left pane lists exactly what the archive holds — SKILL.md plus every resource, with its size — and the right pane renders the selected file in place, markdown for `.md`, a source listing for text files, a note instead of a preview for binaries.

## The exporter (`scripts/hub`)

`pnpm hub:export` reads only tracked sources — `skills/`, `packages/specialist/src/builtins.ts`, `packages/mcp-sources/src/*` and `extensions_config.json` — and writes `apps/hub/public/`, which is gitignored because every input is tracked. Skill and specialist archives are built in memory (`fflate`), so an export needs no network and no temporary directory. Each skill's files are also copied to `skills/<id>/<path>` (44 files, 0.42 MB) so the Files tab never unpacks a zip in the browser.

## External skills and session packages

`pnpm hub:sync-skills` freezes a snapshot of the MindScienceSkills tree (364 skills) from GitCode into `snapshot.tar.gz` and `index.json`; extraction refuses absolute paths and `..` entries.

A session drop is `<id>.sdresearch` plus an `<id>.json` sidecar, and publication is all-or-nothing: one bad package aborts before the first byte is written. Verification enforces the contract — 50 MiB cap, whole-file sha256, the manifest inventory, `records.json` hashed but never parsed. The published `sessions/index.json` is the persistent index; a run merges by id, a package leaves only through an explicit `unpublish`, and unpublishing leaves the uploaded file in place so old links keep working.

## Deployment

The site is served by nginx at `/`, which proxies `/api/` to the service, so page, catalogue and download content share one origin. `docker-compose.yml` runs MySQL, the API and nginx on one host; `pnpm hub:build:api --root` builds the site without the exporter, and the database is the source of the browse payload (`GET /api/v1/catalog`).

The static publishing workflows are gone: a production write is a deployment, not a push to `main`. The exporter remains as the importer's input, and `pnpm hub:sync-skills` remains a manual snapshot step.

## The backend (`services/hub-api`)

FastAPI + SQLAlchemy. The reference establishes the shape: an asset row carrying what the site shows, a version row carrying what a download serves, review state on the version, and `public_latest_version` deciding what is listed. This keeps that contract and differs where our data does: five asset kinds in one lifecycle (`skill`, `team`, `specialist`, `connector`, `session`) instead of six per-type models; no plugin-specific schema validation; stateless HMAC session tokens instead of Redis, so the database is the only stateful dependency; and the reference's `{code, message, data}` envelope and `/api/v1/...` paths.

Uploads are validated before anything is written: the 50 MiB cap measured on the bytes rather than `Content-Length`, path traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, encrypted and duplicate entries, an uncompressed-size ceiling, and a per-entry sha256 inventory that becomes the Files tab. Downloads resolve through `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`, which checks visibility and returns a short-lived presigned URL. Registration closes after the first account, which is the administrator; later accounts come from the administrator.

## Storage and data placement

One private bucket; keys are `assets/<kind>/<publisher>/<asset>/<version>/<filename>` composed in one function. Nothing is anonymously readable, and a bucket listing is refused. Metadata — assets, versions, manifests, users, review state, audit — lives in the database; the bytes live in the bucket; the site and its `catalog.json` remain static files served by the front end.

## Importer and site switch

`scripts/import_catalog.py` reads the exporter's `catalog.json` and writes the same data into the database and the bucket: it preserves catalogue ids, verifies each artifact against the catalogue's sha256 before uploading, wraps single-file specialists and connectors in a one-entry archive while checking the digest against the file rather than the wrapper, marks imported versions approved, and is idempotent. `--dry-run` validates without writing.

The site gets one build-time switch: with `VITE_HUB_API_BASE=/api/v1` the download button asks the API for a URL before navigating, which a private bucket requires; if that call fails the anchor still points at the catalogue URL, so a static deployment is unchanged.

## CI

`hub-api.yml` runs the service's tests and builds its image on changes under `services/hub-api`; it is informational and not part of `merge-gate`. The hub's exporter and site checks run in the UT layer, which builds the workspace: L1 stays the static slice (install only), matching the repository's layering.

## Screenshots

Taken from the built site against the local stack (Chromium, 1440 and 390 CSS px):

| Home, 1440 | Detail with the Files tab, 1440 |
|---|---|
| ![Home at 1440](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-1440.png) | ![Detail Files tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-files-1440.png) |

| Detail in Chinese, 1440 | Home at 390 |
|---|---|
| ![Chinese detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/detail-zh-1440.png) | ![Home at 390](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ink999107/sciencediscovery/feat/asset-hub/docs/hub/screenshots/home-390.png) |

## Validation

- `pnpm hub:test`: 44 passed (4 suites), including the case asserting every served skill file matches the repository byte for byte.
- `python -m pytest` in `services/hub-api`: 18 passed — registration and its closing, login, tampered tokens, administrator-created accounts, upload → pending → hidden, approval → listed and downloadable with matching sha256, rejection, owner-only uploads, the Files listing and text preview, path-shaped ids through the `%2F` encoding, the size/traversal/non-zip refusals, and the importer end to end including idempotence and a checksum mismatch.
- Importer against the real catalogue: 387 assets, 385 versions, two session packages skipped because their `.sdresearch` files were not in the site tree.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/hub typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and the hub build with and without the API switch.
- The earlier static-hub layers (UT 7718 planned / 7687 executed / 7670 passed, ST 63 planned / 62 passed, mocked E2E 188 planned / 181 passed) were measured on `de624faa`; the failures are this host's known constants and are itemised in the commit history of the branch. UI-only commits after that re-ran typecheck, build and `hub:test`.

## E2E user journeys

**Static site — PASS.** Driven in headless Chromium at 1440, 768 and 390 CSS px in English and 390 in Chinese: `document.scrollWidth` equals `clientWidth` on home and detail pages, the rail becomes a chip strip below 900 px, deep links resolve after a reload, session READMEs are fetched from the sibling prefix, and the Files browser lists and previews the archive's contents. A publication increment kept the entries it did not deliver (1 → 2 → 3 packages, every earlier URL still 200), and unpublishing removed only the named id while its file still returned 200.

**Backend — PASS on a local stack.** MySQL 8.0 (container) + the service + the built site + the real bucket, driven over HTTP and in Chromium; not yet on a deployment host.

- Import into MySQL and OBS: 387 assets, 385 versions; two sessions skipped as above.
- `http://127.0.0.1:8612/site/skills/antibody-design`: the button's static `href` is `/site/packages/antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`; the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/antibody-design?version=1.0.0` and the presigned URL serves 109171 bytes whose sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- The path-id external skill `astronomy/astronomical_analysis/astropy`: the click issues `GET /api/v1/artifacts/astronomy%2Fastronomical_analysis%2Fastropy?version=snapshot-20261117` and the download's sha256 equals the catalogue's.
- Over HTTP, not the test client: administrator login, create, upload (`201`, `pending`), approve, download; the bytes match, and the test asset and object were removed.
- The bucket is private: an unsigned `GET` of an object returns `403`, as does a bucket listing.
- The save dialog path was driven in Chromium with the picker stubbed (headless cannot show the dialog): suggested name `antibody-design-1.0.0.zip`, 109171 bytes written, equal to the catalogue's size; the session header reads `Run at Nov 17, 2026, 6:38 AM` and `Model DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, with no `local-smoke`.

Building against the real bucket surfaced three fixes now in the branch: boto3 1.36+ adds a CRC32 trailer OBS rejects (`XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch`); external skill ids are paths up to 88 characters (84 exceed 64), so columns are 191 and routes use a path converter; and the development host's clock is 28 minutes fast, which SigV4 rejects — the smoke tooling compensates, the service deliberately does not, and its README states that the deployment host must run NTP.

## Release

Release category: `release:feature` — the GitHub label is pending a maintainer, because this account has no write access to the upstream repository's labels.

User impact: a static site lists the repository's skills, specialists, connectors and session packages with READMEs and downloads; assets can also be published into a service with accounts, review and version history, served from a private bucket through short-lived links.

Compatibility and migration: none for existing behaviour. New app, new service, new scripts and three workflows. The database schema is created at startup and the importer is the migration path from `catalog.json`; the static publishing pipeline keeps working while the backend is introduced.

CSV 重复 ID 处理生成的后缀可能与输入中已有的 ID 相同，导致多条记录共用一个内部标识。点击值为 `333` 的记录时，会同时高亮两行，详情面板却显示 `111`。

## 保证 CSV 记录的内部标识唯一

- 为记录分配内部标识时，检查其是否与已分配的标识冲突；缺少原始 ID 时生成的标识也执行相同检查。
- 为每个基础标识记录下一次可尝试的后缀，避免大量重复 ID 反复扫描已占用的后缀。
- 保留原始 CSV 单元格值和解析结果的确定性，每条受影响的记录只计入一次重复 ID 警告。

复现数据：

```csv
id,value
sample#4,111
sample,222
sample,333
```

打开 CSV 可视化，切换到 **Data table（数据表）**，点击值为 **333** 的记录。修复后只高亮这一行，详情面板显示 **333**。

## 验证结果

测试提交：`82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7`，基于 `main` 的 `c33c1ae2b7100ab86de451afb02aefe0bd7a3045`。

- CSV 测试：**通过 29 / 失败 0 / 跳过 0**。其中三项 ID 冲突回归用例在修复前均失败。
- 性能回归：包含 20,000 个已占用后缀 ID 和 20,000 个重复 ID 的 40,000 行 CSV，在加入后缀游标前超过子进程的 10 秒时限；加入游标后，本地测试约 287 毫秒完成。
- UT（`pnpm ci:ut`）：计划 **3723**，执行 **3723**，通过 **3723**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- ST（`pnpm ci:st`）：计划 **2**，执行 **2**，通过 **2**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 静态检查（`pnpm ci:l1`）：计划 **4**，执行 **4**，通过 **4**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 使用模拟模型的浏览器 E2E（`pnpm ci:e2e`）：计划 **71**，执行 **71**，通过 **71**，失败 **0**，跳过 **0**。
- 加入后缀游标后，独立代码审查未发现仍需处理的问题。

此前测试失败及原因：

- 首次 UT **3721/3723** 通过：本机 bubblewrap 0.6.1 不支持 `--disable-userns`，且克隆固定版本的研究评估器时发生 TLS 连接中断。
- 另一次 UT **3720/3723** 通过。其中两项评估相关失败在未修改的 `main` 上同样出现（**3717/3719** 通过）：Python 3.14 与固定版本的 SciPy 不兼容，以及全局评估器路径覆盖使另一项契约检查暴露出依赖缺失。将固定版本的评估器准备到预期缓存位置，并使用 Python 3.12.13 后，两项问题均解决。其余一项权限队列断言属于间歇性失败：该用例在 `main`、较早的修复分支测试，以及使用全新服务状态的最终完整测试中均通过。
- 首次完整浏览器测试执行 **71** 项，**通过 70 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**；CSV 流程已通过。唯一失败是 J3 的托管 Python 环境前置条件，Conda 下载依赖时出现 `SSL routines::unexpected eof while reading`。未修改的 `main` 执行 **70** 项，**通过 69 / 失败 1 / 跳过 0**，复现了相同问题。修复分支重新测试时使用单独复制并补齐的依赖缓存。

## E2E 用户流程

提交 `82c93acb4b386c279dce800b70e89be1dfa927b7` 在浏览器和本机进程运行的产品环境中验证**通过**。完整模拟模型浏览器测试 **71/71** 通过，**失败 0 / 阻塞 0 / 跳过 0**。

CSV 流程的 **4/4** 个用户步骤全部通过：通过真实沙箱生成并声明 CSV 产物、打开可视化、点击 **333**，再依次切换 **111 → 222 → 333**。预期与实际结果一致：始终只高亮一条记录，选中数量为 1，详情值与所选记录一致，并保留原始 ID。同一操作也已在正在运行的本地产品中手动验证。

可复用用例位于 `test/journey-inspect-csv-records.spec.ts`，纳入 `pnpm ci:e2e`。该流程使用独立的本地模拟模型，覆盖无需真实模型凭据的 PR 测试场景。最终完整测试使用单独复制并补齐的科学计算依赖缓存，J3 的环境创建、使用、审计和删除流程也全部通过。

## 发布说明

发布类别：`release:fix`

用户影响：选择存在 ID 冲突的 CSV 记录时，详情面板显示该记录的数据，并且只高亮所选行。

兼容性与迁移：无需迁移。原始 CSV 值保持不变；重新打开 CSV 时，受影响的内部行标识会重新生成为唯一值。

recent_closed_unmerged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_closed_unmerged.body:
Closes #1271

## The defect

The release-version gate read `application/package.json`'s `version` from the **working tree**. On a `pull_request` event the checkout is the **merge commit** — the head merged into the current base — while the comparison point came from `pull_request.base.sha`. A branch based on an older `main` was therefore compared against a tree it never wrote.

The incident: #1264, based on `222e7b06` (0.4.1) while `main` had moved to `0c3d4d52` (0.4.0-rc1, from #1258). The branch changes only `services/api/**`, but the merge tree carried `0.4.0-rc1`, so the gate reported a release change:

```
CI policy failed: application/package.json moves 0.4.1 -> 0.4.0-rc1, which is a
release change, but the title "fix(api): tell /distill-session it has nothing to
distil" does not start with "chore(release):".
```

`Select CI policy` fails first, so L1, UT and ST are skipped and `merge-gate` fails: **nothing on that head is validated**. Rebasing the same head onto current `main` made it pass, which is what identified the trigger as the stale base rather than the change.

Impact: every pull request whose branch is behind `main` is blocked before L1 by a rule it does not violate, and the only workaround — rebase — is undiscoverable and clears approvals.

## The fix

Both sides of the comparison now come from git objects:

```js
const headVersion = versionOf(showFile(head, VERSION_FILE));
const baseVersion = versionOf(showFile(base, VERSION_FILE));
...
const files = Object.fromEntries(RELEASE_METADATA.map(path => [path, readFromHead(path)]));
```

The working tree is not consulted at all. `pull_request.head.sha` is now required alongside `base.sha`, and its absence is a named error rather than a silent pass. The success line prints the version it accepted **from the head commit**, so a stale checkout can no longer make a green gate look like it verified something else:

```
release version OK: application/package.json at 0.4.1 (head 222e7b06a418)
```

## Verification

- **The incident, on real commits:** with the working tree at current `main` (`0.4.0-rc1`) and an event whose `base` and `head` are both `222e7b06` (`0.4.1`), the check now answers `release version OK … at 0.4.1 (head 222e7b06a418)`, rc=0. Before the change the same shape produced the failure above.
- **New regression case** (`a branch behind main is not a version bump (#1271)`): base and head both 0.4.1, and it asserts that no metadata file is even read. Plus `every metadata file is read from the pull request head, and the base from the base`, and a case asserting an event without `head.sha` is refused.
- **Mutation check:** restoring the working-tree read fails three cases, including the #1271 one (`22 pass, 3 fail`); restored, 25/25. So the regression case is load-bearing, not decorative.
- `.ci/*.test.mjs` — the whole selftest including the contract test: **178/178**.
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check`: catalog OK.

## Note on the gate's placement

This changes `.ci/tier-policy.mjs` only — no workflow file, no job in the graph. The placement of the gate itself was settled on #1258 (`policy` job) and is not reopened here.

recent_closed_unmerged.title: fix(ci): read the release version from the pull request head, not the checkout

recent_closed_unmerged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_closed_unmerged.body:
Closes #1265

A provider that refuses `temperature` failed every run with the generic `semantic-error [181001]`, even though the same endpoint served another model fine. The request was always retryable — the field the provider named simply was not on the list of fields this client is willing to drop.

## Root cause

Verified on `main` `a117ae99`, not taken from the report:

- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:346` copies whatever sampling the swarm request carries into the model policy (`temperature`, `top_p`).
- `packages/model/src/client.ts:1574` (`:1594`, `:1614` for the OpenAI Responses and Anthropic variants) writes it into the provider request whenever the policy has it.
- The only 400 recovery is `rejectedControlFallback` (`packages/model/src/client.ts:938`). It gated on a hardcoded thinking-control regex — `/(thinking|reasoning|enable_thinking|chat_template_kwargs)/i` — so a detail that named only `temperature` never reached the per-field check, and `retryWithoutRejectedFields` returned `undefined`. The error was rethrown and the run ended.
- Two further reasons it would still have failed after adding the field to the list, both found while implementing:
  - `rejectedControlWording` (`:833`) is the vocabulary that proves a *parameter* was rejected. It read `unsupported|not supported|…|not allowed|not permitted|no such parameter`, and **`deprecated` was not in it** — which is exactly the word this provider used.
  - the candidate list the retreat is built from was the thinking controls only (`thinkingControlFields`, `:815`).

## What changed

- `temperature` and `top_p` join the retry candidates: `samplingControlFields` is added to a new `retryableControlFields`, which is what the pre-filter, the per-field wording check, the stripped retry, and the retry budget now use.
- `deprecated` and `no longer supported` are added to the rejection vocabulary, so "`temperature` is deprecated for this model" is recognised as a parameter rejection.
- The pre-filter no longer hardcodes thinking words: it asks whether the detail names any field this client can drop.
- The helpers that were thinking-only are renamed to say what they do now (`rejectedRetryableControlFields`, `carriedRetryableControls`, `withoutNamedFields`, `rememberRejectedControls`, …); their two consumers (`services/api/src/model-connectivity.ts`, and a doc reference in `completion.ts`) follow.
- The existing safety rule is untouched: a complaint about a control's **value** or the **state** it was sent in still strips nothing. `valueComplaintWording` keeps `when … is enabled/on/set` out of the rejection path, so "temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled" still fails the call rather than silently changing the requested mode.

## Tests

Two new cases in `packages/model/src/client.test.ts`, both with a stub server:

- **the fix**: the server answers `400 {"message":"`temperature` is deprecated for this model."}` when `temperature` is present and streams a normal turn when it is not. The first turn succeeds after the strip, `top_p` (which the 400 never named) survives, and a second turn sends no `temperature` — the rejection is remembered for the endpoint.
- **the guard**: a 400 saying "temperature is not supported when thinking is enabled" is still not a rejection — the call fails once and `temperature` is never stripped.

Mutation-checked, each revert turning the first case red and the file restored afterwards:

| Reverted | Result |
| --- | --- |
| sampling fields dropped from the retry list | `not ok — a 400 that deprecates a sampling field strips it…` |
| `deprecated` removed from the wording | same case red |
| pre-filter restored to the thinking-only regex | same case red |

## Verification

- `packages/model` `node --import tsx --test src/client.test.ts`: **49/49**, including the two new cases. Run on this Windows host with the suite's `os:linux` tag relaxed for the run only — the file declares `os:linux`, and the tag was restored before pushing, so CI is what reports the tagged run.
- `tsc -p packages/model/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: clean.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (repository root): clean.

## Deliberately not in this PR

- **The gateway keeps forwarding sampling to endpoints that never asked for it.** `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:346` could stop passing `temperature`/`top_p` for endpoints the user configured no sampling for, which would avoid the 400 entirely. That is a behaviour change for every provider — a model that currently receives the swarm's own defaults would stop receiving them — so it belongs in its own change with its own evidence. This PR fixes the failure, not the habit.
- **`services/evolve` is untouched.** `completion.py:116-121` already omits `temperature` by default for the same reason; that is a separate path and a separate fix history.
- **Where `temperature: 0.95` / `top_p: 0.95` come from is not claimed.** The swarm log states it produced those numbers, and `GET /api/models` on the reporting install carries no sampling fields, so it is a JiuwenSwarm/openJiuwen default — and that source is not in this repository. **I could not locate it**, so this description does not name one.

## Risk

The retry only happens after a `400` that names a field the request actually carried, and it stops as soon as the field is accepted. A provider that accepts `temperature` sees exactly the request it saw before.

## What changed

A stop request could be lost when the token-budget reservation raised `BudgetReached` before the next `check_stop()`: the handler always wrote the terminal `budget_exhausted`, so a research the user had ended came back resumable with a budget reason.

`IdeaTreeEngine.run()` now resolves `stop_action` before the budget outcome, exactly like the `Interrupted` handler: `end` -> `ended` / "Ended by user", `pause` -> `paused` / "Paused by user". With no stop request, `budget_exhausted` and its used/limit reason are unchanged, so a plain spent budget stays terminal and `continue` still refuses it.

## Verification

Four executable tests added in `services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py`: end + budget, pause + budget, no-stop control, and a service-level `end` while an in-flight stage raises `BudgetReached`.

- Before the fix (unmodified baseline, candidate tests only): 3 failed / 1 passed — `'budget_exhausted' != 'ended'`, `'budget_exhausted' != 'paused'`, service in-flight end `'budget_exhausted' != 'ended'`; the no-stop control passed.
- After the fix: 56 passed, 1 warning (`uv run --project services/evolve --extra test --extra candidates pytest services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py -q`).
- Full evolve suite: 417 passed / 27 failed on the candidate, 413 passed / 27 failed on unmodified `78ad0029`; failure sets byte-identical, all 27 `no sandbox backend on this host`.
- Independent service-path check: `end`+budget settles `ended` and `continue` returns 409 "Research has ended"; `pause`+budget settles `paused`; plain budget exhaustion settles `budget_exhausted` and `continue` returns 409 budget message.
- `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` cannot execute here: preflight reports `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE` (planned 8557 / 69 / 195, executed 0) — no `bwrap` binary and `unshare -Ur true` is denied. Host capability limit, so GitHub Actions is authoritative for those layers.

## Risk

The change only affects exception resolution; `pause` keeps its resumable outcome. Non-blocking pre-existing gap reported by review: an in-flight `end` is persisted only as `pausing`, so a sidecar restart during the settle still recovers as resumable `interrupted` — same symptom class, different path, outside this Issue's criteria. Docs already describe `budget_exhausted` as terminal, so no doc change.

Closes #1455

### Tests

uv run --project services/evolve --extra test --extra candidates pytest services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py -q
```

recent_merged.author: ink999107
recent_merged.body:
## What

The Quick evidence pass read an Evidence's `extracts` edge source and required it to be a `Paper` node. But `extracts` has three sources in the memory graph — `Paper` (literature search), `SourceFile` (an uploaded PDF), and `WebPage` (web search / news extraction) — so a news task whose Evidence came from a web page was reported as a broken chain:

> Evidence marker [evidence1] does not have an extracts link from a Paper node.

even though the provenance was complete. An uploaded PDF's Evidence hit the same false finding.

The tracer now takes whichever document the edge starts from and maps its metadata into the `paper` field the Deep review prompt reads: title / url / identifier / identifier type for a `WebPage`, file name and file id for a `SourceFile`, and the existing full mapping for a `Paper`. `paperLinked` is renamed `sourceLinked` so the flag says what it checks, and the finding now names all three source kinds.

A stored Quick review is reused while its Artifact version and content hash still match, and reuse serves the record's own findings — neither key moves when the tracer changes, so a report already reviewed under the Paper-only rule would keep the false finding (and the `REVISE_AND_RETRY` decision built on it) on every later checkpoint, including a Deep review that reuses the Quick record. `QUICK_REVIEWER_VERSION` is therefore bumped to `2.7.0-evidence-source-chain`, following the repository's earlier review-coverage bump, so those records are recomputed. `SEMANTIC_REVIEWER_VERSION` is unchanged: a Paper-sourced bundle is unaffected by this fix, and the Deep path picks up the fresh Quick record through `reusableQuick`.

## Validation

- `packages/provenance` unit suite: 37 pass
- `services/api` reviewer-specialist suite: 182 pass, including new cases for a WebPage source (BBC news article metadata), an uploaded PDF source, and a regression test that seeds a stored review carrying `CITATION_EVIDENCE_CHAIN_BROKEN` under the old version and asserts the next checkpoint recomputes it without that finding (the test fails if the version is left at `2.6.0-review-coverage`)
- `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build`: clean

## E2E user journeys

Not covered by a browser journey: the tracer queries the memory graph, and the desktop mocked suite answers every `/api/**` call from memory without a graph. This is a coverage gap, not an exemption — the change is covered by the API unit cases above (Paper, WebPage and SourceFile sources, plus the existing missing-node / query-failure distinctions). The visible effect is the disappearance of a false finding from the review card; the card's rendering is covered by `reviewer.spec.ts`.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer — this fork has no write access to upstream labels)
User impact: evidence extracted from a news web page or an uploaded PDF is no longer reported as a broken Paper link in the review.
Compatibility and migration: none.

recent_merged.author: yuanzhou75
recent_merged.body:
Closes #1446.

The card at the foot of the transcript is the session's own record that an Idea Tree exploration exists, and it is the way into the task panel. After an interruption it could stay at 已中断 for the rest of the session, even while the panel showed the same research as 进行中 and then 已完成.

## Why the two disagreed

The card and the panel read the research through two independent paths, and only the panel was told that 继续 changed its status:

- `useIdeaResearches` re-lists every 5 s **only while some research is live** (`running` / `pausing`). The interruption leaves the research at `interrupted`, so the list stops asking — the one mechanism that would have corrected the card is exactly the one that turns off.
- 继续 goes through the panel's own `control("continue")`, which writes the answer into the panel's local view and lets the panel's stream follow the run. Nothing reaches the list hook, and the panel had no way to tell it.
- The shell re-reads the list when the live run reports `ideaResearchesCreated`, or when the session is opened. A resume creates nothing, so neither fires.

So after 继续 the list still held the `interrupted` snapshot, that snapshot was not live, and the card had nothing left that would ever refresh it. A session switch repaired it because that path reads the list again.

## What changed

- **`apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchPanel.tsx`** — the panel reports every whole view it learns from its own write or read through a new optional `onResearchChanged` prop: the answer of `pause` / `continue` / `end`, and the view a read returns (on open, on a retry, after a refused control, on a reconnect refetch). It is held in a ref, so a caller passing an inline lambda cannot change the identity of the reads and effects.
- **`apps/desktop/src/app/use-idea-researches.ts`** — the list hook takes such a snapshot with `apply`: that one research is replaced in place, and only when the list already holds it. A research the list does not contain is dropped rather than added, because the panel's answers can arrive after the reader switched sessions: the list is that session's set of researches, and a foreign card would outlive the switch. The snapshot also carries the session it came from, so an answer that outlived a session switch cannot be written into the session now on screen. A snapshot that says `running` also makes the research live again, which is what puts it back on the 5-second poll until the engine reports a terminal status — the third point of the report. And a list read that was already in flight when the answer arrived cannot undo it: a status read before the resume loses to the snapshot taken after it, otherwise the older read would put `interrupted` back and switch the poll off again.
- **`apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaResearchPanel.tsx`** — the panel reports the answer together with the session it was asked in, **even if the reader closed the panel meanwhile** (pressing 继续 and then closing it is the shortest path to the reported bug), and keeps writing its own state only while mounted.
- **`apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`** — passes `idea.apply` to the panel, the same shape the Evolve panel already uses (`onRunChanged` → `refreshEvolve`).

The card and the panel are now two readers of one state instead of two independent snapshots: pressing 继续 moves the card to 进行中 with the answer the service returned, and the poll carries it to 已完成 when the run does.

No new user-facing text: the statuses and their labels already exist, and this only makes the card read the state the panel reads.

## Tests

- `apps/desktop/tests/idea-tree-list.test.tsx`: a resumed research replaces the stale entry in place (not a second card) and goes back on the poll — the timer is ticked with a mock clock, so the assertion is that requests resume because the status became live; a snapshot for a research the list does not hold is ignored; a snapshot that names another session is not written into this one; and a list read that started before the answer cannot put the old status back.
- `apps/desktop/tests/idea-tree-panel.test.tsx`: 继续 is one control call and reports the state the engine returned, with the session it belongs to; and pressing 继续 then closing the panel still reports the answer — the case where the component is gone but the session is not.
- `apps/desktop` on this head, Windows host: **247 tests, 122 pass, 0 fail, 125 skipped** (the skips are the `os:linux`-tagged cases); `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean.

## Scope

The Electron window is not automated in this environment, so the evidence is component-level.

## Frames

The repository's own `IdeaResearchCards` with the desktop stylesheet, driven by the real `useIdeaResearches` hook over a stub client whose list read answers `interrupted` — the state an HTTP 402 leaves behind. Nothing is re-implemented for the picture, and no language switching happens in the middle: the interface language is in place before the bundle runs.

1. The list answers `interrupted`: this is the card the report shows stuck.
2. The panel's 继续 answer is applied, **with no list read at all** — this is the `onResearchChanged` → `apply` path.
3. Nothing else is done by hand: the resumed research is live again, the 5-second poll resumes by itself, and the read it makes returns `completed`.

Nightly 45212568993 recorded `research settled as "interrupted": Model HTTP 502: {"error":"Model stream failed after response headers: read ECONNRESET"}` for research-11 and the harness scored it `FAIL` with `provider faults 0`. Idea Tree relays the local `/internal/evolve-llm` proxy's answer (`vendor/idea_tree/research.py:240-250`), and only the gateway's own vocabulary counted as provider context, so nothing matched. First defect of #1340.

## Change
- `Model HTTP <5xx>` now counts as provider context: the relayed 502/ECONNRESET text classifies as `provider-transport`, a relayed provider 5xx as `provider-server-error` with its status. `429`/`422` stay non-provider.
- The proxy's own 503 "no API token" refusal stays a product failure and vetoes a sibling outage.
- Review follow-up: the proxy also writes 5xx itself — a 502 for its request validation (`completion.ts:67-78`), its own abort/20-minute ceiling (`llm-proxy.ts:89,123,176-179`), an unreachable upstream, and the catch-all 500 `Internal server error` (`http/index.ts:5044-5051`). A relayed 5xx carrying that product wording is now vetoed, on the relayed line, so it cannot excuse a product failure; the gateway's relayed 5xx is unchanged.
- Regression cases in both classifier test files.

## Validation
`node --test ...`: 40/40 pass; with the previous classifier restored 38 pass, 2 fail (the new cases). `pnpm ci:selftest`: 185/185 (184 before). `pnpm test:tagged:selftest`: 76 tests, 69 pass, 6 fail / 1 skip — the same six pre-existing `No module named 'pytest'` failures as baseline. Not run: `ci:ut`/`ci:st`/`ci:e2e` (no `bwrap`; no product behaviour change).

## E2E user journeys
Not applicable: CI accounting code only.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: nightly accounting stops blaming the product for a provider outage and stops excusing the proxy's own 5xx.
Compatibility and migration: none

Eight edge cases can lose data during recovery, cause inconsistent research state, or change how the desktop and web apps present results. This change adds focused regression coverage for each case.

## Persistence and run history

- Repair the local graph journal tail before new records are appended. A torn final record is truncated, including invalid partial UTF-8. A valid final record without a newline is kept and terminated so the next append stays separate.
- Skip malformed run-stream JSONL records during replay. Require a non-negative safe integer sequence, a string timestamp, and an event object with a string type.

## Tool execution and context

- Propagate parallel tool rejections with `undefined` or `null` after draining in-flight calls, and stop scheduling new calls. Register both regression cases with literal titles so the tagged UT collector can discover them.
- Reject sparse arrays with an error identifying the missing index. Explicit `null` entries remain valid.

## Desktop and web

- Preserve literal comparisons in paper titles and abstracts. Remove common HTML and JATS inline and structural tags, handle escaped tags with quoted attributes, and split escaped blocks into paragraphs.
- Keep CSV artifact row keys unique even when generated IDs would collide with explicit IDs that appear later in the import.
- Keep the latest Idea Research snapshot when a list response races a stream update, so paused research stays paused and the Continue button remains available.

## Account check-ins

- Validate the daily reward and streak settings at startup and document the accepted environment variable format. Keep the existing defaults and legacy bonus-period setting.

## Validation

- On `c17479d718765c219bba22c3f279e320cfaeec85`, 70 focused checks passed in review: 19 desktop paper-text, 48 web CSV, and 3 Idea Research card tests. The new regression test delays the list response until after the stream reports `paused` and verifies that the Continue button remains available.
- GitHub Actions passed L1, UT, ST, and the [merge gate](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45585984445/job/139122562993) on this head.
- Before rebasing, the tagged Node collector on `f12d1c25` collected 7,563 test descriptors from the 756 files in the fork CI request. The two scheduler regression callbacks both passed. This was a focused check of the earlier revision.

## E2E user journeys

- The previously failing Idea Tree journey passed in an isolated local stack and in the [GitHub L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config) rerun](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45585984445/job/139112952177) for `c17479d718765c219bba22c3f279e320cfaeec85`. The journey verifies pause, manual resume, and three rounds of iteration. The [journey report and screenshots](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45585984445/artifacts/15009777596) are available in the CI artifact.
- Chromium component checks verified the desktop provenance card and CSV row selection with fixed inputs. Full-stack journeys for CSV import, desktop paper display, run replay, and account check-in remain unverified.

## UI screenshots

Captured in Chromium using the repository's actual React components and styles with fixed evidence and CSV inputs. The desktop screenshots open the evidence card's provenance tab. The CSV screenshots open the Data table tab and click the same `sample#4` record with value `10`.

### Desktop evidence card

Before the review follow-up (`63b7bd13`), the paper card displays literal JATS tags. After the follow-up, the same input displays as two readable paragraphs, preserving `<LOD`, `>0`, and the text from the inline tags.

**Before**

![Desktop paper card before the follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8929ec3a-92af-4b10-9b3c-738e0b2aa8eb)

**After**

![Desktop paper card after the follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4111d6c6-027c-4d75-aa48-56343d47e904)

### Web CSV data table

Before the PR (`c3a2305a` parser), clicking one row highlights a second row with the same internal key. After the PR, only the clicked record is highlighted.

**Before**

![Web CSV table before the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc7be5c1-aa5c-4c05-9b84-30164cca6a28)

**After**

![Web CSV table after the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3979dc9-eeaa-4f54-b293-e25a23105a31)

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`

User impact: CSV artifact rows retain distinct identities, paper text keeps literal comparisons, and saved research state and run history recover more reliably. The Idea Research card stays paused and keeps Continue available after a delayed refresh. Invalid check-in settings fail at startup with a configuration error.

Compatibility and migration: No data migration is required. Use non-negative decimal integers such as `0` or `100` for check-in settings. Unset an unused variable to use its default. Blank values, signed values, and scientific notation cause a startup configuration error.
